en.Question: Under Paragraphs 83–90 of AAOIFI GS 18, what duties apply to management when an SSB resolution requires further clarity, who serves as the process owner for the SDM implementation and reporting mechanism, and what governance requirements govern training and CPD?
en.A: Management must avoid using its own judgment and interpretation when an SSB decision requires clarity and must refer the matter back to the SSB; the SCD serves as the process owner for the SDM implementation and reporting mechanism (agreeing on the mechanism and criteria with TCWG, management, and the SSB); and management must provide sensitisation and training on effective SDM and psychological tendencies, while TCWG and the SSB must self-evaluate their understanding in this area and consider adopting a continuous professional development (CPD) mechanism.
en.B: Management may interpret ambiguous SSB Fatwas at its own commercial discretion; the external auditor is the process owner for SDM reporting; and TCWG and SSB members are exempt from self-evaluating their understanding of psychological tendencies.
en.C: The Chief Financial Officer serves as process owner for SDM reporting, and psychological tendency training applies solely to junior call-center staff.
en.D: Management must refer unclear SSB rulings to external legal counsel rather than back to the SSB, and CPD mechanisms are prohibited for SSB scholars.
en.True answer: Management must avoid using its own judgment and interpretation when an SSB decision requires clarity and must refer the matter back to the SSB; the SCD serves as the process owner for the SDM implementation and reporting mechanism (agreeing on the mechanism and criteria with TCWG, management, and the SSB); and management must provide sensitisation and training on effective SDM and psychological tendencies, while TCWG and the SSB must self-evaluate their understanding in this area and consider adopting a continuous professional development (CPD) mechanism.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 18, Par. 83–90 (Par. 86: where an SSB decision requires further clarity, management shall avoid using its own judgment and interpretation and refer the matter back to the SSB; Par. 88: SCD shall be the process owner for the SDM implementation and reporting mechanism, agreeing on mechanism and criteria with TCWG, management, and SSB; Par. 89: management ensures sensitisation and training on effective SDM and psychological tendencies, while TCWG and SSB shall self-evaluate their understanding in this area and consider adopting a CPD mechanism).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 18: Shari'ah Decision-Making Process
en.Question: Under Appendix D ('Key stages for the SDM process', pp. 68–72) of AAOIFI GS 18, what are the six sequential stages of the SDM process, and what specific control and record-keeping safeguards apply in Stage 3 (Brainstorming sessions) and Stage 5 (Records management)?
en.A: The 6 stages begin with Final Fatwa issuance and end with initial problem diagnosis; Stage 3 prohibits assigning any critic role, and Stage 5 requires deleting records after 12 months.
en.B: The six sequential stages are: (1) Problem diagnosis, (2) Data collection, (3) Brainstorming sessions, (4) Decision-making, (5) Records management, and (6) Decision review; in Stage 3 (Brainstorming sessions), one member is assigned to play the role of a critic tasked with finding faults/inconsistencies in arguments raised to mitigate groupthink risk; and in Stage 5 (Records management), SCD collates all documents/discussions (including dissenting remarks), seeks verification from stakeholders, and keeps records safely in multiple locations with multiple authorized personnel for an appropriate period (e.g., 7 years).
en.C: Stage 3 is owned solely by the external auditor, and Stage 5 stores records in a single physical folder accessible only to the marketing director for 2 years.
en.D: There are only 4 stages in Appendix D, and dissenting remarks are excluded from Stage 4 and Stage 5 records.
en.True answer: The six sequential stages are: (1) Problem diagnosis, (2) Data collection, (3) Brainstorming sessions, (4) Decision-making, (5) Records management, and (6) Decision review; in Stage 3 (Brainstorming sessions), one member is assigned to play the role of a critic tasked with finding faults/inconsistencies in arguments raised to mitigate groupthink risk; and in Stage 5 (Records management), SCD collates all documents/discussions (including dissenting remarks), seeks verification from stakeholders, and keeps records safely in multiple locations with multiple authorized personnel for an appropriate period (e.g., 7 years).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 18, Appendix D (pp. 68–72) (Sets out the 6 sequential stages: 1. Problem diagnosis, 2. Data collection, 3. Brainstorming sessions, 4. Decision-making, 5. Records management, 6. Decision review; Stage 3 activities explicitly specify: 'Assign one member to play the role of a critic tasked with the responsibility to find faults and / or inconsistencies in the arguments raised, where possible and relevant (to mitigate the groupthink risk)'; Stage 5 outputs require SCD to ensure records are verified by stakeholders and 'kept safely in multiple locations with multiple authorised personnel for an appropriate period (e.g., 7 years)').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 18: Shari'ah Decision-Making Process
en.Question:
In March 2026, an Islamic commercial bank encounters four governance situations involving its Shari'ah Supervisory Board (SSB):
(1) Senior management replaces an SSB scholar who objected to a controversial Tawarruq structure and recruits a replacement scholar who is explicitly informed that his primary mandate is to issue a favorable Fatwa for that structure; the new scholar accepts the appointment.
(2) Upon joining, the newly constituted SSB decides to overturn a prior Fatwa issued two years earlier without reviewing the previous SSB's working papers, basis of conclusion, or meeting minutes, and without consulting the former SSB members.
(3) On a separate new product Fatwa, two SSB scholars vote in favor and one scholar dissents; the SSB omits the dissenting scholar's opinion, reasons, and signature from the Fatwa document altogether.
(4) When reviewing a new Diminishing Musharakah product for approval, the SSB members refuse to review its accounting recognition and financial reporting treatment, asserting that accounting matters fall outside the SSB's competence and mandate.
According to AAOIFI GS 18, how many of these four actions violate the standard, and why?
en.A: Only 1 violates GS 18 (action 1), because a new SSB is never required to review prior Fatwa files, dissenting opinions are optional in Fatwas, and accounting review is excluded from SSB responsibilities.
en.B: Only 2 violate GS 18 (actions 1 and 2), because dissenting opinions need never be recorded in Fatwas and SSB members are absolved from reviewing accounting treatments.
en.C: All 4 violate GS 18: (1) Par. 25–26 prohibit institutions from replacing SSB scholars to obtain a predetermined Fatwa and declare accepting such an appointment a governance and ethical breach by the scholar; (2) Par. 24, Par. 80 & Appendix G (BC33–BC35) mandate reviewing earlier decisions, supporting evidence/basis of conclusion, and meeting minutes before revising a previous Fatwa, and recommend consulting predecessor SSB members; (3) Par. 72(g) & BC38 require always documenting any dissenting opinion with reasons, name, and signature as part of the minimum contents of a Fatwa (even if public disclosure upon publication depends on RSA requirements); (4) Par. 8(a)(iii), Par. 73 & Appendix G (BC27–BC31) mandate that SSB product approval includes reviewing accounting recording/reporting and confirm that SSB members cannot be absolved of ensuring Shari'ah-compliant accounting and financial reporting.
en.D: 3 violate GS 18 (actions 1, 2, and 3), while action 4 is compliant because Appendix G explicitly removed accounting review from SSB product approvals.
en.True answer: All 4 violate GS 18: (1) Par. 25–26 prohibit institutions from replacing SSB scholars to obtain a predetermined Fatwa and declare accepting such an appointment a governance and ethical breach by the scholar; (2) Par. 24, Par. 80 & Appendix G (BC33–BC35) mandate reviewing earlier decisions, supporting evidence/basis of conclusion, and meeting minutes before revising a previous Fatwa, and recommend consulting predecessor SSB members; (3) Par. 72(g) & BC38 require always documenting any dissenting opinion with reasons, name, and signature as part of the minimum contents of a Fatwa (even if public disclosure upon publication depends on RSA requirements); (4) Par. 8(a)(iii), Par. 73 & Appendix G (BC27–BC31) mandate that SSB product approval includes reviewing accounting recording/reporting and confirm that SSB members cannot be absolved of ensuring Shari'ah-compliant accounting and financial reporting.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 18 integrates four mandatory rules: (1) Par. 25–26 prohibit proactive replacement of SSB scholars for predetermined Fatwas and classify a scholar's acceptance of such an appointment as a breach of good governance and ethics; (2) Par. 24, Par. 80 & BC33–BC35 make reviewing previous Fatwa working papers, basis of conclusion, and minutes mandatory when revising a prior Fatwa, alongside consulting predecessor SSB members; (3) Par. 72(g) & BC38 mandate documenting reservations/dissenting opinions with reasons, name, and signature in every Fatwa (while public disclosure when publishing depends on RSA rules); (4) Par. 8(a)(iii), Par. 73 & BC27–BC31 explicitly reject absolving SSB members from reviewing accounting and financial reporting aspects of Islamic finance products.

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 18: Shari'ah Decision-Making Process
en.Question:
During the rollout of a new digital Murabaha financing product in 2026, examine the following four actions by the bank's management, SCD, TCWG, and SSB:
(1) Following Appendix F ('Product development process flow'), the bank structures product development across three phases—Idea generation and acceptance, Converting concepts to products, and Commercialisation—and obtains SSB approval at three distinct checkpoints: after Concept paper, after Documentation and manuals/SOPs, and after Pilot run (prior to Full-scale launch).
(2) To persuade the SSB to relax asset-possession steps in the digital Murabaha flow, senior management submits a memo stating that without relaxation the bank will suffer catastrophic financial losses—providing zero factual, statistical, or economic data—and insists the SSB must approve it because two competing banks already offer it.
(3) After the SSB issues a conditional Fatwa containing an ambiguous clause regarding late-payment charity calculation, operations managers apply their own commercial interpretation to launch the product immediately without referring the ambiguity back to the SSB.
(4) The Shari'ah Compliance Department (SCD) acts as process owner for the SDM implementation and reporting mechanism (agreed with TCWG, management, and SSB), while TCWG and the SSB conduct self-evaluations of their understanding of psychological tendencies and adopt a continuous professional development (CPD) mechanism.
According to AAOIFI GS 18, which evaluation across (1)–(4) is completely accurate?
en.A: (1) Non-compliant—Appendix F requires only one SSB approval at the end; (2) Compliant—unsubstantiated loss claims and competitor precedence justify relaxation; (3) Compliant—management may interpret ambiguous SSB clauses; (4) Non-compliant—the CFO is process owner for SDM reporting.
en.B: (1) Compliant; (2) Compliant; (3) Non-compliant; (4) Non-compliant.
en.C: (1) Non-compliant; (2) Non-compliant; (3) Compliant; (4) Compliant.
en.D: (1) Compliant—Appendix F ('Product development process flow', p. 75) depicts three phases (Idea generation and acceptance, Converting concepts to products, Commercialisation) with SSB approval checkpoints at all three stages (after Concept paper, after Documentation and manuals/SOPs, and after Pilot run before Full-scale launch); (2) Non-compliant—violates Par. 49 & 85 (prohibiting management from insisting on approval based on competitor/peer precedence) and Par. 50–51 (requiring factual, statistical, financial, and economic evidence rather than unsubstantiated loss threats); (3) Non-compliant—violates Par. 86, which mandates that where an SSB decision requires further clarity, management shall avoid using its own judgment and interpretation and shall refer the matter back to the SSB; (4) Compliant—follows Par. 88–89, designating the SCD as process owner for the SDM implementation and reporting mechanism and requiring TCWG and the SSB to self-evaluate their understanding of psychological tendencies and consider adopting a CPD mechanism.
en.True answer: (1) Compliant—Appendix F ('Product development process flow', p. 75) depicts three phases (Idea generation and acceptance, Converting concepts to products, Commercialisation) with SSB approval checkpoints at all three stages (after Concept paper, after Documentation and manuals/SOPs, and after Pilot run before Full-scale launch); (2) Non-compliant—violates Par. 49 & 85 (prohibiting management from insisting on approval based on competitor/peer precedence) and Par. 50–51 (requiring factual, statistical, financial, and economic evidence rather than unsubstantiated loss threats); (3) Non-compliant—violates Par. 86, which mandates that where an SSB decision requires further clarity, management shall avoid using its own judgment and interpretation and shall refer the matter back to the SSB; (4) Compliant—follows Par. 88–89, designating the SCD as process owner for the SDM implementation and reporting mechanism and requiring TCWG and the SSB to self-evaluate their understanding of psychological tendencies and consider adopting a CPD mechanism.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 18 integrates four provisions: (1) Appendix F (p. 75) structures product development into three phases (Idea generation and acceptance, Converting concepts to products, Commercialisation) with three SSB approval gates (after Concept paper, after Documentation/manuals/SOPs, and after Pilot run prior to Full-scale launch); (2) Par. 49 & 85 prohibit management from insisting on approval due to competitor/peer approvals, and Par. 50–51 require factual, statistical, financial, and economic data rather than unsubstantiated loss claims; (3) Par. 86 requires management to refer unclear SSB decisions back to the SSB rather than applying its own judgment/interpretation; (4) Par. 88–89 establish SCD as process owner for the SDM implementation/reporting mechanism and require TCWG and SSB self-evaluation and CPD on psychological tendencies.

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Which of the following accurately describes which prior AAOIFI Governance Standards are superseded by AAOIFI GS 19 (alongside GS 21) and the effective date of GS 19?
en.A: GS 19 supersedes GS 5 ('Independence of Shari'ah Supervisory Board') and GS 8 ('Central Shari'ah Board'), and became effective on 1 July 2021.
en.B: GS 19, together with GS 21 ('Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report'), supersedes the earlier GS 1 ('Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment, Composition and Report') and GS 2 ('Shari'ah Review'), and is effective on or after 1 January 2026.
en.C: GS 19 supersedes GS 9 ('Shari'ah Compliance Function') and GS 11 ('Internal Shari'ah Audit'), and becomes effective on 1 January 2028.
en.D: GS 19 leaves the original GS 1 in full force without superseding any standard and has no effective date.
en.True answer: GS 19, together with GS 21 ('Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report'), supersedes the earlier GS 1 ('Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment, Composition and Report') and GS 2 ('Shari'ah Review'), and is effective on or after 1 January 2026.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Preface PR5, Introduction IN3–IN4, Par. 4 & Par. 25–26 (PR5, IN4 & Par. 26: GS 19, along with GS 21 'Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report', supersedes GS 1 'Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment, Composition and Report' and GS 2 'Shari'ah Review'; Par. 4: read in conjunction with GS 1 (2024), GS 20, GS 21, and GS 5; Par. 25: effective on or after 1 January 2026).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 2–3 and 5(a) of AAOIFI GS 19, which institutions and structures fall within the scope of the standard?
en.A: All IFIs (including Islamic finance windows, standalone branches, and divisions of conventional financial institutions) across all sectors, as well as non-IFI institutions adopting AAOIFI GSs (including Waqf and other social finance institutions) insofar as practicable, and SSBs established for Sukuk and other structures as required by relevant AAOIFI GSs.
en.B: Exclusively full-fledged standalone Islamic commercial banks, excluding Islamic banking windows, Takaful operators, Waqf institutions, and Sukuk SSBs.
en.C: Only national Central Shari'ah Boards (CSBs) established by central banks, while institution-level SSBs are excluded.
en.D: Only private corporate issuers of equity shares, excluding licensed banking and capital market institutions.
en.True answer: All IFIs (including Islamic finance windows, standalone branches, and divisions of conventional financial institutions) across all sectors, as well as non-IFI institutions adopting AAOIFI GSs (including Waqf and other social finance institutions) insofar as practicable, and SSBs established for Sukuk and other structures as required by relevant AAOIFI GSs.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 2–3 & Par. 5(a) (Par. 2 & 5(a): applies to all IFIs, including stand-alone branches, divisions, and Islamic finance windows of conventional financial institutions, across all sectors; Par. 3: also applies to other institutions adopting AAOIFI GSs, including Waqf and other social finance institutions, and to SSBs established for Sukuk and other structures as required by relevant AAOIFI GSs [such as GS 12]).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Under the Explanation to Paragraph 5(b) of AAOIFI GS 19, if an ambiguity is identified during a compliance, audit, or rating exercise regarding the interpretation of tiers (i) to (iv) of the hierarchy of Shari'ah principles and rules (AAOIFI Shari'ah Standards, regulatory Shari'ah requirements, CSB rulings, or AAOIFI FAS Shari'ah-related requirements), whose clarification prevails?
en.A: The external financial auditor's interpretation.
en.B: The rating agency's lead analyst's interpretation.
en.C: The clarification of the institution's Shari'ah Supervisory Board (SSB).
en.D: The Chief Executive Officer's commercial interpretation.
en.True answer: The clarification of the institution's Shari'ah Supervisory Board (SSB).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 5(b) Explanation ('In case of an ambiguity, identified during a compliance, audit or rating exercise, as the case may be, with regard to interpretations related to (i) to (iv) above, the Shari'ah supervisory board's clarification shall prevail').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 8–10 and Appendix B (BC1–BC5) of AAOIFI GS 19, what is the governance status, voting right, and appointing mechanism for 'SSB advisors'?
en.A: SSB advisors are mandatory voting members of the SSB who hold equal voting rights with Shari'ah scholars on Fatwas and may chair the SSB.
en.B: SSB advisors are appointed directly by the SSB itself on an informal ad-hoc basis and are exempt from GS 19 provisions.
en.C: SSB advisors are strictly prohibited under GS 19 so that only Fiqh scholars participate in SSB deliberations.
en.D: SSB advisors (experts in fields such as finance, accounting, economics, or law) may preferably—though not mandatorily—be appointed without any voting rights; they are subject to all relevant GS 19 provisions applicable to SSB members (insofar as suitable) in addition to advisor-specific criteria, and the Board declined assigning their appointment authority to the SSB itself in order to maintain their independence and stature.
en.True answer: SSB advisors (experts in fields such as finance, accounting, economics, or law) may preferably—though not mandatorily—be appointed without any voting rights; they are subject to all relevant GS 19 provisions applicable to SSB members (insofar as suitable) in addition to advisor-specific criteria, and the Board declined assigning their appointment authority to the SSB itself in order to maintain their independence and stature.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 8–10 & Appendix B, BC1–BC5 (Par. 8–10: experts in related fields may preferably be appointed as SSB advisors and are subject to all relevant GS 19 provisions applicable to SSB members insofar as suitable, plus advisor-specific fit and proper criteria in Par. 19; BC4–BC5: Board chose a middle ground stipulating that SSB advisors may preferably—not mandatorily—be appointed without having any voting rights, and declined assigning their appointment authority to the SSB itself to maintain their independence and stature).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 12–14 and Appendix B (BC6–BC8) of AAOIFI GS 19, to whom does the SSB refer for administrative matters, how does this affect its functional independence, and how is SSB remuneration determined?
en.A: The SSB refers to Those Charged with Governance (TCWG) for any administrative matters while remaining completely independent in its function as SSB; SSB members are approved by shareholders in their general meeting upon TCWG's recommendation, and shareholders may periodically authorize TCWG to fix SSB members' remuneration.
en.B: The SSB reports administratively and functionally to the Chief Executive Officer (CEO), who unilaterally sets SSB fees every quarter.
en.C: The SSB reports administratively to the external financial auditor, and SSB remuneration is fixed exclusively by the national central bank.
en.D: Because the SSB refers to TCWG for administrative matters, TCWG holds authority to override or amend SSB Fatwas on commercial grounds.
en.True answer: The SSB refers to Those Charged with Governance (TCWG) for any administrative matters while remaining completely independent in its function as SSB; SSB members are approved by shareholders in their general meeting upon TCWG's recommendation, and shareholders may periodically authorize TCWG to fix SSB members' remuneration.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 12–14 & Appendix B, BC6–BC8 (Par. 12: SSB members approved by shareholders in general meeting at recommendation of TCWG; Par. 13: 'SSB shall refer to TCWG for any administrative matters. However, it shall be completely independent in its function as SSB'; Par. 14: 'Shareholders may periodically authorise TCWG to fix the remuneration of the SSB members').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Under Paragraph 17(a)–(d) of AAOIFI GS 19, which four factors must an institution assess when evaluating the competence and capability of an SSB candidate?
en.A: Political party affiliation, personal net worth, conventional bond trading volume, and family lineage.
en.B: (a) Demonstrated capacity through qualifications and experience to successfully undertake the position's responsibilities, (b) mental fitness to perform duties, (c) sound knowledge of the business, and (d) ability to allocate sufficient time and attention to the institution considering existing SSB memberships with other organisations, employment, or other time commitments.
en.C: Age above 65 years, residency in the bank's head-office city, fluency in at least four European languages, and ownership of bank shares.
en.D: Prior employment as a commercial loan officer, zero memberships on any other boards, and certification in conventional derivatives.
en.True answer: (a) Demonstrated capacity through qualifications and experience to successfully undertake the position's responsibilities, (b) mental fitness to perform duties, (c) sound knowledge of the business, and (d) ability to allocate sufficient time and attention to the institution considering existing SSB memberships with other organisations, employment, or other time commitments.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 17(a)–(d) (Lists four specific factors in assessing competence and capability: (a) demonstrated, through qualifications and experience, the capacity to successfully undertake responsibilities of the position; (b) mentally fit to perform duties; (c) sound knowledge of the business; and (d) ability to allocate sufficient time and attention to the institution, taking into account existing SSB memberships with other organisations, employment, or other time commitments).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Under Paragraph 19 of AAOIFI GS 19, what are the minimum academic/professional qualification and technical work experience requirements in the Fit and Proper criteria for an 'SSB advisor'?
en.A: A bachelor's degree in any field and at least 2 years of junior banking experience.
en.B: A Ph.D. in classical Usul al-Fiqh and at least 20 years of Fatwa-issuing experience.
en.C: A suitable academic qualification (master's degree or above) and/or professional qualification, along with suitable practical, research, or academic experience in the relevant technical field(s) (such as economics, law, banking, finance, or related fields) of preferably 15 years, but not less than 10 years (in addition to being a Muslim with basic understanding of Shari'ah principles/Fiqh al-Muamalat).
en.D: No academic degree or minimum years of experience are required as long as the advisor holds a valid CPA license.
en.True answer: A suitable academic qualification (master's degree or above) and/or professional qualification, along with suitable practical, research, or academic experience in the relevant technical field(s) (such as economics, law, banking, finance, or related fields) of preferably 15 years, but not less than 10 years (in addition to being a Muslim with basic understanding of Shari'ah principles/Fiqh al-Muamalat).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 19(a)–(k) (Specifically Par. 19(a), (b), (d), (e): Muslim individual; basic understanding of Shari'ah principles and rules and preferably appropriate understanding of Fiqh al-Muamalat; suitable academic [master's degree or above] and/or professional qualification; and suitable practical, research, or academic experience in relevant technical field(s) such as economics, law, banking, finance, and/or related fields of 'preferably 15 years, but not less than 10 years').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Under Paragraph 18 of AAOIFI GS 19, which combination of qualifications, experience, language proficiency, and scholarly stance is required for a Shari'ah scholar to serve as an SSB member?
en.A: Bachelor's degree in Finance, 3 years of commercial banking experience, fluency in English only, and promotion of unique anomalous opinions contradicting scholarly consensus.
en.B: Master's degree in Computer Science, 5 years of Fintech experience, and basic familiarity with Arabic.
en.C: Ph.D. in Secular Law, 15 years of corporate litigation experience, and no requirement to be Muslim.
en.D: Muslim individual; well-versed in Fiqh and Usul al-Fiqh; Shari'ah-related (preferably Fiqh-related) master's degree or above from a recognised institution; at least 10 years of practical, research, or academic experience in Fiqh al-Muamalat; good command of Arabic and common business language(s) in the jurisdiction; reasonable understanding of economics, law, banking, finance, and the financial sector regulatory framework; and NOT having anomalous opinions contradicting well-established contemporary scholarly consensus.
en.True answer: Muslim individual; well-versed in Fiqh and Usul al-Fiqh; Shari'ah-related (preferably Fiqh-related) master's degree or above from a recognised institution; at least 10 years of practical, research, or academic experience in Fiqh al-Muamalat; good command of Arabic and common business language(s) in the jurisdiction; reasonable understanding of economics, law, banking, finance, and the financial sector regulatory framework; and NOT having anomalous opinions contradicting well-established contemporary scholarly consensus.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 18(a)–(l) (Requires: (a) Muslim; (b) well-versed in Fiqh and Usul-Al-Fiqh; (c) Shari'ah-related [preferably Fiqh-related] master's degree or above from recognised institution; (d) at least 10 years practical/research/academic experience in Fiqh Al-Muamalat; (e) experience in Islamic finance/economics/banking/law/business; (f) good command of Arabic and common business language(s); (g) reasonable understanding of economics, law, banking, finance; (h) demonstrable interest/commitment and not having anomalous opinions in contradiction of well-established contemporary scholarly consensus; (i) good understanding of legal/regulatory framework; (j)–(l) character, time, independence).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Under Paragraph 20(d)–(e) of AAOIFI GS 19 ('Ethical considerations for appointment as an SSB member'), which business insolvency and employment history factors must be evaluated during pre-appointment character screening?
en.A: Whether the person has been a director, partner, or involved in the management of a business that went into receivership, insolvency, or compulsory liquidation while connected with that organisation or within a reasonably short period (e.g., one year) after departure, AND whether the person has been dismissed, asked to resign, or resigned from employment or a position of trust/fiduciary appointment because of questions about honesty and integrity.
en.B: Only whether the person was personally declared bankrupt within the preceding 30 days, ignoring any corporate insolvencies or integrity-related resignations.
en.C: Whether the person ever resigned voluntarily from any academic university post to join an Islamic bank.
en.D: Insolvency of a managed business is considered only if the business collapsed more than 15 years prior to the SSB nomination.
en.True answer: Whether the person has been a director, partner, or involved in the management of a business that went into receivership, insolvency, or compulsory liquidation while connected with that organisation or within a reasonably short period (e.g., one year) after departure, AND whether the person has been dismissed, asked to resign, or resigned from employment or a position of trust/fiduciary appointment because of questions about honesty and integrity.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 20(d)–(e) (Requires evaluating: (d) whether the person has been a director, partner, or otherwise involved in the management of a business that has gone into receivership, insolvency, or compulsory liquidation while connected with that organisation or within a reasonably short period [e.g., one year] after departure; and (e) whether the person has been dismissed, asked to resign, or resigned from employment or a position of trust, fiduciary appointment, or similar position because of questions about honesty and integrity).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Under Paragraph 21(d) and (f) of AAOIFI GS 19, how do criminal convictions and regulatory limits on simultaneous SSB memberships affect the disqualification of an SSB member?
en.A: Any minor traffic misdemeanor automatically disqualifies an SSB member, whereas exceeding regulatory limits on simultaneous SSB memberships carries no disqualification consequence.
en.B: An SSB member may be disqualified if convicted of any criminal offence including financial impropriety or moral turpitude (explicitly excluding misdemeanours), OR if he is not in compliance with the maximum limit of global/local SSB memberships if specified by the respective RSA.
en.C: Criminal convictions disqualify an SSB member only if the sentence exceeds 10 years in prison, and GS 19 universally caps global SSB memberships at 2 boards for all jurisdictions.
en.D: Neither criminal offences nor exceeding RSA membership caps can disqualify an active SSB member until his 5-year contract expires.
en.True answer: An SSB member may be disqualified if convicted of any criminal offence including financial impropriety or moral turpitude (explicitly excluding misdemeanours), OR if he is not in compliance with the maximum limit of global/local SSB memberships if specified by the respective RSA.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 21(d) & (f) (Par. 21(d): disqualified if 'convicted of any criminal offence, including financial impropriety or moral turpitude (except misdemeanours)'; Par. 21(f): disqualified if 'not in compliance with the maximum limit of global / local SSB memberships / if specified by the respective RSA').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 22–24 of AAOIFI GS 19, what approvals are required to dismiss an SSB member, and when must the institution notify the Regulatory and Supervisory Authority (RSA) of an SSB member's resignation or removal?
en.A: The CEO may dismiss an SSB member unilaterally, and the RSA is notified once a year in the annual financial report.
en.B: Dismissal requires only a simple majority vote of the remaining SSB members, and RSA notification is optional.
en.C: Dismissal of an SSB member requires a recommendation by TCWG, approval of the shareholders in a general meeting, AND approval of the RSA (unless otherwise specified by the RSA); furthermore, the institution must notify the relevant RSA of any resignation or removal of an SSB member as and when it happens or when action is contemplated/initiated, whichever is earlier, stating the reasons.
en.D: Dismissal requires only TCWG board resolution, and the RSA is notified 6 months after a replacement scholar is hired.
en.True answer: Dismissal of an SSB member requires a recommendation by TCWG, approval of the shareholders in a general meeting, AND approval of the RSA (unless otherwise specified by the RSA); furthermore, the institution must notify the relevant RSA of any resignation or removal of an SSB member as and when it happens or when action is contemplated/initiated, whichever is earlier, stating the reasons.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 22–24 (Par. 23: 'The dismissal of a member of the SSB shall require a recommendation by TCWG and be subject to the approval of the shareholders in a general meeting. It shall also be subject to the RSA's approval unless otherwise specified by the RSA'; Par. 24: 'The institution shall notify the relevant RSA of any resignation or removal of an SSB member as and when it happens or when action is contemplated / initiated, whichever is earlier, stating the reasons').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: In Appendix B (Basis for Conclusions, BC12–BC17) of AAOIFI GS 19, what positions did the Board adopt regarding (1) lowering the minimum 3-member SSB requirement for smaller institutions and (2) adding trainee scholars to the SSB composition?
en.A: (1) GS 19 automatically reduces the minimum SSB size to 1 scholar for all institutions with fewer than 50 employees; (2) appointing at least two trainee scholars to every SSB is mandatory.
en.B: (1) RSAs have zero flexibility to allow fewer than 3 SSB members under any circumstances; (2) trainee scholars are mandatory voting members.
en.C: (1) Smaller institutions need no SSB at all; (2) trainee scholars may chair the SSB after 6 months.
en.D: (1) The Board kept the general minimum of 3 SSB members unchanged in GS 19, while noting that the respective RSA has flexibility to allow a smaller number considering size of operations, nature of business, and cost saving under GS 1 (2024) Principles 12 and 13; (2) the Board concluded that trainee scholars shall NOT be added to the SSB composition and that it should not be considered best practice.
en.True answer: (1) The Board kept the general minimum of 3 SSB members unchanged in GS 19, while noting that the respective RSA has flexibility to allow a smaller number considering size of operations, nature of business, and cost saving under GS 1 (2024) Principles 12 and 13; (2) the Board concluded that trainee scholars shall NOT be added to the SSB composition and that it should not be considered best practice.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Appendix B, BC12–BC17 (BC13–BC14: kept general minimum of 3 SSB members unchanged to ensure diverse viewpoints/expertise, while noting the RSA has flexibility to allow a smaller number considering size of operations, nature of business, and cost saving under GS 1 (2024) Principles 12 and 13; BC16–BC17: concluded that due to lack of sufficient expertise/experience and the sensitive responsibility of supervision and Shari'ah decision-making authority, trainee scholars shall NOT be added to SSB composition and it should not be considered best practice).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Comparing the Fit and Proper criteria for an 'SSB scholar member' (Paragraph 18) versus an 'SSB advisor' (Paragraph 19) under AAOIFI GS 19, which distinction in qualifications, experience duration, and language proficiency is completely accurate?
en.A: An SSB scholar member requires a Shari'ah-related (preferably Fiqh-related) master's degree or above, at least 10 years of experience in Fiqh al-Muamalat, and good command of both Arabic and the common business language(s) in the jurisdiction; whereas an SSB advisor requires a suitable academic (master's or above) and/or professional qualification in a technical field (finance, accounting, economics, law), preferably 15 years (and not less than 10 years) of experience in that technical field, basic understanding of Shari'ah principles/Fiqh al-Muamalat, and good command of the common business language(s) in the jurisdiction (without mandating Arabic fluency).
en.B: An SSB scholar member needs only 5 years of experience in Fiqh al-Muamalat, whereas an SSB advisor requires 20 years of Fatwa-issuing experience and classical Arabic mastery.
en.C: Both SSB scholar members and SSB advisors require a master's degree in Fiqh and at least 15 years of Fiqh al-Muamalat experience.
en.D: An SSB advisor needs only 3 years of technical experience and is exempt from being a Muslim.
en.True answer: An SSB scholar member requires a Shari'ah-related (preferably Fiqh-related) master's degree or above, at least 10 years of experience in Fiqh al-Muamalat, and good command of both Arabic and the common business language(s) in the jurisdiction; whereas an SSB advisor requires a suitable academic (master's or above) and/or professional qualification in a technical field (finance, accounting, economics, law), preferably 15 years (and not less than 10 years) of experience in that technical field, basic understanding of Shari'ah principles/Fiqh al-Muamalat, and good command of the common business language(s) in the jurisdiction (without mandating Arabic fluency).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 18 vs. Par. 19 (Par. 18 [SSB member]: Muslim, master's or above in Shari'ah/Fiqh, at least 10 years experience in Fiqh al-Muamalat, good command of Arabic AND common business language(s); Par. 19 [SSB advisor]: Muslim, basic understanding of Shari'ah principles and preferably Fiqh al-Muamalat, master's degree or above and/or professional qualification in technical field, 'preferably 15 years, but not less than 10 years' experience in technical field, and good command of common business language(s) in the jurisdiction).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: In Appendix B (Basis for Conclusions, BC1–BC11) of AAOIFI GS 19, why did the Board (1) make 'SSB advisors' non-voting preferred advisors rather than mandatory voting members like expert members in GS 8 (CSB), and (2) exclude limits on simultaneous SSB seats and mandatory rotation periods from GS 19?
en.A: (1) Because technical experts have no useful input to offer an SSB; (2) because AAOIFI opposes any rotation or seat limits for Shari'ah scholars.
en.B: (1) To avoid jeopardizing the sanctity of Shari'ah decisions while still capturing technical expertise, the Board took a middle ground—making SSB advisors preferable (not mandatory) without voting rights, and appointed by the institution rather than the SSB itself to maintain their independence and stature; (2) the Board excluded limits on simultaneous SSB seats and rotation rules from GS 19 because certain independence rules already reside in GS 5 ('Independence of Shari'ah Supervisory Board') and will be addressed comprehensively in a dedicated revision project of GS 5.
en.C: (1) Because technical experts are banned by AAOIFI's charter from attending SSB meetings; (2) because rotation rules are governed exclusively by external financial auditors.
en.D: (1) Because SSB advisors are required to be non-Muslim consultants; (2) because GS 19 already mandates a strict limit of 1 SSB seat per scholar globally.
en.True answer: (1) To avoid jeopardizing the sanctity of Shari'ah decisions while still capturing technical expertise, the Board took a middle ground—making SSB advisors preferable (not mandatory) without voting rights, and appointed by the institution rather than the SSB itself to maintain their independence and stature; (2) the Board excluded limits on simultaneous SSB seats and rotation rules from GS 19 because certain independence rules already reside in GS 5 ('Independence of Shari'ah Supervisory Board') and will be addressed comprehensively in a dedicated revision project of GS 5.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Appendix B, BC1–BC5 & BC9–BC11 (BC3–BC5: although GS 8 includes expert members on CSBs, public comments raised concern that mandatory voting expert members on an institutional SSB could jeopardize the sanctity of Shari'ah decisions; Board chose a middle ground—preferable, non-voting SSB advisors appointed by the institution rather than the SSB itself; BC9–BC11: Board excluded limits on simultaneous SSB seats and rotation rules from GS 19 because independence requirements belong under GS 5 and will be addressed in a comprehensive revision project of GS 5).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question:
An Islamic bank evaluates three individuals regarding ethical and disqualification standards under Paragraphs 20–21 of AAOIFI GS 19:
• Individual X (candidate): Served as managing partner of an investment advisory firm that entered compulsory liquidation 7 months after X left the firm.
• Individual Y (candidate): Previously resigned from a fiduciary trust appointment after an internal inquiry raised serious questions about his honesty and integrity.
• Individual Z (active SSB member): Was recently fined for a minor traffic speeding misdemeanour that involved neither financial impropriety nor moral turpitude.
Which evaluation across Individuals X, Y, and Z is completely accurate under GS 19?
en.A: All three (X, Y, and Z) are automatically disqualified/barred under GS 19.
en.B: None of X, Y, or Z raises any ethical or disqualification issue under GS 19.
en.C: Individuals X and Y trigger mandatory ethical character screening considerations before appointment (X under Par. 20(d), because compulsory liquidation occurred within a reasonably short period—e.g., one year—after departure; Y under Par. 20(e), because he resigned from a fiduciary position due to questions about honesty and integrity), whereas active member Z is NOT subject to disqualification under Par. 21(d) because criminal conviction disqualification explicitly excludes misdemeanours.
en.D: Only Individual Z is disqualified for the traffic misdemeanour, while Individuals X and Y face zero ethical scrutiny.
en.True answer: Individuals X and Y trigger mandatory ethical character screening considerations before appointment (X under Par. 20(d), because compulsory liquidation occurred within a reasonably short period—e.g., one year—after departure; Y under Par. 20(e), because he resigned from a fiduciary position due to questions about honesty and integrity), whereas active member Z is NOT subject to disqualification under Par. 21(d) because criminal conviction disqualification explicitly excludes misdemeanours.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 20(d)–(e) & Par. 21(d) (Par. 20(d): ethical screening must evaluate whether candidate was director/partner/involved in management of a business that went into receivership, insolvency, or compulsory liquidation while connected or within a reasonably short period [e.g., 1 year] after departure—7 months falls within 1 year; Par. 20(e): evaluates dismissal or resignation from employment/trust/fiduciary appointment due to questions about honesty and integrity; Par. 21(d): disqualifies for conviction of any criminal offence including financial impropriety or moral turpitude, explicitly stating '(except misdemeanours)').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 22–24 of AAOIFI GS 19, which sequence of steps and approvals is mandatory when an Islamic bank initiates the dismissal of an SSB member?
en.A: The CEO issues a termination notice immediately, obtains post-facto ratification from the Board Audit Committee within 60 days, and notifies the RSA at year-end without stating reasons.
en.B: The remaining SSB members vote to remove the member, and the bank notifies the RSA only after a replacement member has been elected at the next Annual General Meeting.
en.C: The RSA unilaterally dismisses the member without TCWG recommendation or shareholder involvement.
en.D: The process must be independent, transparent, and bias-free; the institution must notify the relevant RSA as and when the removal happens or when action is contemplated/initiated (whichever is earlier), stating the reasons; and dismissal requires a recommendation by TCWG, approval of the shareholders in a general meeting, AND approval of the RSA (unless otherwise specified by the RSA).
en.True answer: The process must be independent, transparent, and bias-free; the institution must notify the relevant RSA as and when the removal happens or when action is contemplated/initiated (whichever is earlier), stating the reasons; and dismissal requires a recommendation by TCWG, approval of the shareholders in a general meeting, AND approval of the RSA (unless otherwise specified by the RSA).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 22–24 (Par. 22: removal/dismissal/rotation must be independent, transparent, objective, and free from bias; Par. 23: dismissal requires recommendation by TCWG, approval of shareholders in general meeting, AND RSA approval unless otherwise specified by RSA; Par. 24: institution shall notify relevant RSA of any resignation or removal as and when it happens or when action is contemplated/initiated, whichever is earlier, stating the reasons).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: In Appendix B (BC6–BC8) and Paragraphs 12–16 of AAOIFI GS 19, why did the Board retain shareholder approval (on TCWG recommendation) for appointing SSB members rather than vesting appointment authority in TCWG or the RSA, and what happens if an institution fails to appoint an SSB within the RSA's stipulated timeframe?
en.A: The Board kept appointment authority with shareholders (as owners and key stakeholders) to maintain a reasonable balance between the stature and authority of TCWG and the SSB since both are appointed by the same authority (shareholders), while allowing shareholders to periodically authorize TCWG to fix SSB remuneration; if an institution fails to appoint an SSB within the timeframe stipulated by the RSA, the RSA may at its discretion appoint a temporary SSB with the cost borne by the institution.
en.B: The Board vested permanent appointment authority in TCWG for convenience, and if an institution fails to appoint an SSB on time, the RSA permanently liquidates the bank.
en.C: The Board vested appointment authority in the external financial auditor, and any temporary SSB appointed by the RSA is funded from the central bank's budget.
en.D: SSB members are appointed for indefinite lifetime contracts, and TCWG fixes SSB remuneration unilaterally without shareholder authorization.
en.True answer: The Board kept appointment authority with shareholders (as owners and key stakeholders) to maintain a reasonable balance between the stature and authority of TCWG and the SSB since both are appointed by the same authority (shareholders), while allowing shareholders to periodically authorize TCWG to fix SSB remuneration; if an institution fails to appoint an SSB within the timeframe stipulated by the RSA, the RSA may at its discretion appoint a temporary SSB with the cost borne by the institution.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 12–16 & Appendix B, BC6–BC8 (BC8: Board decided to keep SSB appointment authority with shareholders as owners/key stakeholders because in order to maintain a reasonable balance between the stature and authority of TCWG and the SSB, it is necessary that both are appointed by the same authority, i.e., shareholders; Par. 14: shareholders may periodically authorise TCWG to fix remuneration; Par. 15: RSA at its discretion may appoint a temporary SSB if institution fails to appoint within stipulated time, with cost borne by institution; Par. 16: written contract for service for 3 to 5 years).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question: Which of the following accurately synthesizes AAOIFI GS 19 provisions on (1) diversity in SSB composition (Paragraph 11), (2) RSA flexibility for smaller institutions (Appendix B, BC12–BC14), and (3) appointment of trainee scholars to an SSB (Appendix B, BC15–BC17)?
en.A: (1) SSB composition must consist exclusively of senior scholars from a single Madhhab; (2) smaller institutions can never have fewer than 3 SSB members even with RSA approval; (3) trainee scholars are mandatory on every SSB.
en.B: (1) SSB composition should preferably reflect diverse expertise and exposure, including representation from different schools of thought in the country, different fields of relevant industry expertise, and both senior and junior scholars; (2) while GS 19 maintains a general minimum of 3 SSB members, the respective RSA has flexibility to allow a smaller number considering operational size, nature of business, and cost saving under GS 1 (2024) Principles 12 and 13; and (3) trainee scholars shall NOT be added to the SSB composition and should not be considered best practice.
en.C: (1) Junior scholars are barred from serving on SSBs; (2) GS 19 automatically exempts all Islamic windows from having an SSB; (3) trainee scholars may serve as non-voting SSB chairs.
en.D: (1) Diversity applies only to external auditors; (2) RSAs have no authority over SSB size; (3) trainee scholars are required for succession planning.
en.True answer: (1) SSB composition should preferably reflect diverse expertise and exposure, including representation from different schools of thought in the country, different fields of relevant industry expertise, and both senior and junior scholars; (2) while GS 19 maintains a general minimum of 3 SSB members, the respective RSA has flexibility to allow a smaller number considering operational size, nature of business, and cost saving under GS 1 (2024) Principles 12 and 13; and (3) trainee scholars shall NOT be added to the SSB composition and should not be considered best practice.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19, Par. 11 & Appendix B, BC12–BC17 (Par. 11: SSB composition should preferably reflect diverse expertise and exposure, including representation from different schools of thought in the country, different fields of expertise/knowledge/experience relevant to Islamic finance, and both senior and junior scholars; BC13–BC14: general minimum is 3 members, but RSA has flexibility to allow a smaller number considering operational size, nature of business, and cost saving under GS 1 (2024) Principles 12 and 13; BC17: trainee scholars shall NOT be added to the SSB composition and it should not be considered best practice).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question:
In January 2026, a newly licensed Islamic bank nominates four individuals to form its Shari'ah Supervisory Board (SSB) governance structure:
• Candidate 1 (for SSB scholar member): A Muslim scholar holding a Master's degree in Fiqh with 11 years of Fiqh al-Muamalat research/advisory experience, fluent in Arabic and the local business language, with a clean ethical record.
• Candidate 2 (for SSB scholar member): A Muslim scholar holding a Ph.D. in Shari'ah with 14 years of experience, who publicly advocates anomalous Fatwas directly contradicting established contemporary scholarly consensus and was managing director of a company that entered compulsory liquidation 8 months after he resigned.
• Candidate 3 (for non-voting SSB advisor): A Muslim banking and accounting specialist holding a Master's in Finance with 12 years of Islamic banking experience and a basic understanding of Shari'ah principles/Fiqh al-Muamalat, fluent in the local business language (though not fluent in classical Arabic).
• Candidate 4 (for trainee scholar on the SSB): A recent Shari'ah graduate with 1 year of experience nominated as a 'trainee scholar' on the SSB to build future succession.
According to AAOIFI GS 19, which evaluation across Candidates 1–4 is completely accurate?
en.A: Candidates 1, 2, and 3 are all eligible, while only Candidate 4 is excluded.
en.B: Candidates 1 and 4 are eligible, while Candidates 2 and 3 are disqualified (Candidate 3 lacks classical Arabic fluency and 15 years of experience).
en.C: Candidate 1 is eligible under Par. 18; Candidate 2 fails Par. 18(h) (anomalous opinions contradicting established contemporary scholarly consensus) and triggers ethical screening under Par. 20(d) (compulsory liquidation of a managed business within 1 year after departure); Candidate 3 IS eligible as a non-voting SSB advisor under Par. 19 (which requires a Master's/professional qualification, not less than 10 years [preferably 15 years] technical experience, basic Shari'ah understanding, and common business language—not classical Arabic); and Candidate 4 is ineligible because Appendix B (BC15–BC17) concludes that trainee scholars shall NOT be added to the SSB composition.
en.D: Only Candidate 1 is eligible; Candidate 3 fails because SSB advisors require 15 years of Fiqh al-Muamalat experience.
en.True answer: Candidate 1 is eligible under Par. 18; Candidate 2 fails Par. 18(h) (anomalous opinions contradicting established contemporary scholarly consensus) and triggers ethical screening under Par. 20(d) (compulsory liquidation of a managed business within 1 year after departure); Candidate 3 IS eligible as a non-voting SSB advisor under Par. 19 (which requires a Master's/professional qualification, not less than 10 years [preferably 15 years] technical experience, basic Shari'ah understanding, and common business language—not classical Arabic); and Candidate 4 is ineligible because Appendix B (BC15–BC17) concludes that trainee scholars shall NOT be added to the SSB composition.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19 integrates four rules: (1) Par. 18(a)–(l): Candidate 1 meets all SSB scholar member criteria (Muslim, Master's in Fiqh, ≥10 years Fiqh al-Muamalat, Arabic + business language); (2) Par. 18(h) disqualifies scholars holding anomalous opinions contradicting well-established contemporary scholarly consensus, and Par. 20(d) flags management involvement in a business entering compulsory liquidation within ~1 year after departure; (3) Par. 19(a)–(k): Candidate 3 qualifies as a non-voting SSB advisor (Muslim, Master's in Finance, 12 years ≥ 10-year minimum [15 preferred] technical experience, basic Shari'ah understanding, common business language—Arabic is not required in Par. 19); (4) Appendix B, BC15–BC17: Board explicitly concluded that trainee scholars shall NOT be added to the SSB composition.

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 19: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition
en.Question:
During 2026, an Islamic bank experiences four governance events involving its Shari'ah Supervisory Board (SSB):
(1) Because an SSB scholar repeatedly questioned the Shari'ah structure of a profitable Murabaha campaign, the Board of Directors (TCWG) passes an executive resolution dismissing the scholar immediately—without seeking shareholder approval in a general meeting and without obtaining RSA approval.
(2) Management waits until three weeks after the dismissal resolution is executed before notifying the RSA, and omits stating the reasons for the removal.
(3) Another SSB member is convicted of a minor municipal parking misdemeanour (not involving financial impropriety or moral turpitude), while a third SSB member accepts a 6th global SSB seat in breach of the RSA's mandatory cap of 4 SSB memberships per scholar.
(4) During an external Shari'ah compliance and fiduciary rating under GS 10, an ambiguity arises regarding the interpretation of a Shari'ah-related requirement in an AAOIFI Financial Accounting Standard (FAS), and the rating agency insists its own interpretation overrides the institution's SSB clarification.
According to AAOIFI GS 19, which evaluation across (1)–(4) is completely accurate?
en.A: (1) Compliant—TCWG may dismiss SSB members unilaterally; (2) Compliant—notifying the RSA within 30 days after dismissal suffices; (3) Both members are automatically disqualified; (4) Compliant—rating agencies override institutional SSBs on FAS interpretations.
en.B: (1) Non-compliant; (2) Compliant; (3) Neither member is subject to disqualification; (4) Non-compliant.
en.C: (1) Compliant; (2) Non-compliant; (3) Only the member with the parking misdemeanour is disqualified; (4) Compliant.
en.D: (1) Non-compliant—under Par. 23, dismissal of an SSB member requires a recommendation by TCWG, approval of shareholders in a general meeting, AND approval of the RSA (unless otherwise specified by the RSA); (2) Non-compliant—violates Par. 24, which mandates notifying the relevant RSA of any resignation or removal as and when it happens or when action is contemplated/initiated (whichever is earlier), stating the reasons; (3) Under Par. 21(d) and (f), the parking misdemeanour does NOT disqualify the second member (Par. 21(d) explicitly excludes misdemeanours), whereas the third member IS subject to disqualification under Par. 21(f) for breaching the RSA's maximum limit on global/local SSB memberships; (4) Non-compliant—under Par. 5(b) Explanation, if an ambiguity is identified during a compliance, audit, or rating exercise regarding interpretations of tiers (i) to (iv) (including AAOIFI FAS Shari'ah-related requirements), the institution's SSB clarification shall prevail.
en.True answer: (1) Non-compliant—under Par. 23, dismissal of an SSB member requires a recommendation by TCWG, approval of shareholders in a general meeting, AND approval of the RSA (unless otherwise specified by the RSA); (2) Non-compliant—violates Par. 24, which mandates notifying the relevant RSA of any resignation or removal as and when it happens or when action is contemplated/initiated (whichever is earlier), stating the reasons; (3) Under Par. 21(d) and (f), the parking misdemeanour does NOT disqualify the second member (Par. 21(d) explicitly excludes misdemeanours), whereas the third member IS subject to disqualification under Par. 21(f) for breaching the RSA's maximum limit on global/local SSB memberships; (4) Non-compliant—under Par. 5(b) Explanation, if an ambiguity is identified during a compliance, audit, or rating exercise regarding interpretations of tiers (i) to (iv) (including AAOIFI FAS Shari'ah-related requirements), the institution's SSB clarification shall prevail.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 19 integrates four rules: (1) Par. 23 requires TCWG recommendation, shareholder general meeting approval, AND RSA approval (unless otherwise specified by RSA) for dismissing an SSB member; (2) Par. 24 mandates notifying the RSA of any resignation or removal as and when it happens or when action is contemplated/initiated (whichever is earlier), stating the reasons; (3) Par. 21(d) explicitly excludes misdemeanours from criminal conviction disqualification, while Par. 21(f) subjects a member to disqualification for non-compliance with the RSA's maximum limit of global/local SSB memberships; (4) Par. 5(b) Explanation stipulates that in case of an ambiguity identified during a compliance, audit, or rating exercise regarding interpretations of tiers (i)–(iv) (which include AAOIFI FAS Shari'ah-related requirements), 'the Shari'ah supervisory board's clarification shall prevail'.

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Which of the following accurately describes which prior standard AAOIFI GS 20 supersedes (together with GS 19), its companion standards, and its effective date?
en.A: GS 20, together with GS 19 ('Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition'), supersedes the earlier GS 1 ('Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment, Composition and Report'), is read in conjunction with GS 1 (2024), GS 19, GS 21, and GS 5, and is effective on or after 1 January 2026.
en.B: GS 20 supersedes GS 5 ('Independence of Shari'ah Supervisory Board') and GS 8 ('Central Shari'ah Board'), and became effective retroactively on 1 July 2021.
en.C: GS 20 supersedes GS 9 ('Shari'ah Compliance Function') and applies exclusively to standalone full-fledged Islamic commercial banks.
en.D: GS 20 leaves the original GS 1 in full force without superseding any standard and becomes effective on 1 January 2030.
en.True answer: GS 20, together with GS 19 ('Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition'), supersedes the earlier GS 1 ('Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment, Composition and Report'), is read in conjunction with GS 1 (2024), GS 19, GS 21, and GS 5, and is effective on or after 1 January 2026.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Preface PR5, Par. 2–4 & Par. 84 (PR5: GS 20, along with GS 19, supersedes GS 1 'Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment, Composition and Report'; Par. 2–3: applies to all IFIs including Islamic finance windows across all sectors, and to other institutions adopting AAOIFI GSs including Waqf/social finance and Sukuk SSBs; Par. 4: read in conjunction with GS 1 (2024), GS 19, GS 21, and GS 5; Par. 84: effective on or after 1 January 2026).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 7–9 of AAOIFI GS 20, what is the legal/governance effect of SSB Fatwas and rulings on the institution, and what restriction applies to the SSB's involvement in business and managerial activities?
en.A: SSB Fatwas are purely non-binding commercial recommendations that management may ignore, while SSB members are encouraged to participate directly in executive credit committees.
en.B: Fatwas and rulings (related to Shari'ah matters) issued by the SSB are binding on the institution (insofar as aligned with the hierarchy of Shari'ah principles and rules), the SSB is responsible for the quality, accuracy, and soundness of its decisions, and the SSB and its members must NOT be involved in any manner with regard to business and managerial decisions and operational responsibilities of the institution.
en.C: SSB Fatwas are binding only on retail customers, while the SSB Chairman co-signs operational treasury trades alongside the CEO.
en.D: The SSB bears zero accountability for the quality or accuracy of its rulings, and may assume operational management of the Shari'ah Compliance Department.
en.True answer: Fatwas and rulings (related to Shari'ah matters) issued by the SSB are binding on the institution (insofar as aligned with the hierarchy of Shari'ah principles and rules), the SSB is responsible for the quality, accuracy, and soundness of its decisions, and the SSB and its members must NOT be involved in any manner with regard to business and managerial decisions and operational responsibilities of the institution.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 7–9 (Par. 7: 'The SSB shall issue Fatwas and rulings (related to Shari'ah matters) which shall be binding on the institution (insofar as aligned with the hierarchy of Shari'ah principles and rules (see paragraph 5(g)))'; Par. 8: 'The SSB shall be responsible for the quality, accuracy and soundness of its decisions'; Par. 9: 'The SSB and its members should not be involved in any manner with regard to business and managerial decisions and operational responsibilities of the institution').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 10–15 of AAOIFI GS 20, which set of specific supervisory duties is assigned to the SSB?
en.A: Approving commercial loan interest rates, setting branch staffing budgets, and preparing corporate tax returns.
en.B: Auditing external IT vendors' hardware warranties and managing retail marketing campaigns.
en.C: Approving all product/service documentation (contracts, agreements, marketing/promotional materials) and reviewing/approving policies/procedures for Shari'ah compliance; vetting the investment accounts (IAs) strategy/policy framework and overseeing profit/loss calculation and distribution to IAHs; reviewing and approving the accounting treatment of products/services (considering Chapter 7 of AAOIFI's Conceptual Framework); reviewing and approving annual Zakah calculations (per FAS 39); and specifying disposal of prohibited earnings, verifying their charitable use, and taking measures to systematically reduce/eliminate such income.
en.D: Preparing daily journal entries for Mudaraba pools and directly distributing Zakah cash to individual recipients.
en.True answer: Approving all product/service documentation (contracts, agreements, marketing/promotional materials) and reviewing/approving policies/procedures for Shari'ah compliance; vetting the investment accounts (IAs) strategy/policy framework and overseeing profit/loss calculation and distribution to IAHs; reviewing and approving the accounting treatment of products/services (considering Chapter 7 of AAOIFI's Conceptual Framework); reviewing and approving annual Zakah calculations (per FAS 39); and specifying disposal of prohibited earnings, verifying their charitable use, and taking measures to systematically reduce/eliminate such income.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 10–15 & Footnotes 10–12 (Par. 10: approve all product/service contracts, agreements, marketing/promotional materials, and review/approve policies/procedures for Shari'ah compliance; Par. 12: vet IAs strategy/policy framework and oversee profit/loss calculation and distribution to IAHs; Par. 13 & Footnote 11: review/approve accounting treatment considering AAOIFI Conceptual Framework Ch. 7; Par. 14 & Footnote 12: review/approve annual Zakah calculations per FAS 39; Par. 15: specify disposal of prohibited earnings, verify charitable use, and reduce/eliminate recurrence).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 26–30 of AAOIFI GS 20, what are the mandatory requirements for SSB meeting quorum, minimum annual meeting frequency, minimum member attendance, proxy attendance, and advance agenda submission?
en.A: Quorum requires 100% attendance; minimum 2 meetings per year; 50% attendance allowed via proxy; agenda sent 24 hours before the meeting.
en.B: Quorum is any 2 members; minimum 12 meetings per year; 90% attendance required; agenda sent at the start of the meeting.
en.C: Quorum is one-third of members; minimum 1 meeting per year; proxy attendance permitted for absent scholars; agenda sent 3 days in advance.
en.D: Quorum requires a majority of SSB members present; the SSB must meet no less than four times a year; each member must attend at least three-fourths (75%) of meetings during a calendar year (including via video or conference call) and CANNOT appoint another person to attend on his behalf; and the agenda with sufficient details/background documents must be sent in advance in no case less than one week prior to the meeting.
en.True answer: Quorum requires a majority of SSB members present; the SSB must meet no less than four times a year; each member must attend at least three-fourths (75%) of meetings during a calendar year (including via video or conference call) and CANNOT appoint another person to attend on his behalf; and the agenda with sufficient details/background documents must be sent in advance in no case less than one week prior to the meeting.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 26–30 (Par. 26: proper quorum in which a majority of members shall be present; Par. 27: meet frequently, but no less than four times a year; Par. 28: each member shall attend at least three-fourths [75%] of meetings during a calendar year, including through video or conference calls, and cannot appoint another person to attend on his behalf; Par. 30: agenda and related background documents sent in advance, in no case less than one week prior to the meeting).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 33–36 of AAOIFI GS 20, what rules govern the approval of SSB meeting minutes, circular approvals, and meetings between the SSB and Those Charged with Governance (TCWG)?
en.A: Meeting minutes (recording decisions, rationale, and any dissenting opinions) must be approved (and preferably signed) by all attending SSB members no later than in the next meeting; any SSB approval taken through circulation must be recorded as part of the minutes of the next SSB meeting; and the SSB is strongly recommended to meet with TCWG at least once a year and document its observations, concerns, and suggestions.
en.B: Minutes are approved solely by the CEO, circular approvals are never recorded in meeting minutes, and the SSB is prohibited from meeting with TCWG.
en.C: Minutes require approval only at the end of the 5-year SSB term, and dissenting opinions are omitted from minutes.
en.D: Circular approvals replace formal SSB meetings entirely, and TCWG meetings occur only once every three years.
en.True answer: Meeting minutes (recording decisions, rationale, and any dissenting opinions) must be approved (and preferably signed) by all attending SSB members no later than in the next meeting; any SSB approval taken through circulation must be recorded as part of the minutes of the next SSB meeting; and the SSB is strongly recommended to meet with TCWG at least once a year and document its observations, concerns, and suggestions.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 33–36 (Par. 33: minutes include decisions, rationale, and dissenting notes, and shall be approved—and preferably signed—by all attending SSB members no later than in the next meeting; Par. 35: any SSB approval taken through circulation shall be part of the minutes of the next SSB meeting; Par. 36: SSB is strongly recommended to meet with TCWG at least once a year and document observations, concerns, and suggestions).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 38–39 of AAOIFI GS 20, where must an institution publish its SSB's product/service Shari'ah rulings along with their jurisprudential basis, and whose views must be included in the Shari'ah Compliance Department's pre-submission product review checklist?
en.A: Rulings are kept strictly confidential in internal vaults, and the checklist requires only the marketing manager's signature.
en.B: The institution must ensure that all Shari'ah rulings regarding products/services offered, along with their respective religious/jurisprudential basis, are made available on the institution's website at all times; and the minimum product review checklist used by the SCD before presenting documents to the SSB must cover key features, processes, structure, legal contracts, risk/compliance, marketing collateral, AND must also include the views of the head of legal.
en.C: Rulings are published without their basis of conclusion once every five years, and legal department views are excluded from the checklist.
en.D: Only the external auditor receives copies of product rulings, and the checklist is prepared by external IT vendors.
en.True answer: The institution must ensure that all Shari'ah rulings regarding products/services offered, along with their respective religious/jurisprudential basis, are made available on the institution's website at all times; and the minimum product review checklist used by the SCD before presenting documents to the SSB must cover key features, processes, structure, legal contracts, risk/compliance, marketing collateral, AND must also include the views of the head of legal.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 38–39 (Par. 38: 'The SSB shall, at all times, make available all the Shari'ah rulings regarding products / services offered by the institution along with their respective basis (religious / jurisprudential evidence). The institution shall ensure that these rulings and their respective basis are made available on the institution's website'; Par. 39: minimum SCD checklist includes key features, processes, structure, documentation/legal contracts, risk and compliance considerations, marketing collateral, and explicitly states: 'The views of the head of legal shall also be included').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 42–47 of AAOIFI GS 20, who designs and implements the continuous professional development (CPD) programme for SSB members, and to whom must TCWG submit the SSB's annual performance assessment report?
en.A: The SSB designs and funds its own CPD programme without management involvement, and the annual performance assessment report is kept confidential from the RSA.
en.B: The external financial auditor designs the SSB's CPD programme, and the performance assessment report is submitted to retail depositors.
en.C: Management designs and implements the continuous professional development programme for SSB members in consultation with the SSB; and the SSB's annual performance assessment report (covering individual and collective assessment across four areas) must be submitted by TCWG to the respective Regulatory and Supervisory Authority (RSA) on an annual basis (unless otherwise specified by the RSA).
en.D: CPD is optional for SSB members, and performance assessments occur once every five years.
en.True answer: Management designs and implements the continuous professional development programme for SSB members in consultation with the SSB; and the SSB's annual performance assessment report (covering individual and collective assessment across four areas) must be submitted by TCWG to the respective Regulatory and Supervisory Authority (RSA) on an annual basis (unless otherwise specified by the RSA).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 42–47 & Appendix C, BC1–BC3 (Par. 42 & BC3: management designs and implements the CPD programme for SSB members in consultation with the SSB; Par. 45–47: SSB conducts annual performance assessment [individually and collectively], and TCWG submits the SSB's performance assessment report to the respective RSA on an annual basis unless otherwise specified by the RSA).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 54–58 and 62 of AAOIFI GS 20, which financial and commercial independence restrictions apply to an SSB member (and his immediate/close family)?
en.A: An SSB member may hold up to 15% of the bank's shares and receive a year-end bonus tied to the bank's net profit growth.
en.B: An SSB member's spouse may serve as the bank's CEO as long as the SSB member abstains from voting on HR budgets.
en.C: An SSB member may own shares in an external Shari'ah audit firm auditing the same bank if his stake is below 25%.
en.D: Remuneration must not be contingent on findings/results or linked to institution performance bonuses; neither the SSB member nor his immediate/close family may serve as CEO, director, or key management (for the current or last financial year) or be an employee (for the current or last financial year) of the institution or related companies; neither he nor his immediate/close family may be a substantial shareholder (5% or as specified by jurisdiction, or 10% of the person's net worth, whichever is lower) of the institution/subsidiaries or of an entity with significant payments to/from the institution; and neither he nor his immediate/close family may be shareholders or employees of a company providing Shari'ah consultancy and/or Shari'ah audit services to the same institution.
en.True answer: Remuneration must not be contingent on findings/results or linked to institution performance bonuses; neither the SSB member nor his immediate/close family may serve as CEO, director, or key management (for the current or last financial year) or be an employee (for the current or last financial year) of the institution or related companies; neither he nor his immediate/close family may be a substantial shareholder (5% or as specified by jurisdiction, or 10% of the person's net worth, whichever is lower) of the institution/subsidiaries or of an entity with significant payments to/from the institution; and neither he nor his immediate/close family may be shareholders or employees of a company providing Shari'ah consultancy and/or Shari'ah audit services to the same institution.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 54–58 & Par. 62 (Par. 54 & 62: no contingent fee or performance-based bonus; Par. 55: no CEO/director/key management/employee role in institution or related companies for current or last financial year for member or immediate/close family; Par. 56–57: no substantial shareholding [5% or 10% of person's net worth, whichever is lower] in institution/subsidiaries or significant payment counterparty; Par. 58: member or immediate/close family shall not be shareholders or employees of a company providing the same institution with Shari'ah consultancy and/or Shari'ah audit services).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 59, 63–64, and 72–73 of AAOIFI GS 20, which rules govern an SSB member's banking relationship with the institution, gift acceptance, conflict-of-interest resolution, post-assignment confidentiality, and public criticism of a majority Fatwa?
