en.A: An SSB member may be a depositor/IAH or seek financing in the normal course of business (without special rates or preferential treatment, and disclosed in the annual report); may accept only gifts/services within normal courtesies of social life; must abstain in temporary conflicts of interest and MUST resign (notifying the general assembly) if a conflict is unresolved or permanent; remains bound by confidentiality even after ceasing to serve; and may document a dissenting opinion per policy, but shall NOT criticize a majority Fatwa publicly or use it to inflict reputational damage.
en.B: An SSB member is entitled to preferential zero-margin financing as a standard benefit, and may hold press conferences criticizing majority Fatwas he disagreed with.
en.C: Confidentiality obligations expire automatically on the day an SSB member completes his 3-year contract.
en.D: If an SSB member faces a permanent conflict of interest, he may remain on the board indefinitely as long as he discloses it once in writing.
en.True answer: An SSB member may be a depositor/IAH or seek financing in the normal course of business (without special rates or preferential treatment, and disclosed in the annual report); may accept only gifts/services within normal courtesies of social life; must abstain in temporary conflicts of interest and MUST resign (notifying the general assembly) if a conflict is unresolved or permanent; remains bound by confidentiality even after ceasing to serve; and may document a dissenting opinion per policy, but shall NOT criticize a majority Fatwa publicly or use it to inflict reputational damage.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 59 (Footnote 17), Par. 63–64 & Par. 72–73 (Par. 59 & Footnote 17: may be depositor/IAH or seek financing in normal course of business with no special rates/preferential treatment, disclosed in annual report; Par. 63: gifts/services acceptable only within normal courtesies of social life; Par. 64(c)–(d): abstain in temporary conflict, resign and notify general assembly if unresolved or permanent; Par. 72: confidentiality obligations do not end when member ceases to serve; Par. 73: right to document dissent per policy, 'but shall not criticise such Fatwa publicly or use it to inflict reputational damage on the institution or its SSB').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 79–83 of AAOIFI GS 20, which transparency and disclosure obligations apply to an institution regarding its SSB report, past 12 months' Shari'ah pronouncements, and annual report disclosures?
en.A: The SSB report is shared solely with the CEO; product Fatwas are disclosed only to institutional Sukuk buyers; and SSB remuneration is omitted from the annual report.
en.B: The SSB report must be published as part of the annual report and presented at the Annual General Meeting (AGM) to shareholders by at least one SSB member (preferably the chairman) who responds to their queries; the institution must disclose SSB pronouncements/resolutions for the past 12 months related to offered products/services along with their rationales/basis of conclusion (maintaining an archive for preceding years) as well as any departures/revisions; and the annual report must disclose at minimum governance arrangements, member qualifications, appointments/changes, total remuneration paid to SSB members in aggregate, material financing/deposit relationships, conflicts of interest, meeting count and individual attendance, number/nature/resolution of Shari'ah non-compliance events, and trainings attended by SSB members.
en.C: Only the individual remuneration of the SSB Chairman is disclosed, while non-compliance events and meeting attendance records are kept strictly confidential.
en.D: Disclosing rationales behind Fatwas is prohibited, and no SSB member is permitted to attend the Annual General Meeting.
en.True answer: The SSB report must be published as part of the annual report and presented at the Annual General Meeting (AGM) to shareholders by at least one SSB member (preferably the chairman) who responds to their queries; the institution must disclose SSB pronouncements/resolutions for the past 12 months related to offered products/services along with their rationales/basis of conclusion (maintaining an archive for preceding years) as well as any departures/revisions; and the annual report must disclose at minimum governance arrangements, member qualifications, appointments/changes, total remuneration paid to SSB members in aggregate, material financing/deposit relationships, conflicts of interest, meeting count and individual attendance, number/nature/resolution of Shari'ah non-compliance events, and trainings attended by SSB members.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 79–83(a)–(i) (Par. 79–80: SSB report published in annual report, and at least one SSB member [preferably chairman] presents SSB report at AGM and responds to shareholder queries; Par. 81–82: disclose past 12 months' pronouncements/resolutions on offered products/services with rationales/basis [plus archive of preceding years] and any departures/revisions in clear, simple language; Par. 83(a)–(i): annual report disclosures including aggregate remuneration [83(d)], attendance [83(g)], non-compliance events/resolution [83(h)], and trainings attended [83(i)]).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 16–19 of AAOIFI GS 20, how do the SSB's governance rights differ between appointing and appraising the Head of the Shari'ah Compliance Department (SCD) versus the Head of Internal Shari'ah Audit (ISA)?
en.A: The SSB unilaterally appoints and dismisses both the Head of SCD and the Head of ISA without management or audit committee involvement.
en.B: The SSB has no role in appointing or appraising either the Head of SCD or the Head of ISA.
en.C: The consent of the SSB must be obtained for appointing the Head of SCD, whereas the SSB must be consulted on appointing the Head of ISA; for annual performance evaluation, the SSB is consulted by management and the audit and governance committee (AGC) to assess both heads, and the appraisal of their Shari'ah-related performance must be conducted by the SSB.
en.D: The SSB is consulted only on the Head of SCD's salary, while the Head of ISA is appraised exclusively by the CEO.
en.True answer: The consent of the SSB must be obtained for appointing the Head of SCD, whereas the SSB must be consulted on appointing the Head of ISA; for annual performance evaluation, the SSB is consulted by management and the audit and governance committee (AGC) to assess both heads, and the appraisal of their Shari'ah-related performance must be conducted by the SSB.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 18–19 (Par. 18: 'The consent of the SSB shall be obtained for the appointment of the head of the Shari'ah compliance department. The SSB shall also be consulted on the appointment of the head of the internal Shari'ah audit department'; Par. 19: 'The SSB shall be consulted by the management and the audit and governance committee to evaluate and assess, on an annual basis, the performance of the head of the Shari'ah compliance department and the head of internal Shari'ah audit. The appraisal of the Shari'ah related performance shall be conducted by the SSB').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraph 77 and Appendix C (BC9–BC12) of AAOIFI GS 20, what accountability rule applies when an SSB delegates specific tasks or relies on one of its members?
en.A: Once a task is delegated to a resident scholar or executive committee, the remaining SSB members are completely relieved of responsibility for that area.
en.B: Delegation transfers legal accountability solely to the Head of the Shari'ah Compliance Department.
en.C: Any delegation of tasks within an SSB is strictly prohibited under all circumstances.
en.D: SSB members are, and remain, individually responsible for their own work as members of the SSB irrespective of any delegation or reliance on other members of the SSB.
en.True answer: SSB members are, and remain, individually responsible for their own work as members of the SSB irrespective of any delegation or reliance on other members of the SSB.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 77 & Appendix C, BC9–BC12 (Par. 77: 'SSB members are, and shall remain, individually responsible for their own work as members of the SSB (irrespective of any delegation or reliance on other members of the SSB)'; BC10–BC12 confirm that while limited delegation may take permissible forms allowed by RSAs and GS 18 Par. 69–71, it never relieves SSB members of individual responsibility).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 20–22 of AAOIFI GS 20, what structured sequence of actions and escalations must an SSB follow when (1) an isolated Shari'ah non-compliance is identified, (2) systematic Shari'ah non-compliance is suspected, and (3) non-compliant activities persist or TCWG fail to address the SSB's concerns?
en.A: (1) Advise management to take corrective action (if feasible), remedial action to deal with consequences (if correction is not feasible), or preventive measures to avoid recurrence—generally stopping the respective products/services immediately until preventive measures are in place; (2) if systematic non-compliance is believed to occur, inform TCWG and suggest suitable measures to rectify the situation; and (3) if non-compliant activities continue despite these measures or TCWG fail to effectively address the concerns, inform the respective Regulatory and Supervisory Authority (RSA) and report such violations in the SSB report.
en.B: (1) Ignore isolated breaches if profit margins remain positive; (2) escalate directly to public media before notifying TCWG; and (3) refrain from mentioning ongoing breaches in the SSB report until the RSA conducts an inspection.
en.C: (1) Allow the non-compliant product to continue selling for 6 months while drafting new policies; (2) report systematic breaches solely to the CEO; and (3) never contact the RSA without the CEO's written permission.
en.D: (1) Demand immediate criminal prosecution of branch tellers; (2) dissolve the Audit Committee; and (3) withhold the annual SSB report until all breaches are resolved.
en.True answer: (1) Advise management to take corrective action (if feasible), remedial action to deal with consequences (if correction is not feasible), or preventive measures to avoid recurrence—generally stopping the respective products/services immediately until preventive measures are in place; (2) if systematic non-compliance is believed to occur, inform TCWG and suggest suitable measures to rectify the situation; and (3) if non-compliant activities continue despite these measures or TCWG fail to effectively address the concerns, inform the respective Regulatory and Supervisory Authority (RSA) and report such violations in the SSB report.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 20(a)–(c) Explanation, Par. 21 & Par. 22 (Par. 20: advise management to take (a) corrective action if feasible, (b) remedial action if correction is not feasible, or (c) preventive measures to avoid recurrence [Explanation: first step is generally stopping the respective products and services immediately till preventive measures take place]; Par. 21: if systematic non-compliance is carried out, inform TCWG and suggest suitable measures; Par. 22: if non-compliant activities continue despite above measures or TCWG fail to effectively address SSB concerns, inform respective RSA and report such violations in SSB report).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 45–47, Appendix B (B1–B2), and Appendix C (BC4–BC8) of AAOIFI GS 20, how is the SSB's annual performance assessment structured to protect its independence and stature?
en.A: The Chief Executive Officer and Board of Directors conduct unilateral technical grading of each scholar's Fatwas and reduce fees for scholars who issue unfavorable rulings.
en.B: Performance assessment is conducted annually both collectively and individually across four core areas (values and ethics, leadership and commitment, independence and objectivity, and knowledge and learning) primarily from within the SSB through a combination of peer assessment and chairman assessment (alongside objective administrative assessment by management, such as meeting attendance) so as not to subordinate the SSB to TCWG or management; if a third party is engaged (with SSB approval), it is responsible ONLY for the administrative assessment and administering the process for peer/self-assessment of technical aspects; and TCWG submits the assessment report to the RSA annually.
en.C: External management consultants directly grade the Fiqhi validity of SSB Fatwas and recommend dismissing conservative scholars.
en.D: Performance assessment applies only to the SSB Secretary, while SSB scholars are exempt from any collective or individual evaluation.
en.True answer: Performance assessment is conducted annually both collectively and individually across four core areas (values and ethics, leadership and commitment, independence and objectivity, and knowledge and learning) primarily from within the SSB through a combination of peer assessment and chairman assessment (alongside objective administrative assessment by management, such as meeting attendance) so as not to subordinate the SSB to TCWG or management; if a third party is engaged (with SSB approval), it is responsible ONLY for the administrative assessment and administering the process for peer/self-assessment of technical aspects; and TCWG submits the assessment report to the RSA annually.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 45–47, Appendix B (B1–B2) & Appendix C, BC4–BC8 (BC7–BC8: assessment must be primarily from within the SSB via peer assessment and chairman assessment—plus objective administrative assessment by management e.g. attendance—so SSB is not subordinated to TCWG/management; Par. 46 Explanation & BC8: if a third party is engaged with SSB approval, it is responsible ONLY for administrative assessment and administering the process for peer/self-assessment of technical aspects; Appendix B B2: 4 areas—values/ethics, leadership/commitment, independence/objectivity, knowledge/learning; Par. 47: TCWG submits report to RSA annually).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 55–57 of AAOIFI GS 20, how are 'immediate family' and 'close family' defined, and what quantitative shareholding threshold disqualifies an SSB member from holding an equity stake in the institution or in a significant payment counterparty?
en.A: Immediate family includes only the spouse, close family includes cousins, and the shareholding threshold is 25% of voting shares.
en.B: Immediate and close family are excluded from independence checks, and an SSB member may hold up to 10% of the institution's equity regardless of personal net worth.
en.C: 'Immediate family' comprises spouse and dependent children, while 'close family' comprises parents, non-dependent children, and siblings; an SSB member or any immediate/close family member (individually or collectively, directly or indirectly) must NOT be a substantial shareholder—defined as 5% (or as specified by the jurisdiction) OR 10% of the net worth of the person, WHICHEVER IS LOWER—of the institution/subsidiaries or of an organization from/to which the institution made or received significant payments in the current or immediate past financial year.
en.D: The substantial shareholding threshold is 5% or 10% of the person's net worth, whichever is HIGHER, and applies only to direct personal holdings.
en.True answer: 'Immediate family' comprises spouse and dependent children, while 'close family' comprises parents, non-dependent children, and siblings; an SSB member or any immediate/close family member (individually or collectively, directly or indirectly) must NOT be a substantial shareholder—defined as 5% (or as specified by the jurisdiction) OR 10% of the net worth of the person, WHICHEVER IS LOWER—of the institution/subsidiaries or of an organization from/to which the institution made or received significant payments in the current or immediate past financial year.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 55–57 (Defines 'immediate family (spouse and dependent children)' and 'close family (parents, non-dependent children and siblings)', and prohibits the SSB member or any immediate/close family member, individually or collectively, directly or indirectly, from being a substantial shareholder—defined as '5% or as specified by the respective jurisdiction, or 10% of the net worth of the person, whichever is lower'—of the institution/subsidiaries/associates [Par. 56] or of an organisation with significant payments in the current or immediate past financial year [Par. 57]).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 31–32, 41, and 81–82 of AAOIFI GS 20, which operational rules govern (1) decision turnaround timelines for SSB issues, (2) attendance of senior management at SSB meetings, and (3) revising previously issued Shari'ah rulings?
en.A: (1) The SSB takes unlimited time with no agreed turnaround benchmark; (2) senior management has an unconditional right to attend and vote in every SSB meeting; (3) revised rulings are kept confidential without public disclosure.
en.B: (1) Turnaround timelines are set unilaterally by the CEO; (2) only external auditors may attend SSB meetings; (3) the SSB is prohibited from ever amending a previous ruling.
en.C: (1) Every query must be answered within 24 hours regardless of complexity; (2) management is strictly barred from ever attending SSB meetings even when invited; (3) departed rulings are deleted from the website archive.
en.D: (1) At the start of the SSB term, the SSB and management must agree on a reasonable maximum timeline (once required information is provided) for deciding issues presented to the SSB; (2) the SSB chairman (or deputy chairman in his absence) is empowered to invite relevant senior management personnel to attend an SSB meeting at the initiative of the SSB or management; and (3) the SSB must adopt a specified process for changing/amending/revising earlier rulings, disseminate revisions to relevant stakeholders, and the institution must appropriately disclose whenever its SSB departs from or revises an earlier pronouncement along with the reasoning.
en.True answer: (1) At the start of the SSB term, the SSB and management must agree on a reasonable maximum timeline (once required information is provided) for deciding issues presented to the SSB; (2) the SSB chairman (or deputy chairman in his absence) is empowered to invite relevant senior management personnel to attend an SSB meeting at the initiative of the SSB or management; and (3) the SSB must adopt a specified process for changing/amending/revising earlier rulings, disseminate revisions to relevant stakeholders, and the institution must appropriately disclose whenever its SSB departs from or revises an earlier pronouncement along with the reasoning.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 31–32, Par. 41 & Par. 81–82 (Par. 31: SSB commits to and specifies a reasonable maximum timeline after required information is provided, agreed upon with management at the start of the SSB term; Par. 32: chairman—and in his absence deputy chairman—empowered to invite relevant senior management personnel to attend an SSB meeting at initiative of SSB or management; Par. 41 & 82: SSB adopts specified process for revising earlier rulings, disseminates to stakeholders, and institution appropriately discloses whenever SSB departs from or revises earlier pronouncement along with reasoning).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 10–15 of AAOIFI GS 20, how do the SSB's responsibilities regarding (1) Investment Accounts (IAs), (2) accounting treatments, (3) annual Zakah calculations, and (4) prohibited earnings operate in practice?
en.A: The SSB vets the IAs strategy/policy framework and oversees profit/loss calculation and distribution to IAHs; reviews and approves the accounting treatment of products/services for Shari'ah compliance (considering Chapter 7 of AAOIFI's Conceptual Framework); reviews and approves annual Zakah calculations on behalf of shareholders (and participatory stakeholders, if applicable, per FAS 39); and specifies the means of disposal of prohibited earnings, verifies their correct charitable use, and takes measures to systematically reduce or eliminate such Shari'ah non-compliant income in the future.
en.B: The SSB calculates daily accounting provisions directly in the general ledger, while management decides how prohibited earnings are spent without SSB verification.
en.C: Zakah calculations are reviewed solely by tax authorities, and prohibited earnings may be retained in bank equity reserves if they are below 1% of revenue.
en.D: Investment account profit-sharing ratios are determined unilaterally by the SSB without vetting the institution's IA policy framework.
en.True answer: The SSB vets the IAs strategy/policy framework and oversees profit/loss calculation and distribution to IAHs; reviews and approves the accounting treatment of products/services for Shari'ah compliance (considering Chapter 7 of AAOIFI's Conceptual Framework); reviews and approves annual Zakah calculations on behalf of shareholders (and participatory stakeholders, if applicable, per FAS 39); and specifies the means of disposal of prohibited earnings, verifies their correct charitable use, and takes measures to systematically reduce or eliminate such Shari'ah non-compliant income in the future.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 12–15 & Footnotes 10–12 (Par. 12: vet IAs strategy/policy framework and oversee profit/loss calculation and distribution to IAHs and participatory stakeholders; Par. 13 & Footnote 11: review/approve accounting treatment of products/services considering AAOIFI Conceptual Framework Ch. 7; Par. 14 & Footnote 12: review/approve annual Zakah calculations on behalf of shareholders/participatory stakeholders per FAS 39; Par. 15: specify means of disposal of prohibited earnings, verify correct charitable use, and take measures to systematically reduce or eliminate occurrence in the future).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 23–25, 48, and 68 of AAOIFI GS 20, who prepares and approves the SSB Charter (TORs), what is TCWG's annual duty regarding SSB independence and conflicts of interest, and how must the SSB interact with a Central Shari'ah Board (CSB)?
en.A: The SSB prepares and approves its own Charter without TCWG involvement; independence checks occur once every 5 years; and the SSB operates independently of any national CSB.
en.B: The SSB Charter (TORs) is prepared by the institution and approved by TCWG (covering 14 minimum items); TCWG must devise a satisfactory mechanism for an annual check of SSB members for independence and conflict of interest; and the SSB must cooperate and, where necessary, work in coordination with the Central Shari'ah Board (CSB, if one exists in the jurisdiction) to achieve standardisation and harmonisation.
en.C: The external auditor prepares the SSB Charter, annual independence checks are performed by the CEO, and coordination with the CSB is prohibited.
en.D: The SSB Charter requires shareholder ratification at every AGM, and TCWG is barred from reviewing SSB conflicts of interest.
en.True answer: The SSB Charter (TORs) is prepared by the institution and approved by TCWG (covering 14 minimum items); TCWG must devise a satisfactory mechanism for an annual check of SSB members for independence and conflict of interest; and the SSB must cooperate and, where necessary, work in coordination with the Central Shari'ah Board (CSB, if one exists in the jurisdiction) to achieve standardisation and harmonisation.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20, Par. 23–24, Par. 48 & Par. 68 (Par. 23–24: SSB charter/TORs prepared by the institution and approved by TCWG, containing at minimum 14 specified elements; Par. 68: 'TCWG of the institution shall devise a satisfactory mechanism for an annual check of SSB members for independence and conflict of interest'; Par. 48: 'The SSB shall cooperate and, where necessary, work in coordination with the CSB (if one exists in the jurisdiction) to achieve standardisation and harmonisation in the respective jurisdiction').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question:
During the 2026 annual independence check of an Islamic bank's Shari'ah Supervisory Board (SSB), TCWG uncovers the following four situations involving four different SSB members:
(1) Scholar 1's financially independent adult son (non-dependent child) owns a 6% equity stake in the Islamic bank (in a jurisdiction with no separate regulatory shareholding threshold).
(2) Scholar 2 holds a 3% equity stake in a Takaful operator that received significant payments from the Islamic bank in the immediate past financial year; that 3% stake represents 12% of Scholar 2's personal net worth.
(3) Scholar 3 obtains a home Murabaha financing facility from the Islamic bank at a special 3% preferential profit-rate discount reserved exclusively for executives and SSB members.
(4) Scholar 4 discovers a permanent, irreconcilable conflict of interest involving his family business and a major corporate client of the bank; he proposes remaining on the SSB while simply abstaining from meetings involving that client.
According to AAOIFI GS 20, which evaluation across (1)–(4) is completely accurate?
en.A: (1) Compliant—non-dependent adult children are excluded; (2) Compliant—3% is below the 5% equity threshold; (3) Compliant—preferential financing rates are standard for SSB members; (4) Compliant—abstaining resolves permanent conflicts.
en.B: (1) Non-compliant; (2) Compliant; (3) Non-compliant; (4) Compliant.
en.C: (1) Non-compliant—under Par. 55–56, non-dependent children are 'close family', and their 6% equity stake exceeds the 5% substantial shareholder threshold; (2) Non-compliant—under Par. 57, substantial shareholding is defined as 5% OR 10% of the person's net worth, WHICHEVER IS LOWER; although 3% is below 5%, 12% of Scholar 2's net worth exceeds the lower 10% net worth cap; (3) Non-compliant—under Par. 59 & Footnote 17, an SSB member may seek financing in the normal course of business ONLY with no special rates or preferential treatment; (4) Non-compliant—under Par. 64(c)–(d), abstaining is permitted only for a temporary conflict of interest, whereas if a conflict remains unresolved or is of a permanent nature, the SSB member MUST resign and the general assembly must be notified.
en.D: (1) Compliant; (2) Non-compliant; (3) Compliant; (4) Non-compliant.
en.True answer: (1) Non-compliant—under Par. 55–56, non-dependent children are 'close family', and their 6% equity stake exceeds the 5% substantial shareholder threshold; (2) Non-compliant—under Par. 57, substantial shareholding is defined as 5% OR 10% of the person's net worth, WHICHEVER IS LOWER; although 3% is below 5%, 12% of Scholar 2's net worth exceeds the lower 10% net worth cap; (3) Non-compliant—under Par. 59 & Footnote 17, an SSB member may seek financing in the normal course of business ONLY with no special rates or preferential treatment; (4) Non-compliant—under Par. 64(c)–(d), abstaining is permitted only for a temporary conflict of interest, whereas if a conflict remains unresolved or is of a permanent nature, the SSB member MUST resign and the general assembly must be notified.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20 integrates four independence rules: (1) Par. 55–56 include non-dependent children in 'close family' and prohibit substantial shareholding (≥5%) in the institution; (2) Par. 57 defines substantial shareholder in a significant payment counterparty (current or immediate past financial year) as '5% or as specified by the respective jurisdiction, or 10% of the net worth of the person, whichever is lower'—12% of net worth exceeds the 10% lower cap; (3) Par. 59 & Footnote 17 allow normal-course financing only with 'no special rates or preferential treatment'; (4) Par. 64(c)–(d) restrict abstention to temporary conflicts and mandate resignation (with notice to general assembly) when a conflict is unresolved or of a permanent nature.

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 20: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Functions and Operations
en.Question:
During calendar year 2026, an Islamic bank's 3-member Shari'ah Supervisory Board (SSB) holds exactly 4 scheduled meetings. Examine the following four operational and disclosure events:
(1) Member A attends 2 meetings in person and 1 meeting via live video conference (3 out of 4 meetings = 75%), whereas Member B attends 2 meetings personally and appoints a junior Shari'ah colleague to attend the other 2 meetings as his proxy.
(2) During the year, the SSB discovers that management is systematically executing Tawarruq commodity trades without genuine commodity possession; after the SSB notifies TCWG and recommends immediate suspension, TCWG fails to take effective action and the non-compliant trades continue—whereupon the SSB informs the Regulatory and Supervisory Authority (RSA) and reports the violations in its SSB report.
(3) On a controversial new Sukuk product approved by a 2–1 SSB majority, the dissenting scholar documents his dissent in the minutes and then publishes an op-ed in a national financial newspaper criticizing the SSB's Fatwa and questioning the bank's Shari'ah credibility.
(4) In its 2026 Annual Report, the bank publishes the SSB report (which is presented at the AGM by the SSB Chairman), discloses the past 12 months' product rulings with rationales, and discloses the total remuneration paid to SSB members in aggregate, meeting attendance records, Shari'ah non-compliance events and their resolution, and trainings attended by SSB members.
According to AAOIFI GS 20, which evaluation across (1)–(4) is completely accurate?
en.A: (1) Both Member A and Member B are compliant; (2) Non-compliant—SSBs may never escalate directly to the RSA; (3) Compliant—dissenting scholars may publicly criticize majority Fatwas; (4) Non-compliant—individual rather than aggregate remuneration must be disclosed.
en.B: (1) Both Member A and Member B violate attendance rules; (2) Compliant; (3) Compliant; (4) Non-compliant.
en.C: (1) Member A violates attendance rules (video calls do not count), while Member B is compliant; (2) Non-compliant; (3) Non-compliant; (4) Compliant.
en.D: (1) Member A IS compliant under Par. 28 (attending 3/4 = 75%, including via video or conference call, meets the ≥75% requirement), whereas Member B violates Par. 28, which explicitly stipulates that an SSB member 'cannot appoint another person to attend on his behalf'; (2) Compliant—follows Par. 21–22, which require escalating systematic non-compliance to TCWG and, if non-compliant activities continue or TCWG fail to address SSB concerns, informing the respective RSA and reporting the violations in the SSB report; (3) Non-compliant—violates Par. 73, which grants a dissenting member the right to document dissent per policy, 'but shall not criticise such Fatwa publicly or use it to inflict reputational damage on the institution or its SSB'; (4) Compliant—satisfies Par. 79–83, including AGM presentation by the SSB Chairman (Par. 80), 12-month product pronouncements with rationales (Par. 81), and annual report disclosures of total remuneration paid to SSB members in aggregate (Par. 83(d)), attendance (Par. 83(g)), non-compliance events/resolution (Par. 83(h)), and trainings attended (Par. 83(i)).
en.True answer: (1) Member A IS compliant under Par. 28 (attending 3/4 = 75%, including via video or conference call, meets the ≥75% requirement), whereas Member B violates Par. 28, which explicitly stipulates that an SSB member 'cannot appoint another person to attend on his behalf'; (2) Compliant—follows Par. 21–22, which require escalating systematic non-compliance to TCWG and, if non-compliant activities continue or TCWG fail to address SSB concerns, informing the respective RSA and reporting the violations in the SSB report; (3) Non-compliant—violates Par. 73, which grants a dissenting member the right to document dissent per policy, 'but shall not criticise such Fatwa publicly or use it to inflict reputational damage on the institution or its SSB'; (4) Compliant—satisfies Par. 79–83, including AGM presentation by the SSB Chairman (Par. 80), 12-month product pronouncements with rationales (Par. 81), and annual report disclosures of total remuneration paid to SSB members in aggregate (Par. 83(d)), attendance (Par. 83(g)), non-compliance events/resolution (Par. 83(h)), and trainings attended (Par. 83(i)).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 20 integrates four provisions: (1) Par. 28 requires ≥75% annual attendance (explicitly counting video or conference calls—so Member A's 3/4 = 75% passes) and prohibits appointing another person/proxy to attend on a member's behalf (Member B fails); (2) Par. 21–22 mandate informing the RSA and reporting violations in the SSB report when systematic non-compliance continues despite measures or when TCWG fail to address SSB concerns; (3) Par. 73 allows documenting dissent per policy but strictly prohibits criticizing the Fatwa publicly or inflicting reputational damage on the institution or its SSB; (4) Par. 79–83 require AGM presentation by an SSB member (preferably chairman), disclosure of past 12 months' pronouncements/rationales, and annual report disclosure of aggregate SSB remuneration (Par. 83(d)), attendance (Par. 83(g)), non-compliance events (Par. 83(h)), and trainings attended (Par. 83(i)).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Which of the following accurately describes which prior standards AAOIFI GS 21 supersedes (alongside GS 19), its scope, and its effective date?
en.A: GS 21 supersedes GS 5 ('Independence of Shari'ah Supervisory Board') and GS 11 ('Internal Shari'ah Audit'), applies solely to commercial banks, and became effective on 1 July 2021.
en.B: GS 21, together with GS 19 ('Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition'), supersedes GS 1 ('Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment, Composition and Report') and GS 2 ('Shari'ah Review'); applies to all IFIs (including Islamic finance windows) across all sectors, non-IFI institutions adopting AAOIFI GSs (such as Waqf and social finance institutions) insofar as practicable, and Sukuk SSBs; and is effective on or after 1 January 2026.
en.C: GS 21 supersedes AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6 ('External Shari'ah Audit') and becomes effective on 1 January 2029.
en.D: GS 21 leaves GS 2 ('Shari'ah Review') in full force and applies exclusively to sovereign Sukuk offerings.
en.True answer: GS 21, together with GS 19 ('Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment and Composition'), supersedes GS 1 ('Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment, Composition and Report') and GS 2 ('Shari'ah Review'); applies to all IFIs (including Islamic finance windows) across all sectors, non-IFI institutions adopting AAOIFI GSs (such as Waqf and social finance institutions) insofar as practicable, and Sukuk SSBs; and is effective on or after 1 January 2026.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Preface PR4, Introduction IN3–IN5, Par. 2–4 & Par. 24–25 (PR4 & Par. 25: GS 21, along with GS 19, supersedes GS 1 'Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Appointment, Composition and Report' and GS 2 'Shari'ah Review'; Par. 2–3: applies to all IFIs including Islamic finance windows across all sectors, non-IFI institutions adopting AAOIFI GSs including Waqf/social finance insofar as practicable, and Sukuk SSBs; Par. 24: effective on or after 1 January 2026).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 6–7 and 18 of AAOIFI GS 21, how is the SSB's annual review related to internal and external Shari'ah audits, and how must the SSB's annual report be published and presented?
en.A: The SSB's review is among the responsibilities of the SSB and shall in NO manner whatsoever be considered an alternative or equivalent to internal Shari'ah audit or external Shari'ah audit; the SSB must annually submit its report to shareholders (and other stakeholders, as applicable), publish it as part of the institution's annual report, and read it at the Annual General Meeting (AGM).
en.B: Completing the SSB's annual review legally exempts an Islamic bank from conducting both internal Shari'ah audit and external Shari'ah audit.
en.C: The SSB's annual report is submitted confidentially to the CEO and is neither published in the annual report nor read at the AGM.
en.D: The SSB's review replaces the external financial statement audit required under national banking laws.
en.True answer: The SSB's review is among the responsibilities of the SSB and shall in NO manner whatsoever be considered an alternative or equivalent to internal Shari'ah audit or external Shari'ah audit; the SSB must annually submit its report to shareholders (and other stakeholders, as applicable), publish it as part of the institution's annual report, and read it at the Annual General Meeting (AGM).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Par. 6–7 & Par. 18 (Par. 6: SSB shall annually submit a report to shareholders [and other stakeholders, as applicable] expressing an opinion on compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules, published as part of the annual report; Par. 7: 'The SSB's review shall be considered among the responsibilities of the SSB, and in no manner whatsoever, shall be considered as an alternative, or equivalent, to internal Shari'ah audit or external Shari'ah audit as required in line with the requirements of relevant AAOIFI GSs'; Par. 18: 'The SSB's report shall be read at the annual general meeting of the institution').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Under Paragraph 8 of AAOIFI GS 21, which five sequential stages comprise the SSB's review process?
en.A: Budget approval, branch marketing, product pricing, dividend payout, and tax filing.
en.B: External rating, sovereign guarantee, contract drafting, customer onboarding, and litigation.
en.C: (a) Planning and designing review procedures, (b) executing review procedures, (c) preparation and review of working papers, (d) documenting conclusions and reporting, and (e) quality assurance.
en.D: Idea screening, IT system coding, pilot testing, commercial launch, and post-launch sales.
en.True answer: (a) Planning and designing review procedures, (b) executing review procedures, (c) preparation and review of working papers, (d) documenting conclusions and reporting, and (e) quality assurance.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Par. 8(a)–(e) (Lists the five stages of the SSB's review: (a) planning and designing review procedures; (b) executing review procedures; (c) preparation and review of working papers; (d) documenting conclusions and reporting; and (e) quality assurance).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 14–15 of AAOIFI GS 21, what is the primary scope of the SSB's review, and which internal and external functions may the SSB utilize or rely upon to support its review process?
en.A: The SSB must personally audit 100% of daily branch cash vouchers without using any secretariat, compliance, or internal audit support.
en.B: The SSB delegates its entire review responsibility to the Chief Financial Officer and relies solely on management's verbal assurances.
en.C: The SSB may rely exclusively on external credit rating agencies and is prohibited from reviewing internal Shari'ah audit reports.
en.D: The SSB's primary scope of review relates to Shari'ah compliance in the design and structure of transactions, products, and services; to support its review of day-to-day implementation, the SSB may use the staff of the SSB secretariat (or the Shari'ah compliance department in its absence) under SSB supervision, and may rely on the work and reports of the internal Shari'ah audit function and external Shari'ah auditors (where applicable).
en.True answer: The SSB's primary scope of review relates to Shari'ah compliance in the design and structure of transactions, products, and services; to support its review of day-to-day implementation, the SSB may use the staff of the SSB secretariat (or the Shari'ah compliance department in its absence) under SSB supervision, and may rely on the work and reports of the internal Shari'ah audit function and external Shari'ah auditors (where applicable).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Par. 14–15 & Appendix B ('Functions relied upon') (Par. 14: SSB's primary scope of review relates to Shari'ah compliance in design and structure of transactions, products, and services, and it may use staff of SSB secretariat—or SCD in its absence—to carry out review procedures under SSB supervision regarding implementation; Par. 15: SSB may also use/rely on work carried out and reports issued by internal Shari'ah audit function and external Shari'ah auditors [where applicable]; Appendix B also lists external auditor's report on financial statements).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Under Paragraph 22(d)(i)–(iv) and Appendix B of AAOIFI GS 21, into which four components is the Opinion paragraph of the SSB's annual report categorized?
en.A: (i) Primary opinion, (ii) exceptions (material non-compliances that could not be resolved/settled), (iii) limitations (missing data, record-keeping deficiencies, or unreliable documents restricting the SSB's conclusion), and (iv) additional opinions (covering impermissible income/charity, Zakah, fiduciary profit/loss sharing, financial reporting, Shari'ah non-compliance risk mechanism, and Islamic window segregation).
en.B: (i) Credit rating score, (ii) tax liability calculation, (iii) executive bonus recommendations, and (iv) market share forecast.
en.C: (i) Unqualified opinion only, (ii) audit fee schedule, (iii) customer complaint log, and (iv) board attendance sheet.
en.D: (i) Primary opinion, (ii) shareholder dividend declaration, (iii) external auditor appointment, and (iv) IT security certification.
en.True answer: (i) Primary opinion, (ii) exceptions (material non-compliances that could not be resolved/settled), (iii) limitations (missing data, record-keeping deficiencies, or unreliable documents restricting the SSB's conclusion), and (iv) additional opinions (covering impermissible income/charity, Zakah, fiduciary profit/loss sharing, financial reporting, Shari'ah non-compliance risk mechanism, and Islamic window segregation).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Par. 22(d)(i)–(iv) & Appendix B (Categorizes the opinion paragraph into four parts: (i) primary opinion; (ii) exceptions [material non-compliances that could not be resolved/settled]; (iii) limitations [missing data, record-keeping deficiencies, or unreliable documents restricting SSB's conclusion]; and (iv) additional opinions [items (a)–(f) in Appendix B]).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Under Appendix B ('Additional opinions' item (a), p. 18) of AAOIFI GS 21, within what maximum timeframe must impermissible income and customer charity amounts be paid or earmarked for payment by management?
en.A: Within 30 days of receipt.
en.B: Within the next 12 months (duly segregated from the institution's own funds) for the purposes and parties approved by the SSB.
en.C: Within 5 years at the discretion of the Chief Financial Officer.
en.D: Within 3 years, after offsetting the institution's administrative overhead expenses against the impermissible income.
en.True answer: Within the next 12 months (duly segregated from the institution's own funds) for the purposes and parties approved by the SSB.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Appendix B, Additional opinions (a) (p. 18) ('any income earned from impermissible sources, along with any charity amounts received from customers / other stakeholders, have been adequately accounted for as impermissible income and have been paid / are earmarked for payment within the next 12 months (duly segregated from the institution's own funds) by the management for the purposes and the parties approved, on a timely basis, in line with the overall policy approved by the SSB').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Under Paragraph 19 of AAOIFI GS 21 and Appendix C (BC9–BC12), when the SSB identifies significant Shari'ah non-compliance issues that were resolved amicably (and hence do not impact the overall compliance opinion) or significant control weaknesses, how should they be communicated?
en.A: They must be highlighted prominently in the primary opinion paragraph of the public shareholders' report in all cases.
en.B: They are never documented or communicated to any governance organ once resolved.
en.C: They are excluded from the main shareholders' SSB report (unless considered material and necessary by the SSB) so as not to unduly harm institutional/industry reputation, and are instead communicated to Those Charged with Governance (TCWG) via a detailed SSB report covering (a) significant compliance/control weaknesses, (b) significant non-compliance issues identified and resolved amicably, and (c) significant areas requiring improvement (and communicated to the RSA where necessary).
en.D: They are reported exclusively to the external marketing agency.
en.True answer: They are excluded from the main shareholders' SSB report (unless considered material and necessary by the SSB) so as not to unduly harm institutional/industry reputation, and are instead communicated to Those Charged with Governance (TCWG) via a detailed SSB report covering (a) significant compliance/control weaknesses, (b) significant non-compliance issues identified and resolved amicably, and (c) significant areas requiring improvement (and communicated to the RSA where necessary).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Par. 19(a)–(c) & Appendix C, BC9–BC12 (Par. 19: a detailed report, when considered necessary, shall be issued to TCWG including (a) significant weaknesses identified in Shari'ah compliance and controls, (b) significant Shari'ah non-compliance issues identified but resolved amicably, hence not reported in the SSB's report, and (c) significant areas requiring improvements; BC11 explains that main shareholders' report omits these unless considered material and necessary by SSB to avoid unduly harming reputation, while communicating them to TCWG via the detailed report and to RSA where necessary).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Under Appendix B ('Inherent limitations of the SSB's function and its report', p. 20) of AAOIFI GS 21, what two inherent limitations of the SSB's function must be disclosed to readers of the SSB's annual report?
en.A: That the SSB has unlimited full-time staff to audit every branch daily, and that the SSB assumes full operational responsibility for executing contracts.
en.B: That the SSB is subordinate to executive management, and that its Fatwas are non-binding.
en.C: That the SSB reviews only tax filings, and that external auditors draft all Shari'ah Fatwas.
en.D: (a) The SSB's involvement with the institution's affairs is in an independent capacity with significant constraints regarding time and resource availability, requiring extensive reliance on various functions and reports to assess day-to-day operational compliance; and (b) the SSB's main function is limited to the design of contracts and transactions (including Fatwa, overall approval of documents and process flows), while compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules in the implementation of contracts and transactions is management's responsibility.
en.True answer: (a) The SSB's involvement with the institution's affairs is in an independent capacity with significant constraints regarding time and resource availability, requiring extensive reliance on various functions and reports to assess day-to-day operational compliance; and (b) the SSB's main function is limited to the design of contracts and transactions (including Fatwa, overall approval of documents and process flows), while compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules in the implementation of contracts and transactions is management's responsibility.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Appendix B, 'Inherent limitations of the SSB's function and its report' (p. 20) (States two inherent limitations: (a) SSB's involvement is in an independent capacity with significant time and resource constraints, requiring extensive reliance on various functions and reports in assessing day-to-day operational compliance; and (b) SSB's main function is limited to the design of contracts and transactions [Fatwa, overall approval of documents and process flows], while compliance in the implementation of contracts and transactions is management's responsibility).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Under Paragraph 22(g) and Appendix B ('Other significant reporting matters', pp. 21–22) of AAOIFI GS 21, which six matters may be judgmentally reported by the SSB to bring them to stakeholders' attention without impacting the overall compliance opinion?
en.A: (i) Key Shari'ah non-compliance risks with weak internal controls, (ii) significant instances of Shari'ah non-compliance identified and later resolved, (iii) key Shari'ah non-compliance issues in matters outside primary scope (e.g., administration, culture, and marketing), (iv) specific considerations related to segregation of funds and operations in Islamic finance windows, (v) key observations on the overall governance and control mechanism, and (vi) material differences between Shari'ah principles/rules applicable to the parent entity and those applied by subsidiaries due to different regulatory regimes.
en.B: (i) Competitor profit margins, (ii) central bank interest rate forecasts, (iii) staff vacation schedules, (iv) branch real-estate lease renewals, (v) IT software vendor prices, and (vi) shareholder dividend tax rates.
en.C: (i) Unresolved material breaches requiring an adverse opinion, (ii) missing audit evidence requiring a scope limitation, (iii) Zakah underpayments, (iv) impermissible income retained by the bank, (v) profit distribution fraud, and (vi) commingling of window funds.
en.D: GS 21 strictly prohibits including any 'Other significant reporting matters' section in the SSB's annual report.
en.True answer: (i) Key Shari'ah non-compliance risks with weak internal controls, (ii) significant instances of Shari'ah non-compliance identified and later resolved, (iii) key Shari'ah non-compliance issues in matters outside primary scope (e.g., administration, culture, and marketing), (iv) specific considerations related to segregation of funds and operations in Islamic finance windows, (v) key observations on the overall governance and control mechanism, and (vi) material differences between Shari'ah principles/rules applicable to the parent entity and those applied by subsidiaries due to different regulatory regimes.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Par. 22(g)(i)–(vi) & Appendix B (pp. 21–22) (Lists the six items under 'Other significant reporting matters' that do not impact the overall compliance opinion and are judgmentally reported by the SSB: (i) key Shari'ah non-compliance risks with weak internal controls; (ii) significant instances of Shari'ah non-compliance identified and later resolved; (iii) key Shari'ah non-compliance issues in matters not part of primary scope [e.g. administration, culture, marketing]; (iv) specific considerations related to segregation of funds/operations in Islamic finance windows; (v) key observations on overall governance and control mechanism; and (vi) material differences between Shari'ah principles/rules applicable to parent entity and subsidiaries due to different regulatory regimes).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Under Appendix B ('Report approval and authentication' and 'Dissenting opinion [if any]', p. 22) of AAOIFI GS 21, how are SSB advisors' signatures and a dissenting SSB member's authentication handled in the SSB's annual report?
en.A: SSB advisors are strictly barred from signing the report, and a dissenting member refuses to sign the main report altogether.
en.B: All SSB members sign the report (indicating unanimous approval except for any dissenting opinion), the report should preferably also be signed by the SSB advisors (if any), and a dissenting member signs the main report (indicating agreement on all other matters) while documenting his specific dissent with his name and signature in the dedicated 'Dissenting opinion' section.
en.C: Only the SSB Chairman signs the report, while dissenting opinions are submitted anonymously without names or signatures.
en.D: The CEO co-signs the SSB report alongside the external financial auditor.
en.True answer: All SSB members sign the report (indicating unanimous approval except for any dissenting opinion), the report should preferably also be signed by the SSB advisors (if any), and a dissenting member signs the main report (indicating agreement on all other matters) while documenting his specific dissent with his name and signature in the dedicated 'Dissenting opinion' section.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Appendix B, 'Report approval and authentication' & 'Dissenting opinion [if any]' (p. 22) (Shows all SSB members signing the report, includes the note '[Preferably, the report shall be signed by the SSB advisors, if any]', and provides the dissenting opinion template in which the dissenting member signs the main report to confirm agreement on all other matters while recording specific points of dissent with his name and signature).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 9–13 and 16 of AAOIFI GS 21, which requirements govern the SSB's review planning, sampling, execution, and working papers?
en.A: The SSB relies solely on unverified verbal summaries from branch managers without reviewing contracts or documenting working papers.
en.B: Sampling is prohibited in SSB reviews; the SSB must examine 100% of every retail transaction globally.
en.C: The review plan must be properly documented including sample selection criteria and sizes (considering transaction complexity and frequency) and cover all activities, products, and locations; execution includes reviewing contracts/agreements, re-ascertaining whether transactions were for SSB-authorized products, reviewing circulars/minutes/reports/policies, consulting with advisors and auditors, and discussing findings with management; and working papers must be complete, adequate, and cross-referenced to respective review procedures.
en.D: Working papers are prepared by the external marketing team and destroyed immediately after the AGM.
en.True answer: The review plan must be properly documented including sample selection criteria and sizes (considering transaction complexity and frequency) and cover all activities, products, and locations; execution includes reviewing contracts/agreements, re-ascertaining whether transactions were for SSB-authorized products, reviewing circulars/minutes/reports/policies, consulting with advisors and auditors, and discussing findings with management; and working papers must be complete, adequate, and cross-referenced to respective review procedures.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Par. 9–13 & Par. 16 (Par. 9–12: plan includes complete understanding of operations, products, locations, branches, subsidiaries, divisions; compiling Fatwas/rulings; documenting sample selection criteria and sizes considering complexity and frequency; covering all activities, products, and locations; Par. 13(a)–(f): executing review procedures including contracts, authorized products, circulars/minutes/reports, consultation with advisors/auditors, discussing findings with management; Par. 16: working papers shall be complete, adequate, and cross-referenced to respective review procedures).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Under Appendix B ('Responsibility for the subsidiaries [where applicable]', p. 20) of AAOIFI GS 21, how are consolidated subsidiaries—including those having a different SSB or operating under a different regulatory Shari'ah regime—addressed in the parent institution's SSB report?
en.A: Consolidated subsidiaries are completely excluded from the scope of the parent institution's SSB report.
en.B: The parent SSB automatically overrides the subsidiary's local regulatory Shari'ah board without reviewing compliance.
en.C: Subsidiaries operating under a different regulatory regime must be deconsolidated from the financial statements prior to issuing the SSB report.
en.D: The scope of the SSB's report includes subsidiaries consolidated in the institution's financial statements; for subsidiaries having a different SSB or operating under different regulatory Shari'ah requirements, the parent SSB performs a review of the overall state of compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules and reports any material differences arising due to a different regulatory Shari'ah requirement under 'Other significant reporting matters'.
en.True answer: The scope of the SSB's report includes subsidiaries consolidated in the institution's financial statements; for subsidiaries having a different SSB or operating under different regulatory Shari'ah requirements, the parent SSB performs a review of the overall state of compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules and reports any material differences arising due to a different regulatory Shari'ah requirement under 'Other significant reporting matters'.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Appendix B, 'Responsibility for the subsidiaries [where applicable]' (p. 20) & 'Other significant reporting matters' (p. 22) ('The scope of our report for the purpose of determining our opinion includes the subsidiary(ies) that are consolidated in the financial statements of the institution. In respect of the subsidiaries that have a different SSB or where different regulatory Shari'ah requirements are in place, for the purpose of forming our opinion, we have performed a review of the overall state of compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules. [Any material differences arising due to a different regulatory Shari'ah requirement shall be reported under the other significant matters]').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Comparing the six 'Additional opinions' required in the Opinion section of the SSB report (Appendix B, pp. 18–19) versus the six 'Other significant reporting matters' (Paragraph 22(g) & Appendix B, pp. 21–22), which structural distinction in their impact on the SSB's compliance opinion is accurate?
en.A: The 'Additional opinions' are affirmative opinion conclusions forming part of the Opinion section (covering impermissible income/charity disposal within 12 months, Zakah computation/payment, fiduciary profit/loss sharing with IAHs/Sukuk-holders, Shari'ah-compliant financial reporting, Shari'ah non-compliance risk assessment mechanism, and window fund segregation), whereas 'Other significant reporting matters' are judgmentally reported observations brought to stakeholders' attention that explicitly do NOT impact the SSB's overall opinion on the institution's compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules.
en.B: Both sections carry identical weight and automatically trigger a modified adverse opinion whenever any observation is listed.
en.C: Additional opinions apply only to conventional banks, whereas Other significant reporting matters are mandatory even when zero issues exist.
en.D: Impermissible income disposal and Zakah computation belong in 'Other significant reporting matters', whereas weak internal controls require an immediate disclaimer of opinion.
en.True answer: The 'Additional opinions' are affirmative opinion conclusions forming part of the Opinion section (covering impermissible income/charity disposal within 12 months, Zakah computation/payment, fiduciary profit/loss sharing with IAHs/Sukuk-holders, Shari'ah-compliant financial reporting, Shari'ah non-compliance risk assessment mechanism, and window fund segregation), whereas 'Other significant reporting matters' are judgmentally reported observations brought to stakeholders' attention that explicitly do NOT impact the SSB's overall opinion on the institution's compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Par. 22(d)(iv), Par. 22(g) & Appendix B (pp. 18–19, 21–22) (Appendix B 'Additional opinions' (a)–(f) are positive opinion statements forming part of the Opinion section; Appendix B 'Other significant reporting matters' explicitly states: 'In connection with this report, we believe that the following matters need to be brought to the attention of the stakeholders. However, these do not impact our overall opinion regarding the state of compliance of the institution with Shari'ah principles and rules. [To be judgmentally reported by the SSB, if applicable.]').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: In Appendix B (pp. 22–23 Note) of AAOIFI GS 21, how must the SSB modify the Primary Opinion paragraph of its report when it identifies material unresolved Shari'ah non-compliances by the institution?
en.A: The SSB issues an unqualified clean opinion in the primary paragraph and mentions the material breaches only in a private verbal briefing to the CEO.
en.B: The primary opinion paragraph is modified to state that some contracts, transactions, and dealings reviewed are NOT in compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules, lists the specific non-compliant contracts, transactions, processes, and/or investment account profit/loss allocations (each with a brief summary, list of non-compliances, and rectification/resolution status), and concludes that on account of those non-compliances, the SSB cannot provide an opinion that the institution's financial arrangements, contracts, and transactions were in compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules.
en.C: The SSB refuses to issue any annual report at all until all non-compliant contracts are settled in court.
en.D: The SSB delegates issuing the modified opinion to the institution's internal marketing department.
en.True answer: The primary opinion paragraph is modified to state that some contracts, transactions, and dealings reviewed are NOT in compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules, lists the specific non-compliant contracts, transactions, processes, and/or investment account profit/loss allocations (each with a brief summary, list of non-compliances, and rectification/resolution status), and concludes that on account of those non-compliances, the SSB cannot provide an opinion that the institution's financial arrangements, contracts, and transactions were in compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Appendix B, Note on modified primary opinion (pp. 22–23) (Provides the exact illustrative modification when material non-compliances are identified: states that some contracts/transactions/dealings are not in compliance, enumerates the specific non-compliant contracts, transactions, processes, and/or investment account profit/loss allocations [each with brief summary, list of non-compliances, rectification or resolution], and concludes: 'On account of the above non-compliances with Shari'ah principles and rules, we cannot provide an opinion as to whether or not the institution's financial arrangements, contracts and transactions... were in compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Under Appendix B ('The responsibilities of those charged with governance (TCWG) and the management', p. 21) of AAOIFI GS 21, how are Shari'ah governance and compliance responsibilities divided between TCWG and Management in the SSB's annual report?
en.A: TCWG executes daily branch Murabaha contracts, while Management independently evaluates TCWG's strategic oversight.
en.B: Both TCWG and Management are relieved of compliance responsibilities once the SSB approves the annual product catalog.
en.C: TCWG has oversight responsibility to ensure an effective and robust Shari'ah compliance environment and culture exists, establish a good governance and control framework, develop a strategy for compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules, and oversee management in implementing it; whereas Management is responsible for implementing the Shari'ah governance framework, embedding Shari'ah compliance in day-to-day functioning, ensuring arrangements/contracts/transactions and policies comply in substance and legal form, and designing, implementing, and maintaining appropriate internal controls and accounting records.
en.D: Management sets the overarching strategic governance framework, while TCWG maintains daily accounting ledgers.
en.True answer: TCWG has oversight responsibility to ensure an effective and robust Shari'ah compliance environment and culture exists, establish a good governance and control framework, develop a strategy for compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules, and oversee management in implementing it; whereas Management is responsible for implementing the Shari'ah governance framework, embedding Shari'ah compliance in day-to-day functioning, ensuring arrangements/contracts/transactions and policies comply in substance and legal form, and designing, implementing, and maintaining appropriate internal controls and accounting records.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Appendix B, 'The responsibilities of those charged with governance (TCWG) and the management' (p. 21) (Distinguishes TCWG's oversight, governance/control framework establishment, compliance strategy development, and management oversight from Management's operational implementation of the Shari'ah governance framework, day-to-day compliance in substance and legal form, and design/implementation/maintenance of internal controls and accounting records).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: In Appendix C (Basis for Conclusions, BC1–BC8) of AAOIFI GS 21, why did the Board expand the SSB's report contents and supersede GS 2 ('Shari'ah Review') by incorporating minimum SSB review procedures directly into GS 21?
en.A: To eliminate the role of internal and external Shari'ah auditors and turn the SSB into a full-time operational accounting department.
en.B: To reduce transparency in SSB reports and allow SSBs to issue opinions without performing any review procedures.
en.C: Because GS 2 was issued in 2020 and conflicted with conventional IFRS banking standards.
en.D: To update the 1997/1998 frameworks (GS 1 and GS 2) for industry evolution, clarify stakeholders' understanding of SSB responsibilities (shifting toward greater supervision alongside SSB advisors), align terminology (Shari'ah review vs. Shari'ah audit), eliminate ambiguities and overlapping functions with internal and external Shari'ah audit, and prescribe minimum SSB review procedures necessary to support the SSB's annual report.
en.True answer: To update the 1997/1998 frameworks (GS 1 and GS 2) for industry evolution, clarify stakeholders' understanding of SSB responsibilities (shifting toward greater supervision alongside SSB advisors), align terminology (Shari'ah review vs. Shari'ah audit), eliminate ambiguities and overlapping functions with internal and external Shari'ah audit, and prescribe minimum SSB review procedures necessary to support the SSB's annual report.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Appendix C, BC1–BC8 (BC1–BC5: updated the 1997 GS 1 report format to clarify SSB responsibilities to stakeholders, align with more supervision and less Fatwa issuance, leverage preferred SSB advisors, and boost stakeholder confidence; BC6–BC8: revised/superseded the 1998 GS 2 'Shari'ah Review' to align nomenclature [review vs. audit], eliminate ambiguities/overlaps with internal and external Shari'ah audit, and prescribe minimum SSB review procedures supporting the SSB's report).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Under Paragraph 22(d)(ii)–(iii) and Appendix B ('Exceptions' and 'Limitations', p. 18) of AAOIFI GS 21, how are 'Exceptions' distinguished from 'Limitations' in the Opinion section of the SSB's annual report?
en.A: 'Exceptions' report instances of material non-compliances with Shari'ah principles and rules that could NOT be resolved or settled, whereas 'Limitations' report constraints (such as missing data, record-keeping deficiencies, or missing/unreliable documents) that restrict the ability of the SSB to conclude with reasonable certainty about the state of compliance.
en.B: 'Exceptions' report minor resolved administrative typos, whereas 'Limitations' list all products approved by the SSB during the year.
en.C: 'Exceptions' and 'Limitations' are identical terms referring solely to regulatory capital shortfalls.
en.D: Neither 'Exceptions' nor 'Limitations' may ever be disclosed in the SSB's published report.
en.True answer: 'Exceptions' report instances of material non-compliances with Shari'ah principles and rules that could NOT be resolved or settled, whereas 'Limitations' report constraints (such as missing data, record-keeping deficiencies, or missing/unreliable documents) that restrict the ability of the SSB to conclude with reasonable certainty about the state of compliance.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Par. 22(d)(ii)–(iii) & Appendix B (p. 18) (Appendix B defines 'Exceptions' as 'instances of material non-compliances with Shari'ah principles and rules, which could not be resolved / settled', and 'Limitations' as 'limitations or constraints, if any, e.g., missing data, record-keeping deficiencies or missing or unreliable documents, that restrict the ability of the SSB to conclude with reasonable certainty about the state of compliance of the institution with Shari'ah principles and rules').

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 16–21 of AAOIFI GS 21, which requirements govern (1) SSB working papers, (2) quality control over the SSB's review, and (3) presenting the SSB report at the Annual General Meeting?
en.A: (1) Working papers are optional if no breaches are found; (2) quality control is conducted by the bank's marketing department; (3) the SSB report is mailed only to institutional shareholders 6 months after the AGM.
en.B: (1) Execution of review procedures must be documented in working papers that are complete, adequate, and cross-referenced to the respective review procedures; (2) the SSB must implement adequate quality control policies and procedures—including review of all working papers and additional discussions with management if required—to ensure the review complied with GS 21; and (3) the SSB's report must be published as part of the annual report and read at the Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the institution.
en.C: (1) Working papers need not be cross-referenced; (2) quality assurance is waived for institutions with fewer than 5 branches; (3) the CEO reads a summarized version of the SSB report at the AGM.
en.D: (1) Only external auditors maintain working papers; (2) quality control applies only once every 3 years; (3) reading the SSB report at the AGM is optional.
en.True answer: (1) Execution of review procedures must be documented in working papers that are complete, adequate, and cross-referenced to the respective review procedures; (2) the SSB must implement adequate quality control policies and procedures—including review of all working papers and additional discussions with management if required—to ensure the review complied with GS 21; and (3) the SSB's report must be published as part of the annual report and read at the Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the institution.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21, Par. 6, Par. 16, Par. 18 & Par. 20–21 (Par. 16: working papers shall be complete, adequate, and cross-referenced to respective review procedures; Par. 20–21: SSB shall implement adequate quality control policies and procedures, including review of all working papers and additional discussions with management if required; Par. 6 & Par. 18: SSB report published as part of annual report and read at the annual general meeting of the institution).

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question:
During the 2026 annual review cycle of Al-Ihsan Islamic Bank (which operates a consolidated foreign subsidiary in a jurisdiction with different regulatory Shari'ah requirements, as well as a domestic Islamic finance window), examine the following four actions by the SSB and management:
(1) Management proposes cancelling the annual internal Shari'ah audit and external Shari'ah audit for 2026, arguing that the SSB's annual review under GS 21 serves as a full statutory equivalent.
(2) During the year, the SSB identifies a significant Shari'ah non-compliance in a batch of Murabaha transactions that management promptly rectifies and resolves amicably in full accordance with SSB instructions; to avoid unnecessary reputational alarm among retail depositors, the SSB omits this resolved incident from the main shareholders' report and instead communicates it in a detailed report to Those Charged with Governance (TCWG).
(3) For the consolidated foreign subsidiary operating under different regulatory Shari'ah requirements, the parent SSB reviews the overall state of compliance and reports the material differences arising from the foreign regulatory regime under 'Other significant reporting matters' in its report.
(4) Impermissible late-payment income collected during 2026 is held in the bank's general operating cash account with a management plan to disburse it to charity over the next 36 months.
According to AAOIFI GS 21, which evaluation across (1)–(4) is completely accurate?
en.A: (1) Compliant—GS 21 reviews replace internal and external Shari'ah audits; (2) Non-compliant—all resolved issues must be placed in the main shareholders' report; (3) Non-compliant—foreign subsidiaries are excluded; (4) Compliant—36 months is allowed for charity disbursement.
en.B: (1) Non-compliant; (2) Non-compliant; (3) Compliant; (4) Compliant.
en.C: (1) Non-compliant—Par. 7 explicitly states that the SSB's review shall in NO manner whatsoever be considered an alternative or equivalent to internal Shari'ah audit or external Shari'ah audit; (2) Compliant—follows Par. 19(b) & Appendix C (BC9–BC12), under which significant Shari'ah non-compliance issues identified and resolved amicably (not impacting the overall opinion) are excluded from the main shareholders' report (unless considered material and necessary by the SSB) and communicated to TCWG via the detailed SSB report; (3) Compliant—follows Appendix B ('Responsibility for the subsidiaries', p. 20 & 'Other significant reporting matters', p. 22), requiring review of consolidated subsidiaries' overall compliance and reporting material differences due to a different regulatory regime under 'Other significant reporting matters'; (4) Non-compliant—violates Appendix B ('Additional opinions' (a), p. 18), which requires impermissible income to be duly segregated from the institution's own funds and paid or earmarked for payment within the next 12 months (not 36 months).
en.D: (1) Compliant; (2) Compliant; (3) Non-compliant; (4) Non-compliant.
en.True answer: (1) Non-compliant—Par. 7 explicitly states that the SSB's review shall in NO manner whatsoever be considered an alternative or equivalent to internal Shari'ah audit or external Shari'ah audit; (2) Compliant—follows Par. 19(b) & Appendix C (BC9–BC12), under which significant Shari'ah non-compliance issues identified and resolved amicably (not impacting the overall opinion) are excluded from the main shareholders' report (unless considered material and necessary by the SSB) and communicated to TCWG via the detailed SSB report; (3) Compliant—follows Appendix B ('Responsibility for the subsidiaries', p. 20 & 'Other significant reporting matters', p. 22), requiring review of consolidated subsidiaries' overall compliance and reporting material differences due to a different regulatory regime under 'Other significant reporting matters'; (4) Non-compliant—violates Appendix B ('Additional opinions' (a), p. 18), which requires impermissible income to be duly segregated from the institution's own funds and paid or earmarked for payment within the next 12 months (not 36 months).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI GS 21 integrates four provisions: (1) Par. 7 strictly prohibits treating the SSB's review as an alternative or equivalent to internal Shari'ah audit or external Shari'ah audit; (2) Par. 19(b) & Appendix C BC9–BC12 allow excluding significant amicably resolved non-compliance issues from the main shareholders' report (unless considered material and necessary by SSB) and reporting them to TCWG via the detailed SSB report; (3) Appendix B (p. 20 & p. 22) includes consolidated subsidiaries in scope and requires reporting material differences arising due to a different regulatory Shari'ah regime under 'Other significant reporting matters'; (4) Appendix B Additional opinions (a) (p. 18) requires impermissible income/charity to be segregated from the institution's own funds and paid/earmarked for payment within the next 12 months.

en.Theme: AAOIFI GS 21: Shari'ah Supervisory Board: Review and Report
en.Question:
In preparing its 2026 annual report to shareholders, the 3-member Shari'ah Supervisory Board (SSB) of Barakah Islamic Bank—assisted by 1 non-voting SSB advisor—faces four reporting and authentication situations:
(1) During the review, the SSB discovers material unresolved Shari'ah non-compliances in a major Mudaraba investment pool's profit-allocation formula that management refused to rectify; the SSB still issues an unmodified clean primary opinion while listing the unresolved Mudaraba breach only in 'Other significant reporting matters'.
(2) One of the three SSB scholars disagrees with the majority on a specific Sukuk structuring ruling in the report; he refuses to sign the main SSB report altogether and demands that his dissenting opinion be published anonymously without his name or signature.
(3) The SSB advisor who assisted the board signs the report alongside the three SSB members, and the report specifies both the date and place of issuance.
(4) At the Annual General Meeting (AGM), the SSB report is published in the annual report, read at the AGM, and presented to shareholders by the SSB Chairman.
According to AAOIFI GS 21, which evaluation across (1)–(4) is completely accurate?
