en.C: Bank Y requires zero transaction testing on a test basis because its internal Shari'ah review was clean.
en.D: Bank X requires 100% population testing of every voucher because ASIFI No. 4 prohibits test-basis sampling when internal controls are weak.
en.True answer: Under Paragraph 14, transaction verification is carried out on a test basis, and the nature and extent of testing is subject to the individual circumstances of each IFI and must be determined by the auditor after careful consideration of those circumstances (resulting in more extensive, substantive test coverage for Bank X than for Bank Y).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 4, Par. 14 ('The auditor shall also verify that the transactions entered into by the IFI are consistent with the fatwas, rulings and guidelines of the SSB. This verification shall be carried out by the auditor on a test basis. The nature and extent of the testing is subject to the individual circumstances of the IFI and shall be determined by the auditor after careful consideration of these circumstances').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 04: Testing for Compliance with Shari'a Rules
en.Question: In an Islamic bank, the internal audit department performs Shari'ah compliance testing as part of its internal work, while an external audit firm performs the statutory financial statement audit. Under Paragraphs 2, 3, 5, and 15 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 4, how are the roles of internal audit and the external auditor distinguished?
en.A: ASIFI No. 4 governs both internal audit and external audit identically, allowing the external auditor to adopt internal audit's conclusions without independent testing.
en.B: For purposes of ASIFI No. 4, the term 'auditor' refers to the external auditor ONLY and does NOT apply to any internal audit function (Par. 2); the external auditor reviews internal audit and internal Shari'a review findings to assess their impact on the nature, timing, or extent of his own examination (Par. 15), while retaining sole responsibility for accumulating sufficient appropriate audit evidence providing reasonable assurance that the financial statements are free of material misstatement and that examined transactions comply with SSB-determined Shari'a Rules and Principles (Par. 3 & 5).
en.C: Internal audit expresses the statutory audit opinion on the financial statements, while the external auditor reports only to the Head of Internal Audit.
en.D: External auditors are prohibited from reading internal audit reports in order to preserve independence.
en.True answer: For purposes of ASIFI No. 4, the term 'auditor' refers to the external auditor ONLY and does NOT apply to any internal audit function (Par. 2); the external auditor reviews internal audit and internal Shari'a review findings to assess their impact on the nature, timing, or extent of his own examination (Par. 15), while retaining sole responsibility for accumulating sufficient appropriate audit evidence providing reasonable assurance that the financial statements are free of material misstatement and that examined transactions comply with SSB-determined Shari'a Rules and Principles (Par. 3 & 5).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 4, Par. 2, Par. 3, Par. 5 & Par. 15 (Par. 2: 'auditor' refers to external auditor only and shall not apply to any internal audit function associated with the IFI; Par. 3 & 5: external auditor obtains sufficient appropriate audit evidence for reasonable assurance and forms/expresses opinion on financial statements; Par. 15: external auditor reviews findings of internal reviews by management, internal audit, and internal Shari'a review [GSIFI No. 3] to determine whether they affect the nature, timing, or extent of his own examination).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 04: Testing for Compliance with Shari'a Rules
en.Question:
During the 2025 statutory financial statement audit of Al-Quds Islamic Bank, the external audit engagement team performs four actions:
(1) The audit team reviews the bank's product development procedures and discovers that a modified Wakalah investment product was launched in June 2025 after review by management and internal audit, but without any review or approval by the Shari'ah Supervisory Board (SSB) in its minutes or reports.
(2) When testing a sample of Istisna contracts, the audit manager argues that an SSB fatwa allowing a specific milestone-billing clause contradicts the audit manager's own reading of classical Fiqh, and proposes issuing a qualified opinion on the ground that the SSB fatwa itself is Islamically invalid.
(3) The audit team reviews the findings of the bank's internal Shari'ah review (conducted under GSIFI No. 3) and internal audit, noting significant branch-level deviations in Murabaha possession documents, and consequently expands the extent and shifts the timing of its external substantive testing.
(4) Before the SSB issues its final annual report, the external auditor provides the SSB with his draft audit report and Shari'ah compliance conclusions, and waits to release his final audit report until after taking note of the SSB's draft report.
According to AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 4, which evaluation across (1)–(4) is completely accurate?
en.A: (1) Product launch process is compliant; (2) Audit manager is right to overrule the SSB fatwa; (3) Non-compliant—internal Shari'ah reviews cannot alter external audit extent; (4) Non-compliant—auditor must publish before seeing the SSB draft report.
en.B: (1) Compliant; (2) Non-compliant; (3) Non-compliant; (4) Compliant.
en.C: (1) Deficient product process—violates Par. 11 & Par. 13, which require that new or modified products undergo reviews by management, internal audit, AND the SSB (per GSIFI No. 2) and require the auditor to consider the effect of unreviewed/non-compliant products on his work; (2) Audit manager is wrong—violates Par. 6–8, under which the SSB holds responsibility to interpret Shari'a Rules and Principles, the auditor is not expected to provide interpretations, and the SSB's fatwas/rulings form the authoritative basis for concluding on Shari'a compliance; (3) Compliant—follows Par. 15, which requires reviewing findings of management, internal audit, and internal Shari'a review (GSIFI No. 3) and adjusting the nature, timing, or extent of external audit work accordingly; (4) Compliant—follows Par. 16 & Par. 17, which mandate making the auditor's draft report/conclusions available to the SSB prior to issuance of the SSB's final report and releasing the auditor's report only after taking note of the SSB's draft report.
en.D: (1) Deficient; (2) Compliant; (3) Compliant; (4) Non-compliant.
en.True answer: (1) Deficient product process—violates Par. 11 & Par. 13, which require that new or modified products undergo reviews by management, internal audit, AND the SSB (per GSIFI No. 2) and require the auditor to consider the effect of unreviewed/non-compliant products on his work; (2) Audit manager is wrong—violates Par. 6–8, under which the SSB holds responsibility to interpret Shari'a Rules and Principles, the auditor is not expected to provide interpretations, and the SSB's fatwas/rulings form the authoritative basis for concluding on Shari'a compliance; (3) Compliant—follows Par. 15, which requires reviewing findings of management, internal audit, and internal Shari'a review (GSIFI No. 3) and adjusting the nature, timing, or extent of external audit work accordingly; (4) Compliant—follows Par. 16 & Par. 17, which mandate making the auditor's draft report/conclusions available to the SSB prior to issuance of the SSB's final report and releasing the auditor's report only after taking note of the SSB's draft report.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 4 integrates four provisions: (1) Par. 11 & Par. 13 require verifying that new or modified products undergo management, internal audit, AND SSB review under GSIFI No. 2 and assessing the effect on the audit; (2) Par. 6–8 establish that interpreting Shari'a lies with the SSB, the auditor is not expected to interpret Shari'a rules, and SSB fatwas/rulings form the basis for concluding on compliance; (3) Par. 15 directs reviewing findings of management, internal audit, and internal Shari'a review (GSIFI No. 3) and evaluating their effect on nature, timing, or extent of external audit work; (4) Par. 16 & Par. 17 mandate providing the auditor's draft report/conclusions to the SSB before the SSB's final report and releasing the auditor's report only after taking note of the SSB's draft report.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 04: Testing for Compliance with Shari'a Rules
en.Question:
At the conclusion of the 2025 audit of Noor Islamic Bank, examine the following four governance and reporting events:
(1) The bank's internal audit department claims that because it performs internal Shari'ah compliance testing, it is governed directly by ASIFI No. 4 and its head should co-sign the external auditor's report.
(2) The SSB issues its draft report to the external auditor indicating material non-compliance with Shari'a Rules and Principles in the bank's Mudaraba profit-distribution pool; based on the SSB's draft report, the external auditor decides to modify his draft audit report, adds a modification, and includes an adequate explanation of the nature of and reasons for the modification.
(3) During the audit, the external auditor declined management's request to formally assess and certify in the audit report that the three SSB scholars possess adequate Fiqh qualifications.
(4) Management asserts that because the external auditor tested Shari'ah compliance on a test basis and issued an audit report, management is no longer responsible for ensuring the bank's activities comply with SSB-determined Shari'a Rules and Principles.
According to AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 4, which evaluation across (1)–(4) is completely accurate?
en.A: (1) Internal audit is right; (2) Non-compliant—auditors never modify reports based on the SSB's draft report; (3) Non-compliant—auditors must certify SSB competence; (4) Management is right.
en.B: (1) Internal audit is wrong; (2) Non-compliant; (3) Non-compliant; (4) Management is right.
en.C: (1) Internal audit is right; (2) Compliant; (3) Compliant; (4) Management is right.
en.D: (1) Internal audit is wrong—under Par. 2, for purposes of ASIFI No. 4, the term 'auditor' refers to the external auditor ONLY and shall NOT apply to any internal audit function associated with the IFI; (2) Compliant—follows Par. 16, which requires that if the SSB's draft report indicates compliance with Shari'a Rules and Principles is lacking and the auditor decides based on it to modify his draft report, he must provide an adequate explanation of the nature of and reasons for the modification; (3) Compliant—follows Par. 10, which explicitly states that the auditor shall have NO responsibility for assessing the competence of the members of the SSB; (4) Management is wrong—violates Par. 5, which establishes that while the auditor is responsible for forming and expressing an opinion on the financial statements, the management of the IFI is responsible for ensuring that the financial statements and the IFI's activities comply with Shari'a Rules and Principles as determined by the SSB.
en.True answer: (1) Internal audit is wrong—under Par. 2, for purposes of ASIFI No. 4, the term 'auditor' refers to the external auditor ONLY and shall NOT apply to any internal audit function associated with the IFI; (2) Compliant—follows Par. 16, which requires that if the SSB's draft report indicates compliance with Shari'a Rules and Principles is lacking and the auditor decides based on it to modify his draft report, he must provide an adequate explanation of the nature of and reasons for the modification; (3) Compliant—follows Par. 10, which explicitly states that the auditor shall have NO responsibility for assessing the competence of the members of the SSB; (4) Management is wrong—violates Par. 5, which establishes that while the auditor is responsible for forming and expressing an opinion on the financial statements, the management of the IFI is responsible for ensuring that the financial statements and the IFI's activities comply with Shari'a Rules and Principles as determined by the SSB.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 4 integrates four provisions: (1) Par. 2 defines 'auditor' as the external auditor only and excludes any internal audit function associated with the IFI; (2) Par. 16 requires providing an adequate explanation of the nature of and reasons for any modification made to the auditor's draft report based on the SSB's draft report indicating lack of Shari'a compliance; (3) Par. 10 confirms the auditor has no responsibility for assessing the competence of SSB members; (4) Par. 5 establishes that management of the IFI is responsible for ensuring that the financial statements and the IFI's activities comply with Shari'a Rules and Principles as determined by the SSB.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Which of the following accurately describes the purpose, relationship with IFAC standards, adoption date, and effective date of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5 ('Auditor's Responsibility to Consider Fraud and Error in an Audit of Financial Statements')?
en.A: It supersedes all IFAC auditing standards completely, applies only to non-financial corporations, was adopted in May 1996, and became effective on 1 January 1998.
en.B: It establishes guidance on the auditor's responsibility when considering the risk of fraud and error in an audit of financial statements of an IFI, complementing standards issued by the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC) by fulfilling specific additional requirements relating to IFIs; it was adopted in Bahrain on 3 May 2003 (3 Rabi' I, 1424 A.H.) and became effective for financial periods beginning 1 Muharram 1425 A.H. or 1 January 2004 A.D.
en.C: It shifts primary responsibility for preventing and detecting internal fraud from IFI management to the external auditor, and became effective on 1 January 2026.
en.D: It applies exclusively to internal Shari'ah audit departments and omits any guidance on management representations.
en.True answer: It establishes guidance on the auditor's responsibility when considering the risk of fraud and error in an audit of financial statements of an IFI, complementing standards issued by the International Federation of Accountants (IFAC) by fulfilling specific additional requirements relating to IFIs; it was adopted in Bahrain on 3 May 2003 (3 Rabi' I, 1424 A.H.) and became effective for financial periods beginning 1 Muharram 1425 A.H. or 1 January 2004 A.D.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 1–3, Par. 21 & Adoption of the Standard (Par. 1–3: establishes guidance on the auditor's responsibility when considering the risk of fraud and error in an audit of financial statements of an IFI, read in conjunction with all ASIFIs, and complements standards issued by IFAC by fulfilling specific additional requirements relating to IFIs; Par. 21: effective for financial periods beginning 1 Muharram 1425 A.H. or 1 January 2004 A.D.; Adoption: adopted by the Accounting and Auditing Standards Board in meeting No. 25 held in Bahrain on 3 Rabi' I, 1424 A.H. / 3 May 2003 A.D.).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Under Paragraph 4(a)–(c) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, how is 'Error' defined, and which three categories of unintentional misstatements are explicitly listed?
en.A: An unintentional misstatement in financial statements, including the omission of an amount or a disclosure, such as: (a) an incorrect accounting estimate as stated in Financial Accounting Standards arising from oversight or misunderstanding of facts; (b) a mistake in the application of accounting principles and standards as stated in AAOIFI's Financial Accounting Standards relating to recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure; and (c) an incorrect application and oversight of Shari'a rules and principles.
en.B: An intentional act by management involving deception to misallocate profits between the IFI and investment accountholders.
en.C: Any deliberate concealment of non-Shari'ah-compliant activities from the Shari'ah Supervisory Board.
en.D: A deliberate falsification of supplier invoices to inflate Murabaha asset balances.
en.True answer: An unintentional misstatement in financial statements, including the omission of an amount or a disclosure, such as: (a) an incorrect accounting estimate as stated in Financial Accounting Standards arising from oversight or misunderstanding of facts; (b) a mistake in the application of accounting principles and standards as stated in AAOIFI's Financial Accounting Standards relating to recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure; and (c) an incorrect application and oversight of Shari'a rules and principles.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 4(a)–(c) ('Error refers to an unintentional misstatement in financial statements, including the omission of an amount or a disclosure, such as: (a) An incorrect accounting estimate as stated in Financial Accounting Standards arising from oversight or misunderstanding of facts; (b) A mistake in the application of accounting principles and standards as stated in AAOIFI's Financial Accounting Standards relating to recognition, measurement, presentation and disclosure; (c) An incorrect application and oversight of Shari'a rules and principles').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Under Paragraph 5(a)–(f) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, how is 'Fraud' defined, and which IFI-specific examples of fraud are explicitly enumerated?
en.A: An unintentional arithmetic mistake by a junior accounting clerk when totaling daily cash receipts.
en.B: Any legitimate difference of opinion between two classical schools of Islamic jurisprudence on a novel contract.
en.C: An intentional act by one or more individuals among management, those charged with governance, employees, or third parties involving the use of deception to obtain an unjust or illegal advantage, including: (a) breach of contracts between the IFI, investors, and third parties such as misappropriation of funds of investment accountholders (IAH) and policyholders (PA); (b) intentional misallocation of profits between the IFI and IAH/PA; (c) IFI's misuse of IAH and PA funds including violation of contracts; (d) intentional non-disclosure by management of activities and relevant information to the SSB, auditors, investors, and shareholders; (e) intentional, consistent violation and misinterpretation of AAOIFI Shari'a standards and the SSB's fatwas, rulings, and guidelines; and (f) intentional manipulation of documents and records to misrepresent financial statements.
en.D: An honest oversight in estimating Zakah allowances due to misunderstanding of facts.
en.True answer: An intentional act by one or more individuals among management, those charged with governance, employees, or third parties involving the use of deception to obtain an unjust or illegal advantage, including: (a) breach of contracts between the IFI, investors, and third parties such as misappropriation of funds of investment accountholders (IAH) and policyholders (PA); (b) intentional misallocation of profits between the IFI and IAH/PA; (c) IFI's misuse of IAH and PA funds including violation of contracts; (d) intentional non-disclosure by management of activities and relevant information to the SSB, auditors, investors, and shareholders; (e) intentional, consistent violation and misinterpretation of AAOIFI Shari'a standards and the SSB's fatwas, rulings, and guidelines; and (f) intentional manipulation of documents and records to misrepresent financial statements.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 5(a)–(f) (Defines fraud as an intentional act by management, TCWG, employees, or third parties involving deception to obtain an unjust or illegal advantage, listing 6 IFI-specific cases: (a) breach of contracts / misappropriation of IAH and PA funds; (b) intentional misallocation of profits between IFI and IAH/PA; (c) misuse of IAH and PA funds including contract violation; (d) intentional non-disclosure by management of activities/relevant info to SSB, auditors, investors, and shareholders; (e) intentional, consistent violation and misinterpretation of AAOIFI Shari'a standards and SSB fatwas/rulings/guidelines; (f) intentional manipulation of documents and records to misrepresent financial statements).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 6–7 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, when is an external auditor NOT responsible for fraud and error versus when IS the external auditor held responsible for negligence and misconduct?
en.A: The external auditor is strictly liable for preventing all fraud in the institution, even when reasonable audit planning and procedures were performed.
en.B: The external auditor is never held liable under any circumstances, even when he discovers material fraud and chooses not to report it.
en.C: The external auditor is responsible for preventing minor errors, whereas management is responsible for reporting detected fraud to regulators.
en.D: The fact that an audit is carried out may act as a deterrent, but the auditor is NOT and cannot be held responsible for the prevention of fraud and error (Par. 6); HOWEVER, the auditor SHALL be held responsible for negligence and misconduct if reasonable efforts are not seen to have been made in designing and planning the audit in order to detect fraud and error AND/OR it is shown that the auditor was aware of material fraud and error and did not take any necessary action to report it to the appropriate authority (Par. 7).
en.True answer: The fact that an audit is carried out may act as a deterrent, but the auditor is NOT and cannot be held responsible for the prevention of fraud and error (Par. 6); HOWEVER, the auditor SHALL be held responsible for negligence and misconduct if reasonable efforts are not seen to have been made in designing and planning the audit in order to detect fraud and error AND/OR it is shown that the auditor was aware of material fraud and error and did not take any necessary action to report it to the appropriate authority (Par. 7).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 6 & Par. 7 (Par. 6: 'The fact that an audit is carried out may act as a deterrent, but the auditor is not and cannot be held responsible for the prevention of fraud and error'; Par. 7: 'However, the auditor shall be held responsible for negligence and misconduct if reasonable efforts are not seen to have been made in designing and planning the audit in order to detect fraud and error and/or it is shown that the auditor was aware of material fraud and error and did not take any necessary action to report it to the appropriate authority').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 8–9 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, may an external auditor rely solely on the Shari'ah Supervisory Board's report to conclude on management's compliance with Shari'ah rules, and is the auditor expected to act as a forensic document authentication expert?
en.A: No to both: the Shari'ah supervisory board's report shall NOT be the sole basis for the auditor's conclusion on management's compliance with Shari'a rules and principles (Par. 8); and unless the audit reveals evidence to the contrary, the auditor is entitled to accept records and documents as genuine, as an audit rarely contemplates authentication of documentation nor are auditors trained as or expected to be experts in such authentication (Par. 9).
en.B: Yes to both: the SSB report is the sole basis required for concluding on Shari'ah compliance, and auditors must subject every document to forensic laboratory authentication.
en.C: The SSB report is the sole basis required, while document authentication is prohibited.
en.D: The auditor cannot rely on the SSB report at all, and every auditor must hold a forensic handwriting certification.
en.True answer: No to both: the Shari'ah supervisory board's report shall NOT be the sole basis for the auditor's conclusion on management's compliance with Shari'a rules and principles (Par. 8); and unless the audit reveals evidence to the contrary, the auditor is entitled to accept records and documents as genuine, as an audit rarely contemplates authentication of documentation nor are auditors trained as or expected to be experts in such authentication (Par. 9).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 8 & Par. 9 (Par. 8: 'In addition, the Shari'a supervisory board's report shall not be the sole basis for the auditor's conclusion on the management's compliance with Shari'a rules and principles'; Par. 9: 'With due consideration to the above, unless the audit reveals evidence to the contrary, the auditor is entitled to accept records and documents as genuine. Accordingly, an audit performed in accordance with ASIFI and other relevant standards issued by the IFAC rarely contemplates authentication of documentation, nor are auditors trained as, or expected to be, experts in such authentication').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 10–12 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, which specific stakeholder funds must the auditor consider when assessing fraud and error misstatement risk in planning, and from whom must the auditor inquire about suspected, discovered, investigated, or reported fraud and errors?
en.A: Only shareholders' common equity funds; inquiries are made solely to the Chief Executive Officer.
en.B: In planning the audit, the auditor must assess the risk that fraud and error may cause the financial statements as well as the assets, balances, and income of the funds of investment accountholders (IAH) and policyholders (PA) to contain material misstatement (Par. 10); and the auditor must inquire whether management, the audit committee, OR members of the Shari'a supervisory board are aware of any fraud and errors that have been suspected, discovered, investigated, and/or reported (Par. 12).
en.C: Only government tax reserve accounts; inquiries are restricted exclusively to external legal counsel.
en.D: Only head-office fixed assets; inquiries to members of the Shari'ah Supervisory Board are prohibited.
en.True answer: In planning the audit, the auditor must assess the risk that fraud and error may cause the financial statements as well as the assets, balances, and income of the funds of investment accountholders (IAH) and policyholders (PA) to contain material misstatement (Par. 10); and the auditor must inquire whether management, the audit committee, OR members of the Shari'a supervisory board are aware of any fraud and errors that have been suspected, discovered, investigated, and/or reported (Par. 12).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 10 & Par. 12 (Par. 10: 'In planning the audit, the auditor shall assess the risk that fraud and error may cause to the financial statements as well as the assets, balances and income of the funds of IAH/PA, to contain material misstatement'; Par. 12: 'The auditor shall inquire whether management, audit committee or members of the Shari'a supervisory board are aware of any fraud and errors that have been suspected, discovered, investigated and/or reported').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Under Paragraph 13 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, when the auditor concludes that the financial statements are materially misstated as a result of fraud and error, what reporting decision must the auditor make?
en.A: Issue an unqualified clean opinion with a private verbal reminder to the accounting clerk.
en.B: Automatically dissolve the bank's Shari'ah Supervisory Board.
en.C: Consider the implications for the audit and decide whether the audit shall be continued with the issuance of a qualified audit opinion or possible disclaimer in the audit report as stated in ASIFI No. 3, paragraphs (27–46).
en.D: Adjust the financial statement figures unilaterally without consulting management or modifying the report.
en.True answer: Consider the implications for the audit and decide whether the audit shall be continued with the issuance of a qualified audit opinion or possible disclaimer in the audit report as stated in ASIFI No. 3, paragraphs (27–46).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 13 ('When the auditor concludes that the financial statements are materially misstated as a result of fraud and error, the auditor shall consider the implications for the audit. The auditor shall then decide whether the audit shall be continued with the issuance of a qualified audit opinion or possible disclaimer in the audit report as stated in ASIFI No. (3), paragraphs (27-46)').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 14–16 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, which documentation duties apply to the auditor regarding fraud/error risk factors, management responses, and discussions held with Shari'ah Supervisory Board (SSB) members?
en.A: Only final audit fees need to be documented; discussions with SSB members are kept strictly off the record.
en.B: Fraud risk factors are documented only if actual criminal convictions occur during the audit year.
en.C: Working papers need only record management's oral assurances without stating the auditor's reasoning or conclusions.
en.D: The auditor must document (1) fraud and error risk factors identified during assessment (and any additional factors identified during audit performance) along with the auditor's response to them (Par. 14), (2) important evidence supporting the opinion, the auditor's reasoning and conclusions on all significant judgement matters, and management's response considered appropriate by the auditor (Par. 15), and (3) discussions held with SSB members, with conclusions supported by AAOIFI's Shari'a standards and the SSB's fatwas, rulings, and guidelines (Par. 16).
en.True answer: The auditor must document (1) fraud and error risk factors identified during assessment (and any additional factors identified during audit performance) along with the auditor's response to them (Par. 14), (2) important evidence supporting the opinion, the auditor's reasoning and conclusions on all significant judgement matters, and management's response considered appropriate by the auditor (Par. 15), and (3) discussions held with SSB members, with conclusions supported by AAOIFI's Shari'a standards and the SSB's fatwas, rulings, and guidelines (Par. 16).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 14–16 (Par. 14: document fraud and error risk factors identified during assessment and during performance of audit, plus auditor's response; Par. 15: document important evidence supporting opinion, auditor's reasoning and conclusion on significant judgement matters, and management's response considered appropriate; Par. 16: 'The auditor shall document discussions held with the Shari'a supervisory board members, and conclusions of such discussions shall be supported by AAOIFI's Shari'a standards and the fatwas, rulings and guidelines issued by the Shari'a supervisory board').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 17–19 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, how are responsibilities for fraud/error prevention and detection divided between IFI Management and Those in Charge of Governance (Corporate Governance Body), and what is the auditor's duty regarding internal controls?
en.A: Primary responsibility for preventing and detecting fraud and error rests with those charged with corporate governance and management of the IFI and IAH/PA funds: management sets proper procedures, creates/maintains a culture of honesty and high ethics compatible with AAOIFI's Code of Ethics for Employees of IFIs, and establishes controls (including controls over applying Shari'a rules/principles to all activities); those in charge of governance ensure through oversight of management the integrity of accounting/financial reporting systems and appropriate controls; and the auditor must assess that management has developed an appropriate system of internal control that includes compliance with Shari'a rules and principles.
en.B: The external auditor sets internal bank procedures and enforces employee ethics, while management is exempt from internal control duties.
en.C: Those in charge of governance manage daily branch cash tellers directly, while management oversees the board of directors.
en.D: Internal controls need only cover conventional accounting accuracy and exclude compliance with Shari'a rules and principles.
en.True answer: Primary responsibility for preventing and detecting fraud and error rests with those charged with corporate governance and management of the IFI and IAH/PA funds: management sets proper procedures, creates/maintains a culture of honesty and high ethics compatible with AAOIFI's Code of Ethics for Employees of IFIs, and establishes controls (including controls over applying Shari'a rules/principles to all activities); those in charge of governance ensure through oversight of management the integrity of accounting/financial reporting systems and appropriate controls; and the auditor must assess that management has developed an appropriate system of internal control that includes compliance with Shari'a rules and principles.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 17–19 (Par. 17: primary responsibility rests with TCWG and management of IFI and IAH/PA funds; management sets proper procedures, creates/maintains a culture of honesty and high ethics compatible with the Code of Ethics for Employees of IFI issued by AAOIFI, and establishes controls including over applying Sharia rules/principles to all activities; Par. 18: TCWG ensure through oversight of management the integrity of accounting/financial reporting systems and appropriate controls including risk monitoring, financial control, and compliance with Sharia rules/principles; Par. 19: auditor shall assess that management has developed an appropriate system of internal control that shall also include compliance with Sharia rules and principles).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Under Paragraph 20(a)–(e) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, which five written representations must the auditor obtain from management, and what broader responsibility does management acknowledge through them?
en.A: Management acknowledges only that it paid the audit fee, while written representations regarding IAH/PA contracts and SSB fatwas are optional.
en.B: Written representations that management: (a) has complied with all requirements of AAOIFI's Shari'a standards and the fatwas, rulings, and guidelines issued by the SSB; (b) has disclosed and raised all matters of concern known by management relating to fraud and error in the IFI; (c) has complied with all provisions of the contracts of IAH/PA; (d) has presented all SSB fatwas, rulings, and guidelines to the auditors; and (e) has placed necessary controls over assets, income, and balances of the IAH/PA—acknowledging its responsibility for the accounting and internal control systems designed to prevent and detect fraud and error.
en.C: Written representations apply exclusively to conventional tax returns and exclude any mention of IAH/PA funds.
en.D: Written representations transfer responsibility for designing internal controls from management to the external auditor.
en.True answer: Written representations that management: (a) has complied with all requirements of AAOIFI's Shari'a standards and the fatwas, rulings, and guidelines issued by the SSB; (b) has disclosed and raised all matters of concern known by management relating to fraud and error in the IFI; (c) has complied with all provisions of the contracts of IAH/PA; (d) has presented all SSB fatwas, rulings, and guidelines to the auditors; and (e) has placed necessary controls over assets, income, and balances of the IAH/PA—acknowledging its responsibility for the accounting and internal control systems designed to prevent and detect fraud and error.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 20(a)–(e) (Lists all 5 mandatory written representations from management: (a) compliance with all requirements of AAOIFI Shari'a standards and SSB fatwas/rulings/guidelines; (b) disclosure/raising of all known matters of concern relating to fraud and error in the IFI; (c) compliance with all provisions of IAH/PA contracts; (d) presentation of all SSB fatwas, rulings, and guidelines to the auditors; and (e) placement of necessary controls over assets, income, and balances of the IAH/PA—through which management acknowledges its responsibility for the accounting and internal control systems designed to prevent and detect fraud and error).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Under Paragraph 11 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, in addition to making inquiries of management, which five specific topics must the auditor's inquiries and discussions cover?
en.A: Only branch staffing budgets, IT software vendor prices, and competitor dividend yields.
en.B: Only external credit rating methodologies and central bank reserve ratios.
en.C: (1) Discussions with SSB members relating to professional judgement, interpretation, compliance, and application of Shari'a rules and principles; (2) how compliance with AAOIFI's Shari'a Standards, FASs, and SSB fatwas/rulings/guidelines is ensured by management; (3) the extent of transactions covered by the Shari'a review for determining adoption of Shari'a rules and principles; (4) the extent of controls over management and activities relating to investment of assets, income, and balances of IAH/PA; and (5) the introduction and application of effective internal control systems to safeguard IAH/PA funds and ensure compliance with Shari'a rules/principles and AAOIFI FASs.
en.D: Discussions with SSB members are strictly excluded from fraud and error planning inquiries.
en.True answer: (1) Discussions with SSB members relating to professional judgement, interpretation, compliance, and application of Shari'a rules and principles; (2) how compliance with AAOIFI's Shari'a Standards, FASs, and SSB fatwas/rulings/guidelines is ensured by management; (3) the extent of transactions covered by the Shari'a review for determining adoption of Shari'a rules and principles; (4) the extent of controls over management and activities relating to investment of assets, income, and balances of IAH/PA; and (5) the introduction and application of effective internal control systems to safeguard IAH/PA funds and ensure compliance with Shari'a rules/principles and AAOIFI FASs.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 11 (Lists all 5 bullet points of mandatory inquiries beyond management inquiries: (1) discussions with SSB members on professional judgement, interpretation, compliance, and application of Sharia rules/principles; (2) how compliance with AAOIFI Shari'a Standards, FASs, and SSB fatwas/rulings/guidelines is ensured by management; (3) extent of transactions covered by Shari'a review; (4) extent of controls over management/activities relating to investment of IAH/PA assets, income, and balances; (5) introduction and application of effective internal control systems to safeguard IAH/PA funds and comply with Sharia rules/principles and AAOIFI FASs).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Under Paragraph 8 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, which four areas require an attitude of professional skepticism by the auditor when planning and performing an audit of an Islamic financial institution?
en.A: Only verifying mathematical footings on petty cash receipts.
en.B: Relying exclusively on the SSB's annual report without evaluating management's control environment or prior-audit knowledge.
en.C: Treating all management representations as conclusively proven facts without questioning inconsistencies.
en.D: (1) Management's compliance with and application of all AAOIFI Shari'a standards as well as the SSB's fatwas, rulings, and guidelines (noting the SSB report shall not be the sole basis); (2) matters that increase the risk of material misstatement resulting from fraud and error (such as management's characteristics and influence over the control environment, industry conditions, and operating characteristics and financial stability); (3) circumstances that make the auditor suspect the financial statements are materially misstated; and (4) evidence obtained (including the auditor's knowledge from previous audits) that brings into question the reliability of management representations.
en.True answer: (1) Management's compliance with and application of all AAOIFI Shari'a standards as well as the SSB's fatwas, rulings, and guidelines (noting the SSB report shall not be the sole basis); (2) matters that increase the risk of material misstatement resulting from fraud and error (such as management's characteristics and influence over the control environment, industry conditions, and operating characteristics and financial stability); (3) circumstances that make the auditor suspect the financial statements are materially misstated; and (4) evidence obtained (including the auditor's knowledge from previous audits) that brings into question the reliability of management representations.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 8 (Lists the four bullet points requiring professional skepticism in accordance with ASIFI No. 1 Par. 6: (1) management's compliance/application of AAOIFI Shari'a standards and SSB fatwas/rulings/guidelines [with SSB report not being sole basis]; (2) matters increasing risk of material misstatement from fraud and error [management characteristics/influence over control environment, industry conditions, operating characteristics and financial stability]; (3) circumstances making auditor suspect financial statements are materially misstated; and (4) evidence obtained [including knowledge from previous audits] bringing into question reliability of management representations).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question:
During the 2025 audit of an Islamic bank and a Takaful operator, the auditor uncovers four misstatements:
• Case 1: Due to an inadvertent misunderstanding of facts in calculating asset impairment, a junior accountant miscalculated an accounting estimate under AAOIFI FASs.
• Case 2: Management deliberately allocated 15% of investment returns belonging to unrestricted investment accountholders (IAH) into shareholders' retained earnings without contractual basis.
• Case 3: Management intentionally withheld information about a series of non-Shari'ah-compliant commodity swaps from both the SSB and the external auditors.
• Case 4: A branch officer inadvertently overlooked an SSB guideline regarding Mudaraba expense deduction on two contracts due to lack of training.
According to Paragraphs 4–5 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, how are Cases 1–4 classified between 'Error' and 'Fraud'?
en.A: Cases 1 and 4 are classified as 'Error' under Paragraph 4 (Case 1 under Par. 4(a) — incorrect accounting estimate arising from oversight or misunderstanding of facts; Case 4 under Par. 4(c) — unintentional incorrect application and oversight of Shari'a rules and principles), whereas Cases 2 and 3 are classified as 'Fraud' under Paragraph 5 (Case 2 under Par. 5(b) — intentional misallocation of profits between the IFI and IAH/PA; Case 3 under Par. 5(d) — intentional non-disclosure by management of activities and relevant information to the SSB and auditors).
en.B: All four cases (Cases 1–4) are classified as 'Fraud' because any deviation from AAOIFI FASs or SSB guidelines is legally fraud.
en.C: Cases 1, 2, and 4 are classified as 'Error', while only Case 3 is classified as 'Fraud'.
en.D: Cases 2 and 3 are classified as 'Error', while Cases 1 and 4 are classified as 'Fraud'.
en.True answer: Cases 1 and 4 are classified as 'Error' under Paragraph 4 (Case 1 under Par. 4(a) — incorrect accounting estimate arising from oversight or misunderstanding of facts; Case 4 under Par. 4(c) — unintentional incorrect application and oversight of Shari'a rules and principles), whereas Cases 2 and 3 are classified as 'Fraud' under Paragraph 5 (Case 2 under Par. 5(b) — intentional misallocation of profits between the IFI and IAH/PA; Case 3 under Par. 5(d) — intentional non-disclosure by management of activities and relevant information to the SSB and auditors).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 4(a)–(c) vs. Par. 5(a)–(f) (Case 1 is unintentional miscalculation of an accounting estimate from misunderstanding facts = Error under Par. 4(a); Case 4 is unintentional oversight of an SSB guideline = Error under Par. 4(c); Case 2 is intentional misallocation of profits between IFI and IAH = Fraud under Par. 5(b); Case 3 is intentional non-disclosure by management of activities/relevant info to SSB and auditors = Fraud under Par. 5(d)).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: During an audit of an Islamic bank's Mudaraba and Wakalah investment pools, the external auditor examines supplier contracts and accounting entries. In Sample Batch A, all documents appear regular with no suspicious anomalies; in Sample Batch B, altered dates, mismatched serial numbers, and evidence from prior audits raise doubts about document authenticity and management representations. Under Paragraphs 8–9 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, how should the auditor proceed in Batch A versus Batch B?
en.A: In Batch A, the auditor must send every invoice to a forensic crime lab for authentication; in Batch B, the auditor must accept the altered documents as genuine because auditors are not forensic experts.
en.B: In Batch A, unless the audit reveals evidence to the contrary, the auditor is entitled to accept records and documents as genuine without forensic authentication (Par. 9); in Batch B, because the audit revealed evidence to the contrary and brought into question the reliability of management representations, the auditor CANNOT simply accept the documents as genuine and must apply professional skepticism to investigate further (Par. 8–9).
en.C: In both Batch A and Batch B, the auditor relies solely on the SSB's annual report without inspecting underlying contracts.
en.D: In both Batch A and Batch B, the auditor must obtain a forensic handwriting certificate for every contract.
en.True answer: In Batch A, unless the audit reveals evidence to the contrary, the auditor is entitled to accept records and documents as genuine without forensic authentication (Par. 9); in Batch B, because the audit revealed evidence to the contrary and brought into question the reliability of management representations, the auditor CANNOT simply accept the documents as genuine and must apply professional skepticism to investigate further (Par. 8–9).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 8 & Par. 9 (Par. 9: 'unless the audit reveals evidence to the contrary, the auditor is entitled to accept records and documents as genuine. Accordingly, an audit... rarely contemplates authentication of documentation, nor are auditors trained as, or expected to be, experts in such authentication'; Par. 8: professional skepticism is required where circumstances make the auditor suspect material misstatement or evidence obtained—including knowledge from previous audits—brings into question the reliability of management representations). Batch A has no contrary evidence; Batch B triggers contrary evidence requiring heightened skepticism.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 14–16 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, an auditor identifies elevated fraud risk factors during audit planning and uncovers additional fraud risk indicators during fieldwork involving Mudaraba profit allocations, followed by discussions with members of the Shari'ah Supervisory Board (SSB). Which set of documentation entries is mandatory in the auditor's working papers?
en.A: Only the final adjusted trial balance; risk factors discovered mid-audit and discussions with SSB members need not be documented.
en.B: Only a summary of management's oral explanations, without documenting the auditor's reasoning or supporting AAOIFI Shari'a standards.
en.C: The working papers must document: (1) all fraud and error risk factors identified during the assessment process AND any additional risk factors identified during audit performance, along with the auditor's response to them (Par. 14); (2) important evidence supporting the opinion, the auditor's reasoning and conclusions on all significant judgement matters, and management's response considered appropriate by the auditor (Par. 15); and (3) all discussions held with SSB members, with conclusions supported by AAOIFI's Shari'a standards and the SSB's fatwas, rulings, and guidelines (Par. 16).
en.D: Working papers must omit management's responses to fraud risk factors to protect management confidentiality.
en.True answer: The working papers must document: (1) all fraud and error risk factors identified during the assessment process AND any additional risk factors identified during audit performance, along with the auditor's response to them (Par. 14); (2) important evidence supporting the opinion, the auditor's reasoning and conclusions on all significant judgement matters, and management's response considered appropriate by the auditor (Par. 15); and (3) all discussions held with SSB members, with conclusions supported by AAOIFI's Shari'a standards and the SSB's fatwas, rulings, and guidelines (Par. 16).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 14–16 (Par. 14: document fraud and error risk factors identified during assessment AND during performance of audit, plus auditor's response; Par. 15: document important evidence, auditor's reasoning and conclusion on significant judgement matters, and management's response considered appropriate; Par. 16: document discussions held with SSB members, with conclusions supported by AAOIFI's Shari'a standards and the SSB's fatwas, rulings, and guidelines).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 10–12 and 20 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, why does ASIFI No. 5 place special emphasis on the funds of Investment Accountholders (IAH) and Policyholders (PA), and which specific audit planning, inquiry, and written representation requirements protect IAH/PA funds?
en.A: IAH and PA funds are treated identically to conventional fixed-interest bank deposits, requiring no separate risk assessment or representations.
en.B: Only shareholders' equity is subject to fraud risk assessment; IAH and PA funds are excluded from external audits.
en.C: IAH and PA funds are protected solely by external credit rating agencies without any internal control or management representation requirements.
en.D: Because IAH and PA funds are managed on a fiduciary/participatory basis where misappropriation or profit misallocation directly harms account/policyholders, ASIFI No. 5 mandates: (1) assessing in audit planning the risk that fraud and error may cause the assets, balances, and income of IAH/PA funds to contain material misstatement (Par. 10); (2) making inquiries regarding the extent of controls over management and investment of IAH/PA assets, income, and balances and internal controls safeguarding them (Par. 11); and (3) obtaining written representations from management confirming compliance with all provisions of IAH/PA contracts and placement of necessary controls over IAH/PA assets, income, and balances (Par. 20(c), (e)).
en.True answer: Because IAH and PA funds are managed on a fiduciary/participatory basis where misappropriation or profit misallocation directly harms account/policyholders, ASIFI No. 5 mandates: (1) assessing in audit planning the risk that fraud and error may cause the assets, balances, and income of IAH/PA funds to contain material misstatement (Par. 10); (2) making inquiries regarding the extent of controls over management and investment of IAH/PA assets, income, and balances and internal controls safeguarding them (Par. 11); and (3) obtaining written representations from management confirming compliance with all provisions of IAH/PA contracts and placement of necessary controls over IAH/PA assets, income, and balances (Par. 20(c), (e)).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 5(a)–(c), Par. 10, Par. 11 & Par. 20(c), (e) (Par. 5(a)–(c) highlight fraud risks specific to IAH/PA funds [misappropriation, profit misallocation, misuse/contract violation]; Par. 10 requires assessing risk of material misstatement in assets, balances, and income of IAH/PA funds; Par. 11 mandates inquiries into controls over investment and safeguarding of IAH/PA assets, income, and balances; Par. 20(c) & (e) mandate written representations that management complied with all provisions of IAH/PA contracts and placed necessary controls over IAH/PA assets, income, and balances).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question:
Compare two audit engagements under Paragraphs 6–7 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5:
• Engagement 1: The external auditor thoroughly plans and executes risk-based audit procedures in accordance with ASIFIs and IFAC standards, exercises professional skepticism, makes all required inquiries, and finds no indication of fraud; later, a sophisticated off-book kickback scheme between a vendor and a branch manager comes to light.
• Engagement 2: The external auditor skips fraud risk planning for investment accounts and discovers during testing that management intentionally misallocated USD 4 million of IAH profits to bank revenue, yet the auditor takes no action to report it to the appropriate authority.
Which evaluation of Engagements 1 and 2 is completely accurate?
en.A: In Engagement 1, the auditor is NOT liable because under Par. 6 an audit provides reasonable assurance and the auditor is not and cannot be held responsible for preventing fraud and error; in Engagement 2, the auditor SHALL be held responsible for negligence and misconduct under Par. 7 both because reasonable efforts were not made in designing/planning the audit to detect fraud and because the auditor was aware of material fraud and did not take necessary action to report it to the appropriate authority.
en.B: In both Engagements 1 and 2, the auditor is liable for negligence and misconduct.
en.C: In neither Engagement 1 nor Engagement 2 can an external auditor ever be held responsible for negligence or misconduct.
en.D: In Engagement 1, the auditor is strictly liable for failing to prevent the kickback scheme; in Engagement 2, the auditor is protected by client confidentiality.
en.True answer: In Engagement 1, the auditor is NOT liable because under Par. 6 an audit provides reasonable assurance and the auditor is not and cannot be held responsible for preventing fraud and error; in Engagement 2, the auditor SHALL be held responsible for negligence and misconduct under Par. 7 both because reasonable efforts were not made in designing/planning the audit to detect fraud and because the auditor was aware of material fraud and did not take necessary action to report it to the appropriate authority.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 6 & Par. 7 (Engagement 1 illustrates Par. 6: auditor planned/performed audit properly for reasonable assurance and is not responsible for preventing fraud; Engagement 2 triggers both limbs of Par. 7: failure to make reasonable efforts in designing/planning the audit to detect fraud and error AND being aware of material fraud and failing to take necessary action to report it to the appropriate authority, resulting in responsibility for negligence and misconduct).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 17–20 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, which combination of ethical, governance, internal control, and written representation requirements governs an Islamic financial institution's defense against fraud and error?
en.A: Management sets ethics rules based solely on local commercial customs, governance bodies delegate all oversight to external auditors, and written representations cover only tax filings.
en.B: Management must set proper procedures, create/maintain a culture of honesty and high ethics compatible with the Code of Ethics for Employees of Islamic Financial Institutions issued by AAOIFI, and establish controls (including over applying Shari'a rules/principles to all activities); those in charge of governance must ensure through oversight of management the integrity of accounting/financial reporting systems and appropriate controls (risk monitoring, financial control, Shari'a compliance); the auditor must assess that management developed an appropriate internal control system including Shari'a compliance; and the auditor must obtain all five mandatory written representations from management acknowledging responsibility for the accounting and internal control systems designed to prevent and detect fraud and error.
en.C: The external auditor designs and operates the bank's internal control system, while management signs a single oral acknowledgment.
en.D: AAOIFI's Code of Ethics for Employees applies only to external auditors and has no relevance to management's fraud prevention duties.
en.True answer: Management must set proper procedures, create/maintain a culture of honesty and high ethics compatible with the Code of Ethics for Employees of Islamic Financial Institutions issued by AAOIFI, and establish controls (including over applying Shari'a rules/principles to all activities); those in charge of governance must ensure through oversight of management the integrity of accounting/financial reporting systems and appropriate controls (risk monitoring, financial control, Shari'a compliance); the auditor must assess that management developed an appropriate internal control system including Shari'a compliance; and the auditor must obtain all five mandatory written representations from management acknowledging responsibility for the accounting and internal control systems designed to prevent and detect fraud and error.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5, Par. 17–20 (Integrates Par. 17 [management procedures, culture of honesty and high ethics compatible with AAOIFI's Code of Ethics for Employees of IFIs, and controls over all activities including Shari'a compliance], Par. 18 [TCWG oversight of management to ensure integrity of accounting/financial reporting systems and risk/financial/Shari'a controls], Par. 19 [auditor assessment of management's internal control system including Shari'a compliance], and Par. 20 [five mandatory written representations acknowledging management's responsibility for accounting and internal control systems]).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question:
During the 2025 audit of Al-Mizan Islamic Bank, the external audit team uncovers four situations:
(1) Senior management consistently and intentionally violated an AAOIFI Shari'a Standard and an SSB fatwa on Mudaraba profit smoothing and intentionally concealed those transactions from both the SSB and the auditors.
(2) Because the SSB's draft report contained no adverse remarks on Mudaraba profit smoothing (as management had concealed the transactions from the SSB), the audit senior proposes relying solely on the SSB's report to conclude that management complied with Shari'a rules and principles.
(3) After discovering the intentional profit misallocation and concealment, the external auditor concludes that the financial statements are materially misstated due to fraud, and evaluates whether to continue the audit with a qualified audit opinion or a possible disclaimer in accordance with ASIFI No. 3, paragraphs (27–46).
(4) When finalizing the audit representation letter, management agrees to sign statements covering accounting estimates and fraud disclosures, but refuses to include written representations confirming compliance with IAH contract provisions and placement of controls over IAH assets, income, and balances.
According to AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, which evaluation across (1)–(4) is completely accurate?
en.A: (1) Classified as Error; (2) Compliant—SSB report is the sole basis required; (3) Non-compliant—fraud always requires an unqualified opinion; (4) Compliant—IAH representations are optional.
en.B: (1) Classified as Fraud; (2) Compliant; (3) Non-compliant; (4) Compliant.
en.C: (1) Classified as 'Fraud'—satisfies Par. 5(b), (d), and (e) (intentional misallocation of profits, intentional non-disclosure of activities/information to the SSB and auditors, and intentional, consistent violation/misinterpretation of AAOIFI Shari'a standards and SSB fatwas); (2) Non-compliant—violates Par. 8, which explicitly stipulates that the SSB's report shall NOT be the sole basis for the auditor's conclusion on management's compliance with Shari'a rules and principles; (3) Compliant—follows Par. 13, which directs the auditor, upon concluding financial statements are materially misstated due to fraud/error, to consider implications and decide whether to continue the audit with a qualified audit opinion or possible disclaimer as stated in ASIFI No. 3, paragraphs (27–46); (4) Non-compliant—violates Par. 20(c) and (e), which mandate obtaining written representations from management that it has complied with all provisions of IAH/PA contracts and placed necessary controls over IAH/PA assets, income, and balances.
en.D: (1) Classified as Error; (2) Non-compliant; (3) Compliant; (4) Non-compliant.
en.True answer: (1) Classified as 'Fraud'—satisfies Par. 5(b), (d), and (e) (intentional misallocation of profits, intentional non-disclosure of activities/information to the SSB and auditors, and intentional, consistent violation/misinterpretation of AAOIFI Shari'a standards and SSB fatwas); (2) Non-compliant—violates Par. 8, which explicitly stipulates that the SSB's report shall NOT be the sole basis for the auditor's conclusion on management's compliance with Shari'a rules and principles; (3) Compliant—follows Par. 13, which directs the auditor, upon concluding financial statements are materially misstated due to fraud/error, to consider implications and decide whether to continue the audit with a qualified audit opinion or possible disclaimer as stated in ASIFI No. 3, paragraphs (27–46); (4) Non-compliant—violates Par. 20(c) and (e), which mandate obtaining written representations from management that it has complied with all provisions of IAH/PA contracts and placed necessary controls over IAH/PA assets, income, and balances.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5 integrates four provisions: (1) Par. 5(b), (d) & (e) classify intentional profit misallocation, intentional non-disclosure to SSB/auditors, and intentional consistent violation of AAOIFI Shari'a standards and SSB fatwas as Fraud; (2) Par. 8 explicitly states that the SSB's report shall NOT be the sole basis for the auditor's conclusion on management's compliance with Shari'a rules and principles; (3) Par. 13 requires considering implications and deciding whether to continue with a qualified opinion or possible disclaimer per ASIFI No. 3 Par. 27–46 when financial statements are materially misstated due to fraud/error; (4) Par. 20(c) & (e) mandate written representations confirming compliance with all provisions of IAH/PA contracts and placement of necessary controls over IAH/PA assets, income, and balances.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 05: Fraud and Error
en.Question:
In planning and executing the 2025 statutory audit of Takaful Al-Amanah (an Islamic insurance operator managing Policyholder [PA] funds), the external auditor evaluates four governance, inquiry, and documentation practices:
(1) During planning, the auditor assesses the risk that fraud and error may cause material misstatement not only in the company's corporate financial statements, but also specifically in the assets, balances, and income of the Policyholders' (PA) funds.
(2) In addition to inquiring of management, the auditor makes inquiries of the Audit Committee and members of the Shari'ah Supervisory Board (SSB) regarding any suspected, discovered, investigated, or reported fraud and errors, and discusses controls over PA fund investments with SSB members.
(3) During audit execution, the auditor discovers a new fraud risk factor involving irregular salvage-recovery claims in PA funds and performs additional audit procedures, but decides not to document the newly identified risk factor or the auditor's response in the working papers, and leaves SSB discussions unsupported by AAOIFI Shari'a standards or SSB rulings.
(4) In evaluating the company's internal controls, the auditor verifies that management has established procedures and a culture of honesty and high ethics compatible with AAOIFI's Code of Ethics for Employees of Islamic Financial Institutions, and assesses whether the internal control system includes compliance with Shari'a rules and principles.
According to AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 5, which evaluation across (1)–(4) is completely accurate?
en.A: (1) Non-compliant—PA funds are excluded from fraud risk assessment; (2) Non-compliant—auditors may not ask the Audit Committee or SSB about fraud; (3) Compliant—mid-audit risk factors and SSB discussions need not be documented; (4) Non-compliant—ethics culture is outside internal control review.
en.B: (1) Compliant; (2) Non-compliant; (3) Compliant; (4) Compliant.
en.C: (1) Non-compliant; (2) Compliant; (3) Non-compliant; (4) Non-compliant.
en.D: (1) Compliant—follows Par. 10, which mandates assessing in audit planning the risk that fraud and error may cause material misstatement in the financial statements as well as the assets, balances, and income of IAH/PA funds; (2) Compliant—follows Par. 11 & Par. 12, which require discussions with SSB members (including controls over IAH/PA investments) and inquiries of management, the audit committee, or SSB members regarding any suspected, discovered, investigated, and/or reported fraud and errors; (3) Non-compliant—violates Par. 14 (mandating documentation of fraud and error risk factors identified during audit performance and the auditor's response to them) and Par. 16 (mandating documentation of discussions held with SSB members with conclusions supported by AAOIFI's Shari'a standards and the SSB's fatwas, rulings, and guidelines); (4) Compliant—follows Par. 17 & Par. 19, which require management to create/maintain a culture of honesty and high ethics compatible with AAOIFI's Code of Ethics for Employees of IFIs and require the auditor to assess that management has developed an appropriate system of internal control that includes compliance with Shari'a rules and principles.
en.True answer: (1) Compliant—follows Par. 10, which mandates assessing in audit planning the risk that fraud and error may cause material misstatement in the financial statements as well as the assets, balances, and income of IAH/PA funds; (2) Compliant—follows Par. 11 & Par. 12, which require discussions with SSB members (including controls over IAH/PA investments) and inquiries of management, the audit committee, or SSB members regarding any suspected, discovered, investigated, and/or reported fraud and errors; (3) Non-compliant—violates Par. 14 (mandating documentation of fraud and error risk factors identified during audit performance and the auditor's response to them) and Par. 16 (mandating documentation of discussions held with SSB members with conclusions supported by AAOIFI's Shari'a standards and the SSB's fatwas, rulings, and guidelines); (4) Compliant—follows Par. 17 & Par. 19, which require management to create/maintain a culture of honesty and high ethics compatible with AAOIFI's Code of Ethics for Employees of IFIs and require the auditor to assess that management has developed an appropriate system of internal control that includes compliance with Shari'a rules and principles.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 5 integrates four provisions: (1) Par. 10 requires assessing risk of material misstatement in financial statements as well as assets, balances, and income of IAH/PA funds; (2) Par. 11 & Par. 12 mandate discussions with SSB members (covering IAH/PA controls) and inquiries of management, audit committee, or SSB members regarding suspected, discovered, investigated, and/or reported fraud and errors; (3) Par. 14 & Par. 16 require documenting fraud/error risk factors identified during audit performance along with the auditor's response, and documenting SSB discussions with conclusions supported by AAOIFI's Shari'a standards and SSB fatwas/rulings/guidelines; (4) Par. 17 & Par. 19 link management's ethical culture (compatible with AAOIFI's Code of Ethics for Employees of IFIs) with the auditor's assessment of internal controls including compliance with Shari'a rules and principles.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Paragraph 44 (including Footnote 3) and Appendices D and F of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6 ('External Shari'ah Audit'), how was the effective date of ASIFI 6 modified due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and what exception applied to engagements already initiated?
en.A: Originally effective for periods beginning on or after 1 January 2019, AGEB deferred the revised effective date to external Shari'ah auditors' reports covering periods beginning on or after 1 January 2020 (encouraging early adoption), while specifying that where external Shari'ah audit engagements were already initiated in line with ASIFI 6 (including signing the engagement letter) or where required by regulators, ASIFI 6 requirements remained valid.
en.B: ASIFI 6 was permanently suspended until 1 January 2028 and prohibited early adoption by any Islamic financial institution.
en.C: ASIFI 6 became effective retroactively on 1 January 1998 and was never deferred.
en.D: AGEB abolished external Shari'ah audits during the COVID-19 pandemic and replaced them with internal marketing reviews.
en.True answer: Originally effective for periods beginning on or after 1 January 2019, AGEB deferred the revised effective date to external Shari'ah auditors' reports covering periods beginning on or after 1 January 2020 (encouraging early adoption), while specifying that where external Shari'ah audit engagements were already initiated in line with ASIFI 6 (including signing the engagement letter) or where required by regulators, ASIFI 6 requirements remained valid.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 44 & Footnote 3 (Par. 44 & Footnote 3 table: original effective date of 1 January 2019 was deferred to 1 January 2020 [for external Shari'ah auditors' reports covering periods beginning on or after 01 January 2020] per AGEB statement issued 25 June 2020; Item 35 of Footnote 3 clarifies that where external Shari'ah audit engagements were already initiated in line with AS 6—including signing the engagement letter—or where required by regulators, AS 6 requirements remained valid).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Paragraph 8(d) and Appendix E (BC18–BC20) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, may the statutory external financial auditor of an IFI also be appointed as its external Shari'ah auditor, and why did the Board restrict external Shari'ah audit eligibility to professional accounting/auditing firms rather than standalone Shari'ah advisory firms?
en.A: No—the statutory external auditor is strictly barred from serving as the external Shari'ah auditor, and standalone Shari'ah advisory firms are the preferred providers.
en.B: Yes—Paragraph 8(d) explicitly states that 'The external auditor may also be appointed as the external Shari'ah auditor of the IFI', and Appendix E (BC18–BC20) explains that only professional accounting/auditing firms (having added Shari'ah subject-matter capability) are eligible because of their disciplined methodical audit approach, risk-based methodology, internal regulatory compliance systems, and team ethical scrutiny, whereas standalone Shari'ah advisory firms were excluded.
en.C: Neither financial auditing firms nor Shari'ah advisory firms are eligible; only central bank staff may conduct external Shari'ah audits.
en.D: Any Shari'ah consultancy firm may conduct external Shari'ah audits without any auditing competence or ISQC 1 quality control system.
en.True answer: Yes—Paragraph 8(d) explicitly states that 'The external auditor may also be appointed as the external Shari'ah auditor of the IFI', and Appendix E (BC18–BC20) explains that only professional accounting/auditing firms (having added Shari'ah subject-matter capability) are eligible because of their disciplined methodical audit approach, risk-based methodology, internal regulatory compliance systems, and team ethical scrutiny, whereas standalone Shari'ah advisory firms were excluded.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 8(d) & Appendix E, BC18–BC20 (Par. 8(d): defines external Shari'ah auditor as a firm having professional knowledge and competence of auditing and relevant Shari'ah principles/rules fulfilling fit and proper criteria, and explicitly states: 'The external auditor may also be appointed as the external Shari'ah auditor of the IFI'; BC18–BC20 explain that only professional accounting/auditing firms [adding Shari'ah subject-matter capability] are eligible due to their disciplined methodical approach, risk-based methodology, compliance systems, and ethical scrutiny, rejecting requests to allow Shari'ah advisory firms).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 9–11 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, what rule governs asserting compliance with ASIFI 6, which ethical code and quality control standard must the external Shari'ah auditor follow, and what team capability requirement is mandatory?
en.A: Partial compliance with ASIFI 6 may be asserted as compliant, quality control follows local HR manuals, and Shari'ah experts need only review the final cover page.
en.B: Compliance with ASIFI 6 may be asserted even if written representations were omitted, and ISQC 1 does not apply to assurance engagements.
en.C: The external Shari'ah auditor shall NOT assert compliance with ASIFI 6 unless he has complied with all requirements of the standard (Par. 9); must comply with AAOIFI's 'Code of Ethics for Accountants and Auditors of Islamic Financial Institutions' and other relevant codes (Par. 10); and must meet quality control requirements such as ISQC 1 while ensuring adequate capability in terms of resources and knowledge of the criteria, which entails the active involvement of Shari'ah expert(s) throughout the engagement (Par. 11).
en.D: Shari'ah experts are prohibited from participating in planning or fieldwork so that financial auditors work independently.
en.True answer: The external Shari'ah auditor shall NOT assert compliance with ASIFI 6 unless he has complied with all requirements of the standard (Par. 9); must comply with AAOIFI's 'Code of Ethics for Accountants and Auditors of Islamic Financial Institutions' and other relevant codes (Par. 10); and must meet quality control requirements such as ISQC 1 while ensuring adequate capability in terms of resources and knowledge of the criteria, which entails the active involvement of Shari'ah expert(s) throughout the engagement (Par. 11).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 9–11 (Par. 9: shall not assert compliance with this standard unless complied with all requirements of this standard; Par. 10: comply with 'Code of Ethics for Accountants and Auditors of Islamic Financial Institutions' issued by AAOIFI and relevant code of ethics; Par. 11: meet ISQC 1 'Quality Control for Firms That Perform Audits and Reviews of Historical Financial Information, And Other Assurance and Related Services Engagements' and ensure adequate capability in resources and knowledge of criteria, entailing 'active involvement of Shari'ah expert(s) throughout the engagement').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 17–18 and Appendix E (BC33–BC34) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, how must the external Shari'ah auditor proceed when nothing specific is available in the criteria for a novel product, and what action is mandatory if the auditor is unable to conclude on the suitability of the criteria?
en.A: Formulate personal Fiqh criteria independently without consulting the SSB, and issue an unqualified opinion.
en.B: Skip auditing the novel product entirely and issue a clean report covering only legacy products.
en.C: Ask the bank's Chief Marketing Officer to define the Shari'ah criteria and issue a qualified opinion.
en.D: Where nothing specific is available in the criteria for an IFI's functions and products, the external Shari'ah auditor must interact with the Shari'ah supervisor(s) of the IFI and form the details for criteria accordingly (Par. 17); and in cases where the external Shari'ah auditor is unable to conclude as to the suitability of criteria, he MUST either withdraw from the engagement OR disclaim the external Shari'ah audit opinion (Par. 18).
en.True answer: Where nothing specific is available in the criteria for an IFI's functions and products, the external Shari'ah auditor must interact with the Shari'ah supervisor(s) of the IFI and form the details for criteria accordingly (Par. 17); and in cases where the external Shari'ah auditor is unable to conclude as to the suitability of criteria, he MUST either withdraw from the engagement OR disclaim the external Shari'ah audit opinion (Par. 18).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 17–18 & Appendix E, BC33–BC34 (Par. 17: assess suitability of criteria, document detailed requirements, and for IFI functions/products where nothing specific is available in the criteria, interact with the Shari'ah supervisor(s) of the IFI and form the details for criteria accordingly; Par. 18 & BC34: 'In cases where the external Shari'ah auditor is unable to conclude as to the suitability of criteria, he shall either withdraw from the engagement or disclaim the external Shari'ah audit opinion').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Paragraph 19 ('Shari'ah audit process flow', p. 13) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, which sequence accurately reflects the order of stages in an external Shari'ah audit engagement?
en.A: 1. Planning → 2. Risk assessment → 3. Materiality assessment → 4. Sampling → 5. Internal controls (assessment) → 6. Internal controls (testing) → 7. Evaluation of observations and Shari'ah non-compliances → 8. Obtaining written representations → 9. Assessment of subsequent events → 10. Using the work of relevant internal functions → 11. Assessment of residual risk → 12. Testing of details → 13. Determination of impacts on the report.
en.B: 1. Determination of impacts on the report → 2. Testing of details → 3. Obtaining written representations → 4. Planning → 5. Sampling.
en.C: 1. Sampling → 2. Issuing the report → 3. Risk assessment → 4. Internal controls assessment → 5. Obtaining written representations.
