en.D: 1. Assessment of residual risk → 2. Planning → 3. Using internal audit work → 4. Materiality assessment → 5. Testing of details.
en.True answer: 1. Planning → 2. Risk assessment → 3. Materiality assessment → 4. Sampling → 5. Internal controls (assessment) → 6. Internal controls (testing) → 7. Evaluation of observations and Shari'ah non-compliances → 8. Obtaining written representations → 9. Assessment of subsequent events → 10. Using the work of relevant internal functions → 11. Assessment of residual risk → 12. Testing of details → 13. Determination of impacts on the report.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 19 Process Flow Chart (p. 13) (Depicts the exact 13-stage sequence: 1. Planning; 2. Risk assessment; 3. Materiality assessment; 4. Sampling; 5. Internal controls - assessment; 6. Internal controls - testing; 7. Evaluation of observations and Shari'ah non-compliances; 8. Obtaining written representations; 9. Assessment of subsequent events; 10. Using the work of relevant internal functions; 11. Assessment of residual risk; 12. Testing of details; 13. Determination of impacts on the report).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 26–30 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, what rules govern the dating of management's written representations, the primary written representation in an attestation engagement, and the consequence if the IFI refuses to provide one or more requested written representations?
en.A: Written representations are dated 30 days after the audit report date, and if management refuses to provide them, the auditor issues a qualified opinion.
en.B: The date of written representations must be as near as practicable to the date of the external Shari'ah auditor's report, but NOT after such date (covering all significant subsequent events); in an attestation external Shari'ah audit, the primary written representation is management's statement of compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules (supplemented by additional written representations); and if the IFI refuses to provide one or more requested written representations, the external Shari'ah auditor MUST disclaim his opinion.
en.C: Written representations are optional in direct external Shari'ah audits, and refusal results only in an emphasis of matter paragraph.
en.D: Written representations are signed by the Shari'ah Supervisory Board rather than management, and may be dated after the report release.
en.True answer: The date of written representations must be as near as practicable to the date of the external Shari'ah auditor's report, but NOT after such date (covering all significant subsequent events); in an attestation external Shari'ah audit, the primary written representation is management's statement of compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules (supplemented by additional written representations); and if the IFI refuses to provide one or more requested written representations, the external Shari'ah auditor MUST disclaim his opinion.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 27–30 (Par. 27: date of written representations shall be as near as practicable to the date of the external Shari'ah auditor's report, but not after such date, including all significant subsequent events; Par. 28: in an attestation external Shari'ah audit, primary written representation is management's statement of compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules [Appendix B2], plus additional written representations; Par. 30: 'If the IFI refuses to provide one or more of the written representations requested the external Shari'ah auditor shall disclaim his opinion').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Paragraph 34 and Appendix E (BC44–BC45) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, what is 'residual risk' in an external Shari'ah audit, and what procedures must the auditor perform when residual risk is not adequately addressed by earlier stages?
en.A: Residual risk is the audit fee remaining unpaid at year-end, resolved by sending a billing reminder.
en.B: Residual risk is eliminated completely once control walkthroughs are completed, making substantive testing unnecessary.
en.C: Residual risk is the risk remaining after controls have been assessed and tested (Stages 1–10); to reduce it to an acceptably low level, the external Shari'ah auditor must obtain further evidence and perform testing of details—including analytical and detailed verification of transactions, physical inspections, confirmations, and re-computation/analytical reviews of quantitative data (such as profit and loss distribution to investment accountholders)—and if unable to reduce risk to an acceptably low level, consider the impact on the external Shari'ah audit report.
en.D: Residual risk is assessed solely by the bank's marketing department and never affects the external Shari'ah audit report.
en.True answer: Residual risk is the risk remaining after controls have been assessed and tested (Stages 1–10); to reduce it to an acceptably low level, the external Shari'ah auditor must obtain further evidence and perform testing of details—including analytical and detailed verification of transactions, physical inspections, confirmations, and re-computation/analytical reviews of quantitative data (such as profit and loss distribution to investment accountholders)—and if unable to reduce risk to an acceptably low level, consider the impact on the external Shari'ah audit report.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 34 & Appendix E, BC44–BC45 (BC44: residual risk is the risk remaining after controls implemented have been assessed and tested [Stages 1–10]; Par. 34 & BC45: auditor assesses residual risk not adequately addressed by earlier stages and obtains further evidence by performing testing of details—including detailed verification of transactions, physical inspections, confirmations, and re-computation/analytical reviews of quantitative data such as profit and loss distribution to IAHs; if unable to reduce risk to an acceptably low level, considers impact on the external Shari'ah audit report).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 35–37 and Appendix E (BC46–BC47) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, which documentation requirements apply to the involvement of subject matter (Shari'ah) experts and differences of view with the IFI's Shari'ah supervisor(s)?
en.A: Shari'ah experts' views are kept purely verbal and excluded from working papers to maintain audit brevity.
en.B: Working papers need only document final audit fees and management's organizational chart.
en.C: Differences with the IFI's SSB are omitted from working papers once the SSB clarifies its ruling.
en.D: Documentation must be sufficient (quantitatively) and appropriate (qualitatively) for an experienced Shari'ah auditor/assurance professional to understand procedures, results, and conclusions; must document observations, conclusions, comments of management/SSB, and details of any differences against Paragraph 15 criteria along with the Shari'ah supervisor(s)' view and conclusions reached; and must document evidence of involvement of subject matter (Shari'ah) experts in the team—including assessment of their capabilities and expertise, working papers, procedures and reviews performed by them, and their views on specific Shari'ah issues.
en.True answer: Documentation must be sufficient (quantitatively) and appropriate (qualitatively) for an experienced Shari'ah auditor/assurance professional to understand procedures, results, and conclusions; must document observations, conclusions, comments of management/SSB, and details of any differences against Paragraph 15 criteria along with the Shari'ah supervisor(s)' view and conclusions reached; and must document evidence of involvement of subject matter (Shari'ah) experts in the team—including assessment of their capabilities and expertise, working papers, procedures and reviews performed by them, and their views on specific Shari'ah issues.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 35–36 & Appendix E, BC46–BC47 (Par. 35: documentation sufficient quantitatively and appropriate qualitatively to enable an experienced Shari'ah auditor/assurance professional to understand procedures, results, and conclusions; Par. 36 & BC47: document observations, conclusions, management/SSB comments, differences against Par. 15 criteria with SSB view, and evidence of involvement of subject matter [Shari'ah] experts—including assessment of capabilities/expertise, working papers, procedures/reviews performed by them, and their views on specific Shari'ah issues).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Paragraph 38(h)–(l) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, which specific elements must be included in the external Shari'ah auditor's report regarding Shari'ah experts, opinion expression, report dating, auditor identification, and the long form report?
en.A: (1) A statement about the involvement of subject matter (Shari'ah) experts; (2) the external Shari'ah auditor's opinion expressed in the positive form; (3) the date of the report, which shall be NO earlier than the date on which sufficient appropriate evidence is obtained—including the report of the IFI's Shari'ah supervisor(s); (4) the name of the external Shari'ah auditor (including firm name and engagement partner, if applicable) and location in the jurisdiction; and (5) a statement that a long form report is being issued to those charged with governance.
en.B: (1) Omission of any mention of Shari'ah experts; (2) opinion expressed in negative assurance form only; (3) report dated at least 15 days before the SSB issues its report; and (4) omission of any reference to the long form report.
en.C: (1) Personal resumes of all junior audit clerks; (2) opinion signed solely by the bank's CEO; and (3) report dated at the start of audit planning.
en.D: (1) A disclaimer of quality control standards; (2) opinion restricted to conventional GAAP; and (3) statement that the long form report is published in national newspapers.
en.True answer: (1) A statement about the involvement of subject matter (Shari'ah) experts; (2) the external Shari'ah auditor's opinion expressed in the positive form; (3) the date of the report, which shall be NO earlier than the date on which sufficient appropriate evidence is obtained—including the report of the IFI's Shari'ah supervisor(s); (4) the name of the external Shari'ah auditor (including firm name and engagement partner, if applicable) and location in the jurisdiction; and (5) a statement that a long form report is being issued to those charged with governance.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 38(h)–(l) (Enumerates: (h) statement about involvement of subject matter [Shari'ah] experts; (i) external Shari'ah auditor's opinion expressed in the positive form; (j) date of report no earlier than the date on which sufficient appropriate evidence is obtained—including the report of the Shari'ah supervisor(s) of the IFI; (k) name of external Shari'ah auditor including firm name and engagement partner [if applicable] and location in jurisdiction; and (l) statement that a long form report is being issued to those charged with governance).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 41–42 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, which three situations require the external Shari'ah auditor to modify his opinion, and what forms can a modified opinion take?
en.A: Modified opinions are triggered solely by minor administrative typos and take only the form of an Emphasis of Matter paragraph.
en.B: The opinion must be modified in the form of a qualified, adverse, or disclaimer of opinion (with a clear description of the reasons in the report) if: (1) the external Shari'ah auditor concludes that there is/are material non-compliance(s) with 'Shari'ah principles and rules', (2) in case of an attestation engagement, the subject matter information (management's statement of compliance) does not reflect a material information, or (3) the external Shari'ah auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence to reach proper conclusions.
en.C: Modified opinions are prohibited under ASIFI 6; if breaches exist, the auditor must simply resign without issuing any report.
en.D: Modified opinions apply only to financial statement audits under ASIFI 2 and never to external Shari'ah assurance engagements.
en.True answer: The opinion must be modified in the form of a qualified, adverse, or disclaimer of opinion (with a clear description of the reasons in the report) if: (1) the external Shari'ah auditor concludes that there is/are material non-compliance(s) with 'Shari'ah principles and rules', (2) in case of an attestation engagement, the subject matter information (management's statement of compliance) does not reflect a material information, or (3) the external Shari'ah auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence to reach proper conclusions.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 41–42 (Par. 41: 'If the external Shari'ah auditor concludes that there is / are material non-compliance(s) with "Shari'ah principles and rules", or in case of an attestation engagement the subject matter information does not reflect a material information, or if the external Shari'ah auditor is unable to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence to reach proper conclusions; the external Shari'ah auditor's opinion shall be modified in form of a qualified, adverse or disclaimer of opinion, as appropriate in the circumstances'; Par. 42: 'The external Shari'ah auditor's assurance report shall contain a clear description of the reasons for the modification(s) in the report').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: In Appendix B2 ('Management's statement of compliance with the Shari'ah principles and rules', pp. 26–28) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, what confirmations must management provide regarding charity funds, and which three officers sign Management's Statement of Compliance?
en.A: Management confirms that charity funds were retained in general bank reserves for 3 years, and the statement is signed solely by the external auditor.
en.B: Management confirms that charity funds were distributed to shareholders as dividends, signed by the Head of Marketing and HR Manager.
en.C: Management confirms that any amounts payable/transferable to the charity fund have been transferred within reasonable time of identification with NO amount pending transfer as of the financial statement date, and that all charity amounts were spent in accordance with the SSB-approved charity policy without unreasonable delay; and the statement is signed by (1) Head of Shari'ah Compliance (or equivalent), (2) Chief Financial Officer, and (3) Chief Executive / President.
en.D: Charity funds are excluded from Management's Statement of Compliance, which is signed solely by the Shari'ah Supervisory Board Chairman.
en.True answer: Management confirms that any amounts payable/transferable to the charity fund have been transferred within reasonable time of identification with NO amount pending transfer as of the financial statement date, and that all charity amounts were spent in accordance with the SSB-approved charity policy without unreasonable delay; and the statement is signed by (1) Head of Shari'ah Compliance (or equivalent), (2) Chief Financial Officer, and (3) Chief Executive / President.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Appendix B2 'Charity' & signature block (pp. 27–28) (Management confirms that any amounts determined to be payable/transferable to charity fund have been transferred within reasonable time of identification and as of the date of financial statements there is no amount of charity pending transfer, and all amounts allocated were spent in accordance with the SSB-approved charity policy without unreasonable delay; signature block on p. 28 lists three signatories: Head of Shari'ah Compliance [or equivalent], Chief Financial Officer, and Chief Executive / President).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Appendix C ('Long form report - suggested contents', p. 29) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, which specific elements must be included in the external Shari'ah auditor's Long Form Report?
en.A: Only the short-form opinion paragraph and a list of bank branch addresses.
en.B: A positive assurance opinion certifying that internal controls are 100% immune from error, omitting the names of Shari'ah experts.
en.C: Confidential customer account balances and individual staff salary schedules.
en.D: Objective and scope of engagement; key audit matters (overall Shari'ah compliance environment, risks associated with Shari'ah non-compliance, capacity/quality of the risk management system including awareness/sensitization of management and TCWG); management's and auditor's responsibilities; broad description of procedures performed; engagement limitations; detailed factual findings identifying gaps/issues and recommendations; a statement that the procedures performed do not constitute an audit or review under applicable standards and no assurance is expressed thereon; and the name and qualifications of the subject matter (Shari'ah) expert(s) appointed.
en.True answer: Objective and scope of engagement; key audit matters (overall Shari'ah compliance environment, risks associated with Shari'ah non-compliance, capacity/quality of the risk management system including awareness/sensitization of management and TCWG); management's and auditor's responsibilities; broad description of procedures performed; engagement limitations; detailed factual findings identifying gaps/issues and recommendations; a statement that the procedures performed do not constitute an audit or review under applicable standards and no assurance is expressed thereon; and the name and qualifications of the subject matter (Shari'ah) expert(s) appointed.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Appendix C (a)–(h) (p. 29) (Enumerates all 8 minimum items of the Long Form Report: (a) objective and scope; (b) key audit matters [overall Shari'ah compliance environment, Shari'ah non-compliance risks, capacity/quality of risk management system including management/TCWG awareness]; (c) responsibilities and key terms; (d) broad description of procedures performed; (e) engagement limitations; (f) detailed factual findings with gap/issue and recommendation; (g) statement that the procedures performed do not constitute an audit or review and no assurance is expressed; and (h) name and qualifications of the subject matter [Shari'ah] expert(s) appointed).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: In Appendix E (Basis for Conclusions, BC3–BC11) and Paragraphs 2–3 of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, how did the Board resolve: (1) whether ASIFI 6 should be classified as a Governance Standard or an Auditing Standard, (2) whether ASIFI 6 imposes a mandatory annual external Shari'ah audit requirement on IFIs, and (3) how ASIFI 6 interacts with ISAE 3000?
en.A: (1) The Board issued ASIFI 6 as an Auditing Standard (rather than a Governance Standard) because its primary applicability is on external Shari'ah auditors providing an independent assurance service rather than on IFIs; (2) requiring IFIs to conduct annual external Shari'ah audits falls within the ambit of regulatory requirements and governance standards rather than an auditing standard itself (and ASIFI 6 remains non-mandatory on auditors until AAOIFI's auditing standards revision project concludes); and (3) ASIFI 6 complements ISAE 3000 (Revised), whose requirements apply to external Shari'ah audits unless contrary to or inconsistent with ASIFI 6 or Shari'ah requirements.
en.B: (1) ASIFI 6 was issued as a Governance Standard binding directly on retail depositors; (2) ASIFI 6 itself legally mandates quarterly external Shari'ah audits for every bank globally; and (3) ISAE 3000 is completely excluded.
en.C: (1) ASIFI 6 is a Financial Accounting Standard; (2) external Shari'ah audits are prohibited unless requested by tax authorities; and (3) ISAE 3000 overrides Shari'ah principles whenever a conflict arises.
en.D: (1) ASIFI 6 was issued as a non-binding marketing brochure; (2) external Shari'ah auditors are exempt from ISAE 3000; and (3) AAOIFI governance standards never require external Shari'ah audits.
en.True answer: (1) The Board issued ASIFI 6 as an Auditing Standard (rather than a Governance Standard) because its primary applicability is on external Shari'ah auditors providing an independent assurance service rather than on IFIs; (2) requiring IFIs to conduct annual external Shari'ah audits falls within the ambit of regulatory requirements and governance standards rather than an auditing standard itself (and ASIFI 6 remains non-mandatory on auditors until AAOIFI's auditing standards revision project concludes); and (3) ASIFI 6 complements ISAE 3000 (Revised), whose requirements apply to external Shari'ah audits unless contrary to or inconsistent with ASIFI 6 or Shari'ah requirements.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 2–3 & Appendix E, BC3–BC11 (BC3–BC4: issued as an Auditing Standard because its primary applicability is on external Shari'ah auditors as an independent assurance service rather than on IFIs; BC5–BC6: mandating annual external Shari'ah audits on IFIs falls under regulatory requirements and governance standards rather than an auditing standard, and ASIFI 6 remains non-mandatory on auditors until the auditing standards revision project concludes; Par. 2–3 & BC7–BC11: ASIFI 6 complements ISAE 3000, whose requirements apply unless contrary to or inconsistent with ASIFI 6 or Shari'ah).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Comparing 'Direct External Shari'ah Audit' versus 'Attestation External Shari'ah Audit' under Paragraphs 5–8, 38(i), 38(m), and Appendix E (BC12–BC15, BC51–BC53) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, why does ASIFI 6 prefer the direct form, and how must an attestation report address material Shari'ah non-compliances that are adequately described in management's Statement of Compliance?
en.A: Attestation audit is preferred because it provides higher assurance; and when management's Statement of Compliance discloses a material Shari'ah non-compliance, the auditor must issue an adverse opinion on management's statement.
en.B: ASIFI 6 prefers Direct External Shari'ah Audit because direct audits provide a higher level of assurance due to the extent of procedures performed and form of reporting (BC14); in an Attestation External Shari'ah Audit, if management's Statement of Compliance fairly and adequately describes a material non-compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules, the auditor must NOT modify/qualify his opinion (since management's statement presents a true and fair view), but MUST include a reference/emphasis paragraph without modifying the opinion drawing attention to the material non-compliance(s) described in management's statement so users do not mistakenly assume full compliance (Par. 38(m), Appendix B1 p. 25, BC51–BC53).
en.C: Both forms produce identical opinion wording, and disclosed non-compliances in management's statement must never be mentioned anywhere in the external auditor's report.
en.D: Attestation audits are prohibited in all jurisdictions, and direct audits report solely on management's written statement rather than underlying contracts.
en.True answer: ASIFI 6 prefers Direct External Shari'ah Audit because direct audits provide a higher level of assurance due to the extent of procedures performed and form of reporting (BC14); in an Attestation External Shari'ah Audit, if management's Statement of Compliance fairly and adequately describes a material non-compliance with Shari'ah principles and rules, the auditor must NOT modify/qualify his opinion (since management's statement presents a true and fair view), but MUST include a reference/emphasis paragraph without modifying the opinion drawing attention to the material non-compliance(s) described in management's statement so users do not mistakenly assume full compliance (Par. 38(m), Appendix B1 p. 25, BC51–BC53).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 5–8, Par. 38(m), Appendix B1 (p. 25) & Appendix E, BC12–BC15, BC51–BC53 (BC14: direct external Shari'ah audit is preferred because it provides a higher level of assurance due to the extent of procedures performed and form of reporting; Par. 38(m), Appendix B1 p. 25 & BC51–BC53: in an attestation engagement, where management's statement of compliance adequately describes a material non-compliance, the auditor does NOT modify/qualify the opinion because the statement fairly presents the state of affairs, but MUST include an un-modified reference/emphasis paragraph drawing attention to the non-compliances in management's statement to prevent users from assuming there is no non-compliance).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 21–22 and Appendix E (BC35–BC38) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, why can materiality thresholds in an external Shari'ah audit differ from those in a financial statements audit, and how must Shari'ah non-compliant income that is quantitatively small be treated?
en.A: Materiality in external Shari'ah audit is calculated solely as 5% of net profit, and non-compliant income below that threshold may be retained in bank equity.
en.B: Qualitative materiality is ignored in ASIFI 6, and quantitatively small observations are omitted from both the short form report and the Long Form Report.
en.C: Materiality in external Shari'ah audit encompasses both quantitative and qualitative considerations (nature, cause, and severity from a Shari'ah perspective) and often differs from financial statement audit materiality because stakeholders (such as investment accountholders) have different decision-making protocols and tolerance limits; furthermore, Shari'ah non-compliant income MUST be mandatorily eliminated from income irrespective of being quantitatively immaterial, and observations that are quantitatively immaterial yet qualitatively significant are reported in the Long Form Report (BC36–BC37).
en.D: External Shari'ah audits provide absolute 100% assurance without using any materiality thresholds.
en.True answer: Materiality in external Shari'ah audit encompasses both quantitative and qualitative considerations (nature, cause, and severity from a Shari'ah perspective) and often differs from financial statement audit materiality because stakeholders (such as investment accountholders) have different decision-making protocols and tolerance limits; furthermore, Shari'ah non-compliant income MUST be mandatorily eliminated from income irrespective of being quantitatively immaterial, and observations that are quantitatively immaterial yet qualitatively significant are reported in the Long Form Report (BC36–BC37).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 21–22 & Appendix E, BC35–BC38 (Par. 21–22: materiality includes quantitative and qualitative considerations [nature, cause, severity from Shari'ah perspective, significance to specific stakeholders] and may not arrive at the same values as a financial statement audit because stakeholder decision-making protocols and tolerance limits differ; BC36–BC37: Shari'ah non-compliant income must be mandatorily eliminated from income irrespective of being quantitatively immaterial, and the Long Form Report ensures that observations quantitatively immaterial yet qualitatively significant are adequately reported).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 31–33 (including Footnote 2) and Appendix E (BC41–BC43) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, how does the external Shari'ah auditor evaluate and use the work of the independent Internal Shari'ah Audit / Review function versus management's Shari'ah Compliance Department?
en.A: Both functions are completely unusable because external Shari'ah auditors are barred from reading any internal reports.
en.B: Both functions are equally independent and may be used interchangeably to replace 100% of external Shari'ah audit testing.
en.C: Management's Shari'ah Compliance Department may replace external audit testing, whereas the Internal Shari'ah Audit function cannot be relied upon.
en.D: The primary criterion for using internal work is relative independence from management (applying ISA 610 methodology): once determined independent and reliable, the external Shari'ah auditor reviews the reports (and working papers where necessary) of the independent Internal Shari'ah Audit / Internal Shari'ah Review function (GSIFI 3) and the SSB's report to determine their impact on the nature, timing, and extent of external audit work; in contrast, Shari'ah-related management functions such as the Shari'ah Compliance Department are NOT independent of management and CANNOT be used as a part replacement for the external Shari'ah auditor's work (though their work may be evaluated as part of effective internal controls).
en.True answer: The primary criterion for using internal work is relative independence from management (applying ISA 610 methodology): once determined independent and reliable, the external Shari'ah auditor reviews the reports (and working papers where necessary) of the independent Internal Shari'ah Audit / Internal Shari'ah Review function (GSIFI 3) and the SSB's report to determine their impact on the nature, timing, and extent of external audit work; in contrast, Shari'ah-related management functions such as the Shari'ah Compliance Department are NOT independent of management and CANNOT be used as a part replacement for the external Shari'ah auditor's work (though their work may be evaluated as part of effective internal controls).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 31–33, Footnote 2 & Appendix E, BC41–BC43 (Par. 31 & BC41–BC43: primary criterion for assessing usability is relative independence from management, applying ISA 610 methodology; independent internal Shari'ah review / internal Shari'ah audit [GSIFI 3] work and SSB reports may be used to complement external audit work and determine nature/timing/extent of procedures; however, Shari'ah-related management functions such as the Shari'ah compliance department are not independent of management and 'shall not be considered for this purpose. Their work, however, can be considered as a part of effective internal controls but not to be used as a part replacement for external Shari'ah auditor's work').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Paragraph 38(b), Paragraph 38(j), and Appendix E (BC21–BC22, BC48–BC50) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, how are the addressees and issuance dates of the Short Form Report versus the Long Form Report determined?
en.A: The Short Form Report is addressed preferably to the shareholders of the IFI (unless regulators designate themselves, the board of directors, or URIAs) and must be dated no earlier than obtaining sufficient appropriate evidence including the report of the IFI's Shari'ah supervisor(s) (on or after the SSB report date, normally issued concurrently on the same date via mutual consultation and draft sharing); whereas the Long Form Report is addressed to Those Charged with Governance (TCWG) rather than shareholders/general public (though sharable with regulators as needed).
en.B: Both the Short Form Report and the Long Form Report are addressed to the general public and must be published in newspapers at least 10 days before the SSB completes its report.
en.C: The Short Form Report is addressed solely to the Chief Executive Officer, while the Long Form Report is addressed to retail depositors.
en.D: The external Shari'ah auditor's report must always be dated prior to the SSB's report so that the SSB can copy its conclusions.
en.True answer: The Short Form Report is addressed preferably to the shareholders of the IFI (unless regulators designate themselves, the board of directors, or URIAs) and must be dated no earlier than obtaining sufficient appropriate evidence including the report of the IFI's Shari'ah supervisor(s) (on or after the SSB report date, normally issued concurrently on the same date via mutual consultation and draft sharing); whereas the Long Form Report is addressed to Those Charged with Governance (TCWG) rather than shareholders/general public (though sharable with regulators as needed).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 38(b), Par. 38(j), Par. 40 & Appendix E, BC21–BC22, BC48–BC50 (Par. 38(b) & BC48: short form report addressed to shareholders of the IFI unless otherwise required by regulators; Par. 38(j) & BC49–BC50: report dated no earlier than obtaining sufficient appropriate evidence including the report of the IFI's Shari'ah supervisor(s)—on or after SSB report date, normally issued concurrently on the same date via draft sharing per AS 4; Par. 40 & BC22: Long Form Report addressed to TCWG and not made public to shareholders/general public, though sharable with regulators as needed).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 13, 24–25, and Appendix E (BC29–BC32, BC39–BC40) of AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 6, why are non-financial behavioral or dress-code matters excluded from the underlying subject matter of an external Shari'ah audit, and how does the standard combine statistical and judgmental sampling?
en.A: Employee dress-code compliance is the primary subject matter of an external Shari'ah audit, and judgmental sampling is strictly prohibited.
en.B: The underlying subject matter is limited to assessing compliance of the IFI's 'financial arrangements, contracts, and transactions' with Shari'ah principles and rules (excluding non-financial personal traits or employee dress codes that do not affect contract permissibility, BC29–BC32); and while sample sizes and selection primarily apply statistical approaches responsive to Shari'ah non-compliance risk and materiality, a judgmental approach MUST be applied on areas affected by qualitative materiality factors, and sample sizes MUST be increased adequately whenever instances of Shari'ah non-compliance are identified (Par. 24–25, BC39–BC40).
en.C: Sampling is prohibited in external Shari'ah audits; auditors must test 100% of all transactions and personal employee conduct.
en.D: When instances of Shari'ah non-compliance are found in a sample, the auditor reduces the sample size to avoid delaying the report.
en.True answer: The underlying subject matter is limited to assessing compliance of the IFI's 'financial arrangements, contracts, and transactions' with Shari'ah principles and rules (excluding non-financial personal traits or employee dress codes that do not affect contract permissibility, BC29–BC32); and while sample sizes and selection primarily apply statistical approaches responsive to Shari'ah non-compliance risk and materiality, a judgmental approach MUST be applied on areas affected by qualitative materiality factors, and sample sizes MUST be increased adequately whenever instances of Shari'ah non-compliance are identified (Par. 24–25, BC39–BC40).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6, Par. 13, Par. 24–25 & Appendix E, BC29–BC32, BC39–BC40 (Par. 13 & BC29–BC32: underlying subject matter is limited to 'financial' arrangements, contracts, and transactions, excluding non-financial matters such as personal traits or employee dress code that do not affect contract permissibility; Par. 24–25 & BC39–BC40: statistical approaches are combined with a judgmental approach on areas affected by qualitative factors of materiality, and in case of identified instances of Shari'ah non-compliance, sample sizes shall be increased adequately).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question:
In Country Z, the banking regulator mandates an Attestation External Shari'ah Audit under ASIFI No. 6 for Al-Wafa Islamic Bank for the year ended 31 December 2025. Examine the following four engagement events:
(1) Management prepares and issues its 'Statement of Compliance with Shari'ah Principles and Rules', signed jointly by the Head of Shari'ah Compliance, the Chief Financial Officer, and the Chief Executive Officer, confirming that all charity amounts identified were transferred to the charity fund within reasonable time with zero balance pending transfer at year-end.
(2) In that Statement of Compliance, management fairly and adequately discloses a material Shari'ah non-compliance involving improper profit allocation on a specific Mudaraba tranche during Q2; when drafting the Attestation External Shari'ah Audit Report, the external auditor decides to issue an unmodified opinion on management's Statement of Compliance while adding an emphasis/reference paragraph (without modifying the opinion) drawing readers' attention to the non-compliance described in management's statement.
(3) Prior to report finalization, management refuses to provide a requested additional written representation confirming disclosure of known deficiencies in internal control design.
(4) Alongside the short form attestation report, the external auditor issues a Long Form Report addressed to the shareholders at large and publishes it on the bank's public website without naming the Shari'ah expert appointed to the audit team.
According to ASIFI No. 6, which evaluation across (1)–(4) is completely accurate?
en.A: (1) Non-compliant; (2) Non-compliant—disclosed non-compliances always require a qualified attestation opinion; (3) Compliant—written representations are optional; (4) Compliant—Long Form Reports are published to shareholders.
en.B: (1) Compliant; (2) Non-compliant; (3) Non-compliant; (4) Compliant.
en.C: (1) Compliant—matches Appendix B2 ('Charity' & signature block, pp. 27–28), signed by Head of Shari'ah Compliance, CFO, and CEO; (2) Compliant—follows Par. 38(m), Appendix B1 (p. 25), and Appendix E (BC51–BC53), under which the auditor does NOT modify/qualify the attestation opinion when management's statement fairly describes a material non-compliance, but MUST include an un-modified reference/emphasis paragraph drawing attention to it so users do not assume full compliance; (3) Non-compliant—violates Par. 26, Par. 28 & Par. 30, which require obtaining additional written representations (including known control deficiencies) and mandate that if the IFI refuses to provide one or more requested written representations, the external Shari'ah auditor MUST disclaim his opinion; (4) Non-compliant—violates Par. 40, Appendix C(h), and Appendix E (BC22), under which the Long Form Report MUST be addressed to Those Charged with Governance (TCWG) rather than shareholders/general public (not made public) and MUST include the name and qualifications of the subject matter (Shari'ah) expert(s) appointed.
en.D: (1) Compliant; (2) Compliant; (3) Compliant; (4) Non-compliant.
en.True answer: (1) Compliant—matches Appendix B2 ('Charity' & signature block, pp. 27–28), signed by Head of Shari'ah Compliance, CFO, and CEO; (2) Compliant—follows Par. 38(m), Appendix B1 (p. 25), and Appendix E (BC51–BC53), under which the auditor does NOT modify/qualify the attestation opinion when management's statement fairly describes a material non-compliance, but MUST include an un-modified reference/emphasis paragraph drawing attention to it so users do not assume full compliance; (3) Non-compliant—violates Par. 26, Par. 28 & Par. 30, which require obtaining additional written representations (including known control deficiencies) and mandate that if the IFI refuses to provide one or more requested written representations, the external Shari'ah auditor MUST disclaim his opinion; (4) Non-compliant—violates Par. 40, Appendix C(h), and Appendix E (BC22), under which the Long Form Report MUST be addressed to Those Charged with Governance (TCWG) rather than shareholders/general public (not made public) and MUST include the name and qualifications of the subject matter (Shari'ah) expert(s) appointed.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6 integrates four rules: (1) Appendix B2 (pp. 27–28) requires charity transfer/spending confirmations and signatures of Head of Shari'ah Compliance, CFO, and CEO; (2) Par. 38(m), Appendix B1 (p. 25) & Appendix E BC51–BC53 mandate issuing an un-modified attestation opinion paired with a reference paragraph drawing attention to material non-compliances adequately described in management's statement; (3) Par. 26, 28 & 30 require obtaining additional written representations (including control deficiencies) and mandate a disclaimer of opinion if the IFI refuses to provide any requested written representation; (4) Par. 40, Appendix C(h) & BC22 require addressing the Long Form Report to TCWG (not shareholders/general public) and disclosing the name and qualifications of appointed Shari'ah expert(s).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Auditing Standard No. 06: External Shari'ah Audit
en.Question:
During the 2025 Direct External Shari'ah Audit engagement of Al-Huda Islamic Bank, evaluate the following four procurement, criteria, reliance, and testing decisions:
(1) A standalone Shari'ah consultancy boutique (which is NOT a professional accounting/auditing firm) submits a bid to be appointed as the bank's external Shari'ah auditor under ASIFI No. 6.
(2) After appointing an eligible professional auditing firm with active Shari'ah experts on the team, the auditors encounter a newly launched tokenized Sukuk product for which nothing specific is available in the criteria; the auditors interact with the bank's SSB to form the criteria details, and for another bespoke derivative-like structure where the auditors are unable to conclude on the suitability of criteria, they evaluate withdrawing or disclaiming the opinion.
(3) To save audit hours, the external Shari'ah audit team uses the work and testing reports of the bank's management-run Shari'ah Compliance Department as a direct 50% replacement for external substantive testing.
(4) After completing control assessment and testing (Stages 1–10), the external Shari'ah auditors determine that high residual risk remains in the profit and loss distribution to Unrestricted Investment Accountholders (URIAs), so they perform testing of details—including re-computation and analytical reviews of quantitative profit-distribution data—to reduce residual risk to an acceptably low level.
According to ASIFI No. 6, which evaluation across (1)–(4) is completely accurate?
en.A: (1) Eligible—Shari'ah consultancy boutiques are permitted; (2) Non-compliant—auditors never interact with the SSB to form criteria details; (3) Compliant—Shari'ah Compliance Department work replaces 50% of external testing; (4) Non-compliant—testing of details is unnecessary after Stage 10.
en.B: (1) Ineligible; (2) Non-compliant; (3) Compliant; (4) Non-compliant.
en.C: (1) Eligible; (2) Compliant; (3) Non-compliant; (4) Compliant.
en.D: (1) Ineligible—under Par. 8(d) & Appendix E (BC18–BC20), only professional accounting/auditing firms (having added Shari'ah subject-matter capability) are eligible to perform external Shari'ah audits, and standalone Shari'ah advisory/consultancy firms are excluded; (2) Compliant—follows Par. 17–18 & Appendix E (BC33–BC34), which direct the auditor to interact with the IFI's Shari'ah supervisor(s) to form criteria details when nothing specific exists, and require withdrawing or disclaiming the opinion when unable to conclude on criteria suitability; (3) Non-compliant—violates Par. 31 & Appendix E (BC43), which establish that Shari'ah-related management functions such as the Shari'ah Compliance Department are NOT independent of management and CANNOT be used as a part replacement for the external Shari'ah auditor's work (though their work may be evaluated as part of internal controls); (4) Compliant—follows Par. 34 & Appendix E (BC44–BC45), which mandate performing testing of details (including re-computation and analytical reviews of profit and loss distribution to IAHs) to reduce remaining residual risk to an acceptably low level.
en.True answer: (1) Ineligible—under Par. 8(d) & Appendix E (BC18–BC20), only professional accounting/auditing firms (having added Shari'ah subject-matter capability) are eligible to perform external Shari'ah audits, and standalone Shari'ah advisory/consultancy firms are excluded; (2) Compliant—follows Par. 17–18 & Appendix E (BC33–BC34), which direct the auditor to interact with the IFI's Shari'ah supervisor(s) to form criteria details when nothing specific exists, and require withdrawing or disclaiming the opinion when unable to conclude on criteria suitability; (3) Non-compliant—violates Par. 31 & Appendix E (BC43), which establish that Shari'ah-related management functions such as the Shari'ah Compliance Department are NOT independent of management and CANNOT be used as a part replacement for the external Shari'ah auditor's work (though their work may be evaluated as part of internal controls); (4) Compliant—follows Par. 34 & Appendix E (BC44–BC45), which mandate performing testing of details (including re-computation and analytical reviews of profit and loss distribution to IAHs) to reduce remaining residual risk to an acceptably low level.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI ASIFI No. 6 integrates four rules: (1) Par. 8(d) & Appendix E BC18–BC20 restrict eligibility to professional accounting/auditing firms (with Shari'ah expertise), excluding standalone Shari'ah advisory firms; (2) Par. 17–18 & BC33–BC34 require interacting with Shari'ah supervisor(s) to form criteria details when nothing specific exists and withdrawing/disclaiming opinion when unable to conclude on criteria suitability; (3) Par. 31 & BC43 forbid using management's Shari'ah Compliance Department as a part replacement for external Shari'ah auditor's work (unlike independent internal Shari'ah audit under ISA 610); (4) Par. 34 & BC44–BC45 require performing testing of details (re-computation, analytical reviews of IAH profit/loss distribution) to reduce residual risk to an acceptably low level.

en.Theme: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13: Waqf Governance
en.Question: Which of the following accurately describes the scope, companion standards, and authoritative hierarchy of the AAOIFI Guidance Note for Governance Standard 13 ('Waqf Governance')?
en.A: It supersedes AAOIFI GS 13 ('Waqf Governance') and AAOIFI Shari'ah Standard (SS) 60, overriding GS 13 in case of any inconsistency.
en.B: Set out in paragraphs 1–78, it provides explanations on the nature and types of Waqf, illustrative terms of reference for committees, and suggested governance and internal control policies; it is read in conjunction with AAOIFI's Shari'ah Standard (SS) 60 on Waqf and GS 13 ('Waqf Governance'), and in case of any inconsistency between GS 13 and the Guidance Note, the requirements of GS 13 prevail.
en.C: It applies exclusively to commercial Islamic banks and has no connection to AAOIFI SS 60 on Waqf.
en.D: In case of any inconsistency between GS 13 and the Guidance Note, the Guidance Note prevails over GS 13.
en.True answer: Set out in paragraphs 1–78, it provides explanations on the nature and types of Waqf, illustrative terms of reference for committees, and suggested governance and internal control policies; it is read in conjunction with AAOIFI's Shari'ah Standard (SS) 60 on Waqf and GS 13 ('Waqf Governance'), and in case of any inconsistency between GS 13 and the Guidance Note, the requirements of GS 13 prevail.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, Introductory Note (p. 3) & Par. 1–2 (Set out in paragraphs 1–78; includes explanations on nature/types of Waqf, illustrative/suggested TORs for committees, and suggestions for governance/internal control policies; read in conjunction with AAOIFI's Shari'ah Standard [SS] 60 on Waqf and GS 13 'Waqf Governance'; explicitly states: 'In case of any inconsistencies between this standard and the guidance note, the requirements of the standard shall prevail').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13: Waqf Governance
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 3–7 of the AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, how are Charitable, Private, Joint, and Family Waqfs distinguished, and what recommendations apply to a Family Waqf?
en.A: Waqf is making a property/source of wealth inalienable and donating its usufruct to beneficiaries: charitable Waqf pays benefits to general charitable activities; private Waqf benefits a close private group; joint Waqf benefits both public and private beneficiaries; and family Waqf benefits immediate or extended family members—where the Waqif must adhere to inheritance principles without violating Shari'ah, is recommended not to limit yield (Ghallah) solely to his offspring (making it a joint Waqf with public entities instead), and should preferably grant beneficiaries in the Waqf deed the right to view the Nazir's annual report (per GS 13 Par. 79).
en.B: Family Waqfs are exempt from Shari'ah inheritance rules and beneficiaries are prohibited from viewing the Nazir's annual report.
en.C: When private beneficiaries' entitlement hierarchy ends, the Waqf corpus reverts automatically to the Nazir's personal estate.
en.D: Joint Waqf refers exclusively to a Waqf co-owned by two foreign sovereign governments.
en.True answer: Waqf is making a property/source of wealth inalienable and donating its usufruct to beneficiaries: charitable Waqf pays benefits to general charitable activities; private Waqf benefits a close private group; joint Waqf benefits both public and private beneficiaries; and family Waqf benefits immediate or extended family members—where the Waqif must adhere to inheritance principles without violating Shari'ah, is recommended not to limit yield (Ghallah) solely to his offspring (making it a joint Waqf with public entities instead), and should preferably grant beneficiaries in the Waqf deed the right to view the Nazir's annual report (per GS 13 Par. 79).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, Par. 3–7 (Par. 3: making property/source of wealth inalienable and donating usufruct to beneficiaries; Par. 4: charitable vs. private vs. joint Waqf; Par. 5: when beneficiaries' entitlement hierarchy ends, benefits go to general public beneficiaries as determined by Waqif or Nazir; Par. 6–7: family Waqf must adhere to inheritance principles without violating Shari'ah; recommended not to limit Ghallah to offspring but make it a joint Waqf with public entities; preferable that Waqf deed in family and joint Waqf gives beneficiaries the right to view the annual report prepared by the Nazir per GS 13 Par. 79).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13: Waqf Governance
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 8–13 of the AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, what juristic status does a Waqf hold from a Shari'ah perspective, what legal forms may it take under jurisdictional law, and what four criteria govern Waqf assets?
en.A: A Waqf has no separate juristic personality and merges into the Nazir's personal balance sheet; Waqf assets may be borrowed or mortgaged property not yet owned by the Waqif.
en.B: A Waqf may only be registered as a commercial joint-stock bank, and assets must be short-term speculative derivatives.
en.C: From a Shari'ah perspective, a Waqf should have an independent juristic personality and a separate financial edict from the Waqif, the beneficiaries, and the Nazir (taking legal forms under local law such as a Waqf, trust, endowment, foundation, cooperative society, company, or corporation); and Waqf assets (1) should typically be sustainable and long-term in nature, (2) must be owned by the Waqif (legally and by Shari'ah) at the time of creation, (3) are chosen at the absolute discretion of the Waqif, and (4) must be Shari'ah-compliant.
en.D: The Nazir selects which assets the Waqif must endow, and non-Shari'ah-compliant assets may be endowed if later purified.
en.True answer: From a Shari'ah perspective, a Waqf should have an independent juristic personality and a separate financial edict from the Waqif, the beneficiaries, and the Nazir (taking legal forms under local law such as a Waqf, trust, endowment, foundation, cooperative society, company, or corporation); and Waqf assets (1) should typically be sustainable and long-term in nature, (2) must be owned by the Waqif (legally and by Shari'ah) at the time of creation, (3) are chosen at the absolute discretion of the Waqif, and (4) must be Shari'ah-compliant.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, Par. 8–13 (Par. 8–9: independent juristic personality and separate financial edict from Waqif, beneficiaries, and Nazir; legal forms per jurisdiction laws such as Waqf, trust, endowment, foundation, cooperative society, company, or corporation; Par. 10–13: Waqf assets should typically be sustainable and long-term in nature; owned by Waqif legally and by Shari'ah at creation; choice of assets is absolute discretion of Waqif; chosen assets must be Shari'ah-compliant).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13: Waqf Governance
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 14–16 of the AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, how must a Nazir handle (1) explicit conditions in the Waqf deed, (2) ambiguous conditions, (3) conflicting conditions, and (4) an imperative need to deviate from a condition?
en.A: The Nazir may freely ignore any Waqf deed condition whenever it reduces short-term commercial investment returns.
en.B: Ambiguous conditions are automatically voided, and conflicting conditions require liquidating the entire Waqf.
en.C: The Nazir may deviate from Waqf deed conditions even if the deviation violates Shari'ah principles or local Waqf laws.
en.D: Explicit conditions must be adhered to (provided they do not violate Shari'ah or jurisdiction Waqf laws); in case of ambiguity, the Waqif's intention must be identified (using customary practices if helpful); where conditions conflict, they should be combined if all can be achieved, or otherwise what is in the best interest of the Waqf must be implemented; and deviation from a condition is permitted ONLY when an imperative need in the best interest of the Waqf and its fundamental objectives requires it—and under NO circumstances may any deviation contravene Shari'ah principles/rules or Waqf-related laws and regulations of the jurisdiction.
en.True answer: Explicit conditions must be adhered to (provided they do not violate Shari'ah or jurisdiction Waqf laws); in case of ambiguity, the Waqif's intention must be identified (using customary practices if helpful); where conditions conflict, they should be combined if all can be achieved, or otherwise what is in the best interest of the Waqf must be implemented; and deviation from a condition is permitted ONLY when an imperative need in the best interest of the Waqf and its fundamental objectives requires it—and under NO circumstances may any deviation contravene Shari'ah principles/rules or Waqf-related laws and regulations of the jurisdiction.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, Par. 14–16 (Par. 14: purpose/conditions set by Waqif in Waqf deed are the basis for Nazir's conduct and must not violate Shari'ah or jurisdiction Waqf laws; Par. 15: adhere to explicit conditions; resolve ambiguity by identifying Waqif's intention using customary practices; combine conflicting conditions if all can be achieved, otherwise implement what is in best interest of Waqf; Par. 16: adhere to conditions unless an imperative need in the best interest of the Waqf and achievement of its fundamental objectives requires deviation, provided no deviation ever contravenes Shari'ah principles/rules or Waqf-related laws/regulations).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13: Waqf Governance
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 17–20 of the AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, how are members of the Board of Nazirs appointed when (1) the Waqif holds appointment authority, (2) the Waqif does NOT have authority to appoint members, and (3) a casual vacancy arises in the absence of the Waqif?
en.A: (1) The Waqif appoints the members (or determines selection criteria and dismissal conditions) and has authority to reconstitute the board periodically or when needed; (2) where the Waqif does NOT have authority to appoint members, they are appointed by a resolution of the board based on a recommendation by the nomination and remuneration committee; and (3) in the absence of the Waqif, the board of Nazirs must fill in any casual vacancy created in the board.
en.B: (1) The Waqif has zero authority over board appointments once the deed is signed; (2) when the Waqif lacks appointment power, the external auditor appoints board members; and (3) casual vacancies remain unfilled until a court dissolves the Waqf.
en.C: (1) Board members are elected exclusively by commercial bank lenders; (2) the nomination and remuneration committee has no role in board appointments; and (3) casual vacancies are filled by the Chief Financial Officer.
en.D: Board of Nazirs members serve for life with no mechanism for reconstitution or filling casual vacancies.
en.True answer: (1) The Waqif appoints the members (or determines selection criteria and dismissal conditions) and has authority to reconstitute the board periodically or when needed; (2) where the Waqif does NOT have authority to appoint members, they are appointed by a resolution of the board based on a recommendation by the nomination and remuneration committee; and (3) in the absence of the Waqif, the board of Nazirs must fill in any casual vacancy created in the board.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, Par. 17–20 (Par. 17: Waqif appoints members or determines eligibility criteria and dismissal conditions; Par. 18: where Waqif does not have authority to appoint, members are appointed by board resolution based on recommendation by the nomination and remuneration committee; Par. 20: Waqif has authority to reconstitute board periodically or when needed, and in the absence of the Waqif, the board of Nazirs must fill in casual vacancies).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13: Waqf Governance
en.Question: Under Paragraph 21(a)–(l) of the AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, which combination of experience, integrity, and clean-record criteria applies to candidates for the Board of Nazirs (unless the Waqf deed specifies otherwise)?
en.A: Candidates need only be major commercial borrowers of the Waqf, with no restrictions on prior bankruptcy or charity suspensions.
en.B: Candidates must possess Shari'ah and legal capacity, appropriate qualifications, diversified knowledge/skills, piety, justice, honesty, and integrity; be able to dedicate time and effort; possess reasonable management experience (preferably prior experience managing a business or charitable initiative in one of the areas the Waqf manages or invests in); NOT have filed a bankruptcy application or been convicted of debt default; NOT have been previously banned from working by official authorities or banned/suspended from any charity or establishment; and NOT have been convicted of any crime, subjected to disciplinary action for integrity issues, or convicted of providing incorrect/misleading information.
en.C: Candidates must hold a Ph.D. in conventional derivatives and are barred from having prior experience in charitable initiatives.
en.D: Prior disciplinary actions for ethical violations or providing misleading information are ignored if the candidate donates money to the Waqf.
en.True answer: Candidates must possess Shari'ah and legal capacity, appropriate qualifications, diversified knowledge/skills, piety, justice, honesty, and integrity; be able to dedicate time and effort; possess reasonable management experience (preferably prior experience managing a business or charitable initiative in one of the areas the Waqf manages or invests in); NOT have filed a bankruptcy application or been convicted of debt default; NOT have been previously banned from working by official authorities or banned/suspended from any charity or establishment; and NOT have been convicted of any crime, subjected to disciplinary action for integrity issues, or convicted of providing incorrect/misleading information.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, Par. 21(a)–(l) (Enumerates 12 selection criteria unless Waqf deed specifies otherwise: Shari'ah/legal capacity, qualifications, diversified skills, piety/justice/honesty/integrity, time/effort commitment, collective legal awareness, reasonable management experience [preferably managing a business or charitable initiative in an area the Waqf manages/invests in], no bankruptcy application or debt default conviction, no official work ban, no ban/suspension from any charity/establishment, no crime or professional/ethical disciplinary action for integrity issues, no conviction for providing incorrect/misleading information, and competence/due care).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13: Waqf Governance
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 26–28 of the AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, what voting threshold is required if the Board of Nazirs itself decides to terminate a board member for a serious breach of duties or misuse of Waqf funds (in the absence of a court or competent authority ruling), and when does termination take effect?
en.A: A simple majority (50% + 1) of members present, taking effect retroactively from the start of the financial year.
en.B: A unanimous 100% vote of all beneficiaries, taking effect 6 months later.
en.C: A decision of the board approved by a two-thirds (2/3) majority of the members; termination takes effect from the time the member is notified of the termination, and the board must take appropriate measures to stop the dismissed member from continuing to portray himself as a member.
en.D: A unilateral decision by the Chief Financial Officer without board voting or notification.
en.True answer: A decision of the board approved by a two-thirds (2/3) majority of the members; termination takes effect from the time the member is notified of the termination, and the board must take appropriate measures to stop the dismissed member from continuing to portray himself as a member.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, Par. 26(f) & Par. 27–28 (Par. 26(f): serious breach in discharging duties/responsibilities or misuse of Waqf funds, decided by a court of law or competent authority OR alternatively a decision of the board approved by a two-third majority of the members; Par. 27: 'The member shall be notified of the termination which shall be effective from the time of the notification'; Par. 28: 'The board shall take the appropriate measures to stop a dismissed member from continuing to portray himself as a member of the board').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13: Waqf Governance
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 29–31 (and Footnote 1) of the AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, when may a prior warning be bypassed before removing a Nazir, and what procedural right MUST always be afforded to the Nazir prior to suspension or removal?
en.A: A prior warning can never be bypassed even in cases of active embezzlement, and the Nazir has no right to be heard.
en.B: The Nazir may be removed instantly without any hearing or evaluation whenever investment returns decline by 1%.
en.C: Only an individual Nazir (and never a juristic person or state Nazir) is covered by these removal rules.
en.D: The Waqif or competent authority may give a written/verbal warning, which MAY BE AVOIDED if the breach is significant and immediate removal is necessary; however, the Nazir MUST be given the opportunity to be heard before suspension or removal (applying across all forms of Nazir: board of Nazirs, individual, state, or juristic person Nazir).
en.True answer: The Waqif or competent authority may give a written/verbal warning, which MAY BE AVOIDED if the breach is significant and immediate removal is necessary; however, the Nazir MUST be given the opportunity to be heard before suspension or removal (applying across all forms of Nazir: board of Nazirs, individual, state, or juristic person Nazir).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, Par. 29–31 & Footnote 1 (Footnote 1: 'Nazir' implies all forms—board of Nazirs, individual Nazir, state Nazir, or juristic person Nazir; Par. 30: 'The Waqif or the competent authority, as per law, may also choose to give the Nazir a written / verbal warning. However, a warning may be avoided if the breach is significant and immediate removal is necessary. The Nazir shall be given the opportunity to be heard before suspension or removal').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13: Waqf Governance
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 32 and 35–38 of the AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, what are the benchmark figures for (1) maximum term of a Board of Nazirs member, (2) recommended minimum board meetings per year, (3) ideal advance notice for meeting papers, (4) board meeting quorum, and (5) decisions by circulation?
en.A: (1) Maximum term of 5 years (unless otherwise prescribed by law); (2) preferably at least 3 meetings a year; (3) information provided ideally 2–3 weeks before the meeting date; (4) quorum requires more than half of the members attending in person or by uninterrupted visual communication (with full voting rights); and (5) decisions by circulation are limited strictly to emergencies.
en.B: (1) Maximum term of 10 years; (2) at least 12 meetings a year; (3) agenda sent 24 hours before; (4) 100% in-person quorum required; and (5) circular resolutions used for all routine matters.
en.C: (1) Indefinite lifetime term; (2) 1 meeting every two years; (3) visual communication attendees cannot vote; and (4) circular resolutions prohibited even in emergencies.
en.D: (1) Maximum term of 2 years; (2) 6 mandatory meetings per year; (3) 1 day advance notice; and (4) quorum of any 2 members.
en.True answer: (1) Maximum term of 5 years (unless otherwise prescribed by law); (2) preferably at least 3 meetings a year; (3) information provided ideally 2–3 weeks before the meeting date; (4) quorum requires more than half of the members attending in person or by uninterrupted visual communication (with full voting rights); and (5) decisions by circulation are limited strictly to emergencies.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, Par. 32 & Par. 35–38 (Par. 32: maximum term for a member of the board of Nazirs shall be five years, unless otherwise prescribed by law; Par. 35: preferably meet at least 3 times a year; Par. 36: information provided well in advance, ideally 2–3 weeks before the meeting date; Par. 37: attended by more than half of the members in person or via uninterrupted visual communication, with visual attendees entitled to vote identically; Par. 38: decisions by circulation limited to emergencies).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13: Waqf Governance
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 40–44 (including Footnote 2) of the AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, what is the preferred size of Board of Nazirs committees, what independence requirements apply to committee members and chairmen, and how is an 'independent member' defined?
en.A: Committees must have 9 to 15 members, all executive managers of the Waqf qualify as independent, and the Waqf CEO chairs every committee.
en.B: Committees should preferably have no less than 3 and no more than 5 members; the majority of committee members must be independent AND the chairman of each committee must also be an independent member—where an 'independent member' is defined as a member who (1) does not take part in the management function of the Waqf, (2) is not involved in any business relationship with the Waqf, and (3) does not have any interest in the benefits of the Waqf.
en.C: Committees have 2 members, and a beneficiary receiving monthly Waqf stipends qualifies as an independent committee chairman.
en.D: Independent members are barred from chairing Board committees.
en.True answer: Committees should preferably have no less than 3 and no more than 5 members; the majority of committee members must be independent AND the chairman of each committee must also be an independent member—where an 'independent member' is defined as a member who (1) does not take part in the management function of the Waqf, (2) is not involved in any business relationship with the Waqf, and (3) does not have any interest in the benefits of the Waqf.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, Par. 40, Par. 43 & Footnote 2 (Par. 40: preferably with no less than three and no more than five members; Par. 43: 'The majority of the committee members shall be independent and the chairman of each committee shall also be an independent member'; Footnote 2: 'An independent member is a member who does not take part in the management function of the Waqf, is not involved in any business relationship with the Waqf and does not have any interest in the benefits of the Waqf').

en.Theme: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13: Waqf Governance
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 60–65 of the AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, which international standards and governance practices are referenced for a Waqf's Complaints Policy and Information Security Policy, and what is recommended regarding a compliance officer?
en.A: Complaints and information security policies are unnecessary for Waqfs, and appointing a compliance officer is discouraged.
en.B: Complaints are governed by Basel III capital rules, and information security is governed by IFRS 9.
en.C: The Complaints Policy should comply with ISO 10002:2014 (or equivalent standards) and it is recommended to appoint a compliance officer EVEN IF not required by the relevant regulator to assure compliance and maintain stakeholder confidence (Par. 62); and the Information Security Policy should take into consideration the requirements of ISO 27001:2013 (or equivalent standards) (Par. 64–65).
en.D: A compliance officer may be appointed only if mandated by criminal court order, and electronic document archiving is prohibited.
en.True answer: The Complaints Policy should comply with ISO 10002:2014 (or equivalent standards) and it is recommended to appoint a compliance officer EVEN IF not required by the relevant regulator to assure compliance and maintain stakeholder confidence (Par. 62); and the Information Security Policy should take into consideration the requirements of ISO 27001:2013 (or equivalent standards) (Par. 64–65).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, Par. 61–65 (Par. 61: archive documents in both paper and electronic formats; Par. 62: Complaints policy compliant with ISO standard No. 10002:2014 [or equivalent], and recommended to appoint a compliance officer even if not required by the relevant regulator; Par. 64–65: Information security policy taking into consideration ISO standard No. 27001:2013 [or equivalent]).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13: Waqf Governance
en.Question: Under Part D (Paragraphs 70–78) of the AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, what governance structures are specified for (1) a Board of Nazirs, (2) a Juristic Person Nazir, and (3) a State Nazir?
en.A: (1) Board of Nazirs must have at least 15 members; (2) Juristic Person Nazir delegates responsibility to external auditors; and (3) State Nazir must always use direct ministerial supervision.
en.B: (1) Board of Nazirs excludes independent members; (2) Juristic Person Nazir cannot appoint dedicated management; and (3) State Nazir must create a separate board for every single Waqf without exception.
en.C: (1) Board of Nazirs has 2 members; (2) Juristic Person Nazir is prohibited under Shari'ah; and (3) State Nazir is exempt from all governance rules.
en.D: (1) A Board of Nazirs typically consists of 3 to 9 members with independent members and optional fair beneficiary representation (Par. 72); (2) when a juristic person (institution) is Nazir, its TCWG takes the responsibility of Nazir and may assign governance/management to its own management/selected personnel OR appoint dedicated (preferably independent) management (Par. 75–76); and (3) when the state is Nazir, rather than direct supervision, it is preferable for the state to form and supervise a supplementary board of Nazirs (with the same rights/responsibilities, and a single supplementary board with support staff may manage multiple state-governed Waqfs) (Par. 77–78).
en.True answer: (1) A Board of Nazirs typically consists of 3 to 9 members with independent members and optional fair beneficiary representation (Par. 72); (2) when a juristic person (institution) is Nazir, its TCWG takes the responsibility of Nazir and may assign governance/management to its own management/selected personnel OR appoint dedicated (preferably independent) management (Par. 75–76); and (3) when the state is Nazir, rather than direct supervision, it is preferable for the state to form and supervise a supplementary board of Nazirs (with the same rights/responsibilities, and a single supplementary board with support staff may manage multiple state-governed Waqfs) (Par. 77–78).
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, Par. 70–78 (Par. 72: Board of Nazirs typically 3 to 9 members with reasonable independent members and fair/transparent beneficiary representation; Par. 75–76: Juristic person Nazir's TCWG takes Nazir responsibility and may assign to own management/selected personnel or appoint dedicated [preferably independent] management; Par. 77–78: State Nazir preferably forms/supervises a supplementary board of Nazirs instead of direct supervision, and a single supplementary board with support staff may manage multiple Waqfs under state Nazir governance).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13: Waqf Governance
en.Question: Under Paragraphs 22–24 of the AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, how are the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Board of Nazirs selected, what are the Chairman's core governance functions, and when does the Deputy Chairman assume the Chairman's responsibilities?
en.A: Unless the Waqif chooses to nominate a chairman, the Board of Nazirs chooses a chairman (and deputy chairman) among themselves under a pre-approved election process; the Chairman agrees on meeting dates in advance, convenes meetings and supervises agenda preparation (while board members retain the right to request specific agenda items), chairs meetings, assigns tasks to suitable members, ensures timely decisions, encourages active participation, reviews board performance, and guides training/onboarding; and the Deputy Chairman assists the Chairman as directed and carries out the Chairman's responsibilities during his absence, temporary illness rendering him incapable, or termination of membership until an alternate is appointed.
en.B: The Chairman is always appointed by the external auditor, board members cannot request agenda items, and the Deputy Chairman permanently replaces the Chairman upon any single missed meeting.
en.C: The Chief Financial Officer chairs all Board of Nazirs meetings, and no Deputy Chairman position exists under the Guidance Note.
en.D: The Chairman has unilateral authority to override Waqf deed conditions without board voting.
en.True answer: Unless the Waqif chooses to nominate a chairman, the Board of Nazirs chooses a chairman (and deputy chairman) among themselves under a pre-approved election process; the Chairman agrees on meeting dates in advance, convenes meetings and supervises agenda preparation (while board members retain the right to request specific agenda items), chairs meetings, assigns tasks to suitable members, ensures timely decisions, encourages active participation, reviews board performance, and guides training/onboarding; and the Deputy Chairman assists the Chairman as directed and carries out the Chairman's responsibilities during his absence, temporary illness rendering him incapable, or termination of membership until an alternate is appointed.
en.main: Rationale: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13, Par. 22–24 (Par. 22: unless Waqif nominates chairman, board chooses chairman among themselves per pre-approved election process, also specifying deputy chairman election; Par. 23(a)–(j): 10 functions of chairman including agreeing meeting dates in advance, convening meetings/supervising agenda [members have right to request agenda items], chairing, task assignment, timely decisions, encouraging participation, reviewing performance, guiding training/onboarding; Par. 24(a)–(b): deputy chairman assists chairman as directed, carries out chairman's responsibilities in absence, temporary illness, or termination of chairman's membership until alternate is appointed, and assumes delegated special tasks).

en.Theme: AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13: Waqf Governance
en.Question: Comparing the four Board committees described in Part B (Paragraphs 45–52) of the AAOIFI Guidance Note for GS 13—Nomination & Remuneration, Investment & Risk Management, Executive, and Governance committees—which structural and functional statement is completely accurate?
en.A: The Executive Committee must consist entirely of external independent directors with zero senior managers, and the Governance Committee is chaired by the Waqf's Chief Executive Officer.
en.B: The Executive Committee (established for a period not exceeding the board's term) consists of at least 3 members where at least one-third (1/3) are board members and two-thirds (2/3) are senior management (developing the organizational structure and authority matrix for board approval); the Governance Committee consists of 3 or more members including at least one independent member who serves as chairman; the Nomination & Remuneration Committee proposes remuneration within the yield (Ghallah) percentage allocated by the Waqf deed/custom and prepares quantitative and qualitative KPIs for performance evaluation; and the Investment & Risk Management Committee manages assets for capital preservation while emphasizing yield (Ghallah) generation and approves selection/dismissal criteria and appraisals for external investment managers.
en.C: The Nomination & Remuneration Committee sets salaries freely without regard to Waqf deed limits on Ghallah, and the Investment Committee focuses exclusively on high-risk speculative trading.
en.D: All four committees must consist of at least 10 members, and senior management is barred from sitting on the Executive Committee.
en.True answer: The Executive Committee (established for a period not exceeding the board's term) consists of at least 3 members where at least one-third (1/3) are board members and two-thirds (2/3) are senior management (developing the organizational structure and authority matrix for board approval); the Governance Committee consists of 3 or more members including at least one independent member who serves as chairman; the Nomination & Remuneration Committee proposes remuneration within the yield (Ghallah) percentage allocated by the Waqf deed/custom and prepares quantitative and qualitative KPIs for performance evaluation; and the Investment & Risk Management Committee manages assets for capital preservation while emphasizing yield (Ghallah) generation and approves selection/dismissal criteria and appraisals for external investment managers.
